1Yuddha Kanda 8.1
ततो नील अम्बुद निभः प्रहस्तो नाम राक्षसः |अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिर् वाक्यम् शूरः सेना पतिस्तदा
tato nīla ambuda nibhaḥ prahasto nāma rākṣasaḥ |abravīt prāñjalir vākyam śūraḥ senā patistadā
A valiant demon by name Prahasta, the commander-in-chief, appearing like a dark
cloud, joined his palms in salutation and spoke these words.


Word by word
1. tataH= thereafter;shuuraH= a valiant;raakSasaH= demon;prahasto naama= named prahasta;senaapatiH= the
commander-in-chief;niila ambuda prakhyaH= appearing like a dark cloud;praaJNjaliH= joined his palms in salutation;abraviit= and spoke;tadaa= then;vaakyam= (the following) words.




2Yuddha Kanda 8.2
देव दानव गन्धर्वाः पिशाचपतगौरगाः |न त्वाम् धर्षयितुम् शक्ताः किम् पुनर् वानरा रणे
deva dānava gandharvāḥ piśācapatagauragāḥ |na tvām dharṣayitum śaktāḥ kim punar vānarā raṇe
"All gods, demons, gandharvas, devils, birds and serpents can be attacked by you in
battle. Why to talk about two human beings?"


Word by word
2. sarve= all;deva daanava gandharvaaH= gods;demons;
Gandharvas;pishraacha pata goragaaH= devils;birds and serpents;shakyaaH= can
be dharSayitum = attacked;raNe= in battle;kim punaH= why to talk about;maanavau= two human beings?




3Yuddha Kanda 8.3
सर्वे प्रमत्ता विश्वस्ता वन्चिताः स्म हनूमता |न हि मे जीवतो गच्चेज् जीवन् स वन गोचरः
sarve pramattā viśvastā vancitāḥ sma hanūmatā |na hi me jīvato gaccej jīvan sa vana gocaraḥ
"All of us, in good faith but with negligence, were cheated by Hanuma. That monkey
cannot go alive, while I am alive."


Word by word
3. sarve= all of us;vishvastaaH= in good faith;pramattaaH= but with negligence;vaNchitaasmi= were cheated;hanumataa= by Hanuma;saH= that;vanagocharaH= monkey;nagachhet hi= cannot
indeed go;jiivan= alive;me= (while) I;jiivitaH= an alive.




4Yuddha Kanda 8.4
सर्वाम् सागर पर्यन्ताम् सशैल वन काननाम् |करोमि अवानराम् भूमिम् आज्ञापयतु माम् भवान्
sarvām sāgara paryantām saśaila vana kānanām |karomi avānarām bhūmim ājñāpayatu mām bhavān
"I shall make the entire earth extending upto the ocean, along with mountains
forests and woods, bereft of monkeys. You command me."


Word by word
4. karomi= I shall make;sarvaam= the entire;bhuumim= earth;saagara paryantaam= extending upto the ocean;sashaila vana
kaananaam= along with mountains forests and woods;avaanaraam= bereft of monkeys;bhavaan= you;aaGYaapayatu= command;maam= me.




5Yuddha Kanda 8.5
रक्षाम् चैव विधास्यामि वानराद् रजनी चर |न आगमिष्यति ते दुह्खम् किंचिद् आत्म अपराधजम्
rakṣām caiva vidhāsyāmi vānarād rajanī cara |na āgamiṣyati te duhkham kiṃcid ātma aparādhajam
"Oh, Ravana! I shall arrange for your defence from that monkey. Not a little trouble
will come to you on account of your guilt (abduction of Seetha)."


Word by word
5. rajanii cara= Oh;Ravana;vidhaasyaami= I shall
arrange;rakSaam caiva= for defence also;vaanaraad= from the monkey;na
kimchit= not a little;duHkham= trouble;aagamishhyati= will come;te= to you;aatma aparaadhajam= on account of your guilt (abduction of
Seetha).




6Yuddha Kanda 8.6
अब्रवीत्तम् सुसम्क्रुद्धो दुर्मुखो नाम राक्षसः |इदम् न क्षमणीयम् हि सर्वेषाम् नः प्रधर्षणम्
abravīttam susamkruddho durmukho nāma rākṣasaḥ |idam na kṣamaṇīyam hi sarveṣām naḥ pradharṣaṇam
A demon by name Durmukha, being seriously enraged, spoke to him as follows: "This
humiliation meted out to us by that monkey is indeed not to be tolerated."


Word by word
6. raakSasaH= a demon;durmukho naama= by name Durmukha;susamkruddhaH= being seriously enraged;abraviit= spoke;tam= to him;idam= this;pradharSaNam= molestation;sarveSaam= to all;naH= of us;na kSamaNiiyam hi= is indeed not to be tolerated.




7Yuddha Kanda 8.7
अयम् परिभवो भूयः पुरस्य अन्तः पुरस्य च |श्रीमतो राक्षस इन्द्रस्य वानर इन्द्र प्रधर्षणम्
ayam paribhavo bhūyaḥ purasya antaḥ purasya ca |śrīmato rākṣasa indrasya vānara indra pradharṣaṇam
"This insult to the city of Lanka and the palaces together with attack by Sugreeva
on the glorious Ravana are still outrageous."


Word by word
7. ayam= this;paribhavaH= insult;purasya= to
Lanka City;antaH purasya ca= and the palaces;vaanarendra pradharSaNam= and
the attack by Sugreeva;the king of monkeys;shriimataH= of the glorious;raakshasendrasya= king of demons;bhuuyaH= is still (outrageous).




8Yuddha Kanda 8.8
अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते हत्वा एको निवर्तिष्यामि वानरान् |प्रविष्टान् सागरम् भीमम् अम्बरम् वा रसा तलम्
asmin muhūrte hatvā eko nivartiṣyāmi vānarān |praviṣṭān sāgaram bhīmam ambaram vā rasā talam
"Proceeding at this moment alone, I shall destroy those monkeys, whether they
entered the ocean or the subterranean region or the sky."


Word by word
8. gatvaa= proceeding;asmin;= at this;muhuurte= moment;ekaH= alone;nivartiSyaami= I shall destroy;vaanaraan= the monkeys;praviSTaan= who entered;saagaram= either into the ocean;bhiimam rasaa
talam= or into the terrific subterranean region under the earth;ambaram vaa= or
into the sky.




9Yuddha Kanda 8.9
ततो अब्रवीत् सुसम्क्रुद्धो वज्र दम्ष्ट्रो महाबलः |प्रगृह्य परिघम् घोरम् मांस शोणित रूपितम्
tato abravīt susamkruddho vajra damṣṭro mahābalaḥ |pragṛhya parigham ghoram māṃsa śoṇita rūpitam
Thereafter the very strong Vajradamshtra, beset with great anger, took hold of a
terrific iron club smeared with flesh and blood and spoke (as follows):


Word by word
9. tataH= thereafter;mahaabalaH= the very strong;vajra damSTraH= Vajradamshtra;susamkruddhaH= beset with great anger;pragR^ihya= took hold of;ghoram= a terrific;parigham= iron club;maamsa shoNita ruupitam= smeared with flesh and blood;abraviit= (and) spoke
(as follows).




10Yuddha Kanda 8.10
किम् नो हनुमता कार्यम् कृपणेन तपस्विना |रामे तिष्ठति दुर्धर्षे सुग्रीवे सह लक्ष्मणे
kim no hanumatā kāryam kṛpaṇena tapasvinā |rāme tiṣṭhati durdharṣe sugrīve saha lakṣmaṇe
"What work for us with that pitiable and miserable Hanuma, when Rama along with
Lakshmana and Sugreeva who are difficult to be conquered exist?"


Word by word
10. kim= what;kaaryam= work;naH= for us;hanumataa= with Hanuma;kR^ipaNena= the pitiable;tapasvinaa= and the
miserable;raame= when Rama;salakSmaNe= along with Lakshmana;sugriive
api= and Sugreeva;durdharSe= who are difficult to be conquered;tiSThati= exist?




11Yuddha Kanda 8.11
अद्य रामम् ससुग्रीवम् परिघेण सलक्ष्मणम् |आगमिष्यामि हत्वा एको विक्षोभ्य हरि वाहिनीम्
adya rāmam sasugrīvam parigheṇa salakṣmaṇam |āgamiṣyāmi hatvā eko vikṣobhya hari vāhinīm
"Now itself, with this iron club, killing Rama, Lakshmana and Sugreeva after
perturbing the army of monkeys, I shall come back."


Word by word
11. adya= Now;ekaH= alone;hatvaa= killing;parigheNa= by this iron club;raamam= Rama;salakSmaNam= along with
Lakshmana;sasugriivam= together with Sugreeva;vikSobhya= and after
perturbing;harivaahiniim= the army of monkeys;aagamiSyaami= I shall come
back.




12Yuddha Kanda 8.12
इदम् ममापरम् वाक्यम् शृणु राजन्यदीच्चसि |उपायकुशलो ह्येव जयेच्चत्रुनतन्द्रितः
idam mamāparam vākyam śṛṇu rājanyadīccasi |upāyakuśalo hyeva jayeccatrunatandritaḥ
"Oh, king! If you are willing, hear my words further. One who is skilled din a
stratagem alone will be without lassitude and can indeed defeat the enemies."


Word by word
12. raajan= Oh;king;yadi icchasi= if you are willing;shR^iNu= hear;aparam= moreover;mama= my;idam vaakyam=
these words;upaayakushalaH eva= one who is skilled in stratagem only;atandritaH= will be without lassitude;jayet hi= (and) can indeed defeat;shatruun= enemies.




13Yuddha Kanda 8.13
कामरूपधराः शूराः सुभीमा भीमदर्शनाः |राक्षसा वा सहस्राणि राक्षसाधिप निश्चिताः
kāmarūpadharāḥ śūrāḥ subhīmā bhīmadarśanāḥ |rākṣasā vā sahasrāṇi rākṣasādhipa niścitāḥ
O, king of demons! Thousands of demons able to change their form at will courageaous
appalling terrifying to look at and firm (in their purpose) can wear human body approach Rama
without embarrassment and all speak to Rama (as follows).


Word by word
13-14. raakshasaadhipa= O;king of demons! sahasraaNi=
thousands of;raakSasaaH= demons;kaamaruupadharaaH= able to change their form
at will;shuuraaH= courageous;subhiimaaH= appalling;bhiimadarshanaaH= terrifying to look at;nishchitaaH= and firm (in their purpose);bibhrataH=
can wear;maanuSam= human;vapuH= body;upasangamya= approach;kaakutsam= Rama;asambhramaaH= without embarrassment;sarve= and all;bruvantu= speak;raghusattamam= to Rama (as follows).




14Yuddha Kanda 8.14
काकुत्थ्समुपसम्गम्य बिभ्रतो मानुषम् वपुः |सर्वे ह्यसम्भ्रमा भूत्वा ब्रुवन्तु रघुसत्तमम्
kākutthsamupasamgamya bibhrato mānuṣam vapuḥ |sarve hyasambhramā bhūtvā bruvantu raghusattamam
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


15Yuddha Kanda 8.15
प्रेषिता भरतेनैव भ्रात्रा तव यवीयसा |स हि सेनाम् समुत्थाप्य क्षिप्रमेवोपयास्यति
preṣitā bharatenaiva bhrātrā tava yavīyasā |sa hi senām samutthāpya kṣipramevopayāsyati
"We have been despatched by Bharata, your younger brother. He is summoning his
forces and will surely come here soon."


Word by word
15. preSimtaa= we have been sent;bharatenaiva= by
Bharata;tava= your;yaviiyasaa= younger;bhraatraa= brother;saH= he;samutthaapya= summoning;senaam= his forces;kshiprameva= will surely soon;upayaasyati= come here.




16Yuddha Kanda 8.16
ततो वयमितस्तुर्णम् शूलशक्तिगदाधराः |चापबाणासिहस्तश्च त्वरितास्तत्र यामहे
tato vayamitasturṇam śūlaśaktigadādharāḥ |cāpabāṇāsihastaśca tvaritāstatra yāmahe
"Carrying spikes, javelins and maces together with arrows and swords in hand, we
will quickly go there from here soon."


Word by word
16. tataH= thereafter;vayam= we;turNam=
quickly;shuula shaktigadaadharaaH= carrying spikes;javelins and maces;caapa
baaNaasihastaashca= with arrows and swords in hand;yaamahe= will go;tatra= there;itaH= from here;tvaritaaH= soon."




17Yuddha Kanda 8.17
आकाशे गणशः स्थित्वा हत्वा ताम् हरिवाहिनीम् |अश्मशस्त्रमहावृष्ट्वा प्रापयाम् यमक्षयम्
ākāśe gaṇaśaḥ sthitvā hatvā tām harivāhinīm |aśmaśastramahāvṛṣṭvā prāpayām yamakṣayam
"Standing as groups in the sky and beating that army of monkeys with a mighty hail
of stones and missiles, we should send them to the world of Death."


Word by word
17. sthitvaa= standing;gaNashaH= as groups;aakaashe= in the sky;hatvaa= beating;taam= that;harivaahiniim= army of monkeys;ashmashastramahaavR^iSTvaa= with a mighty hail
of stones and missiles;praapayaam= we should send 9them) yamakshayam = to the world of
Death.




18Yuddha Kanda 8.18
एवम् चेदुपसर्पेतामनयम् रामलक्ष्मणौ |अवश्यमपनीतेन जहतामेव जीवितम्
evam cedupasarpetāmanayam rāmalakṣmaṇau |avaśyamapanītena jahatāmeva jīvitam
"If Rama and Lakshmana thus approach softly into our trap they will surely abandon
their lives as they are taken away by the trap."


Word by word
18. raamalakshmaNau= (If) Rama and Lakshmana;upasarpetaam
yadi= approach softly into our trap;evam= thus;jahataameva= they will
just abandon;jiivitam= the life;avashyameva= surely;apaniitena= as
they are taken away (by the trap)




19Yuddha Kanda 8.19
कौम्भकर्णिस् ततो वीरो निकुम्भो नाम वीर्यवान् |अब्रवीत् परम कुर्द्धो रावणम् लोक रावणम्
kaumbhakarṇis tato vīro nikumbho nāma vīryavān |abravīt parama kurddho rāvaṇam loka rāvaṇam
Thereafter Kumbhakarna's son, by name Nikumbha, strong and powerful, became very
angry and spoke (as follows) to Ravana, who made people cry.


Word by word
19. tataH= thereafter;kumbhakarNiH= Kumbhakarna's sons;nikumbho naama= by name Nikumbha;viiraH= strong;viiryavaan= and
powerful;paramakruddhaH= became very angry;abraviit= and spoke;raavaNam= to Ravana;loka raavaNam= who made people cry.




20Yuddha Kanda 8.20
सर्वे भवन्तस् तिष्ठन्तु महाराजेन सम्गताः |अहम् एको हनिष्यामि राघवम् सह लक्ष्मणम्सुग्रीवम् सहनूमन्तम् सर्वांश्चैवात्र वानरान्
sarve bhavantas tiṣṭhantu mahārājena samgatāḥ |aham eko haniṣyāmi rāghavam saha lakṣmaṇamsugrīvam sahanūmantam sarvāṃścaivātra vānarān
All of you stay along with the king. I alone will kill there, Rama along with
Lakshman, Sugreeva along with Hanuma and all the monkeys also.


Word by word
20-21b. sarve= all;bhavantaH= of you;tiSThantu= stay;samgataaH= along with;mahaaraajena= the king;aham= I;ekaH= alone;haniSyaami= will kill;atra= there;raaghavam=
Rama;sahalakSmaNam= along with Lakshman;sugriivam= Sugreeva;shanuumantam= along with Hanuman;sarvaan= all;vaanaraan shcaiva=
the monkeys too."




21Yuddha Kanda 8.21
ततो वज्रहनुर्नाम राक्षसः पर्वतोपमःक्रुद्धः परिलिहन् वक्त्रम् जिह्वया वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
tato vajrahanurnāma rākṣasaḥ parvatopamaḥkruddhaḥ parilihan vaktram jihvayā vākyam abravīt
Then, a demon by name Vajrahanu who was resembling a mountain, becoming enraged and
licking the corners of his mouth with his tongue, spoke as follows:


Word by word
21b-22a. tataH= then;raakshasaH= a demon;vajrahanurnaama= by name Vajrahanu;parvatopamaana= who was resembling a
mountain;kruddhaH= becoming enraged;parilihan= licking;sR^ikkaam=
the corners of his mouth;jihvayaa= with his tongue;abraviit= spoke;vaakyam= those words.




22Yuddha Kanda 8.22
स्वैरम् कुर्वन्तु कार्याणि भवन्तो विगत ज्वराः
svairam kurvantu kāryāṇi bhavanto vigata jvarāḥ
"You do your occupations freely redeemed of mental pain, play comfortably and drink
spirituous liquor without any worry. I alone will devour the entire army of monkeys."


Word by word
22b-23. bhavantaH= you;kurvantu= do;karmaaNi=
(your) occupations;svairam= freely;vigata jvaraaH= redeemed of mental pain;kriiDantu= play;svasthaaH= comfortably;pibantu= (and) drink;vaaruNiim madhu= spirituous liquor;nishcintaaH= without worry;aham=
I;ekaH= alone;bhakSayiSyaami= will devour;sarvaam= the entire;harivaahiniim= army of monkeys.




23Yuddha Kanda 8.23
एको अहम् भक्षयिष्यामि तान् सर्वान् हरि यूथपान् |स्वस्थाः क्रीडन्तु निश्चिन्ताः पिबन्तु मधु वारुणीम्
eko aham bhakṣayiṣyāmi tān sarvān hari yūthapān |svasthāḥ krīḍantu niścintāḥ pibantu madhu vāruṇīm
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


24Yuddha Kanda 8.24
अहम् एको हनिष्यामि सुग्रीवम् सह लक्ष्मणम् |स अन्गदम् च हनूमन्तम् रामम् च रण कुन्जरम्
aham eko haniṣyāmi sugrīvam saha lakṣmaṇam |sa angadam ca hanūmantam rāmam ca raṇa kunjaram
At this time I alone will kill Sugreeva along with Lakshmana Hanuma along with
Angada and all monkeys.


Word by word
24. atra= at this time;aham= I;ekaH= alone;haniSyaami= will kill;sugriivam= Sugreeva;saha lakSmaNam= along
with Lakshmana;hanuumantam= Hanuma;sa angadam= along with Angada;sarvaan= (and) all;vaanara amsehca= monkeys."



    
  
  All the demons of King Ravana present there namely Prahasta, Durmukha, Vajradamshtra, Nikumbha and Vajrahanu, eulogising their strengths, assure the king that they can individually kill Rama and his army within no time.

Home/Yuddha Kanda/Sarga 6

  Yuddha Kanda · Sarga 6
  Ravana recalls the over-powering of Lanka and discovering of Seetha…
  Ravana recalls the over-powering of Lanka and discovering of Seetha by Hanuman. He calls a meeting of his ministers and invites suggestions from them in view of the latest situation of a probable attack of Rama and his army on the City of Lanka.

1Yuddha Kanda 6.1
लंकायाम् तु कृतम् कर्म घोरम् दृष्ट्वा भव आवहम् |राक्षस इन्द्रो हनुमता शक्रेण इव महात्मनाअब्रवीद् राक्षसान् सर्वान् ह्रिया किंचिद् अवान् मुखः
laṃkāyām tu kṛtam karma ghoram dṛṣṭvā bhava āvaham |rākṣasa indro hanumatā śakreṇa iva mahātmanāabravīd rākṣasān sarvān hriyā kiṃcid avān mukhaḥ
Having seen the fearful and the terrible act in Lanka done by Hanuma, like Devendra
the powerful King of celestials, Ravana with his face descended a little with shame, spoke to the
demons as follows:


Word by word
1. dR^iSTvaa= having seen;bhayaavaham= the fearful;ghoram= and the terrible;karma= act;kR^itam= done;hanumataa= by Hanuman;shakreNa iva= as Devendra (King of celestials);hamaatmanaa= the powerful;laN^kaayaam= in Lanka;raakshasendraH=
Ravana;avaan mukhaH= had his face down;kimchit= a little;hriyaa=
and spoke;sarvaan= to all;raakshhasaan= the demons (as follows):




2Yuddha Kanda 6.2
धर्षिता च प्रविष्टा च लंका दुष्प्रसहा पुरीतेन वानर मात्रेण दृष्टा सीता च जानकी
dharṣitā ca praviṣṭā ca laṃkā duṣprasahā purītena vānara mātreṇa dṛṣṭā sītā ca jānakī
"By him, who was only a monkey, the irresistible City of Lanka was entered into and
was over-powered. Seetha the daughter of Janaka was also discovered by him.


Word by word
2. tena= by him;vaanara maatreNa= who was only a monkey;dushhpraasahaa= the irresistible;laNkapurii= City of lanka;pravishhTaacha= was entered into;dharshhitaa cha= and was over-powered;siitaa= Seetha;jaanakii= the daughter of Janka;dR^ishhTaam cha= was
also seen (by him).




3Yuddha Kanda 6.3
प्रसादो धर्षितः चैत्यः प्रवरा राक्षसा हताःआविला च पुरी लंका सर्वा हनुमता कृता
prasādo dharṣitaḥ caityaḥ pravarā rākṣasā hatāḥāvilā ca purī laṃkā sarvā hanumatā kṛtā
The thousand-pillared building used as a sanctuary was assaulted by Hanuma. Our most
excellent demons were killed. The entire City of Lanka was made turbid.


Word by word
3. chaityaH praasaadaH= the thousand pillared building used as a
sanctuary;dharshhitaH= was assaulted;hanumataa= by Hanuma;pravaraaH= the most excellent;raakshhaasaaH= demons;hataaH= were killed;sarvaa= the entire;laNkaa purii= City of Lanka;kR^itaa= was made;aavilaa= turbid.




4Yuddha Kanda 6.4
किम् करिष्यामि भद्रम् वः किम् वा युक्तम् अनन्तरम्उच्यताम् नः समर्थम् यत् कृतम् च सुकृतम् भवेत्
kim kariṣyāmi bhadram vaḥ kim vā yuktam anantaramucyatām naḥ samartham yat kṛtam ca sukṛtam bhavet
May prosperity befall on you! What shall I do? What appropriate thing is to be done
next? Please speak that which is well-answering and that, if attempted becomes well-done.


Word by word
4. bhadram= prosperity;vaH= to you! Kim = what;karishhyaami= shall I do? Kim vaa = what thing;yuktam= appropriate thing;anantaram= (is to be done) afterwards? Uchyataam = let it be spoken;yat= that
which is samantham = well-answering;bhavet= and which becomes;sukrutam=
well-done.




5Yuddha Kanda 6.5
मन्त्र मूलम् हि विजयम् प्राहुर् आर्या मनस्विनःतस्माद् वै रोचये मन्त्रम् रामम् प्रति महाबलाः
mantra mūlam hi vijayam prāhur āryā manasvinaḥtasmād vai rocaye mantram rāmam prati mahābalāḥ
"Oh, people of great strength! Wise-men say that victory is dependent on good
forethought. Verily for that reason, I desire a deliberation about Rama."


Word by word
5. mahaabalaaH= Oh;people of great strength! manasvinaH=
wise-men;pravadanti= say;vijayam= that victory;mantramuulam= is
dependent on good forethought;tasmaat vai= just for that reason;rochaye= I
desire;mantram= a deliberation;raamamprati= about Rama.




6Yuddha Kanda 6.6
त्रिविधाः पुरुषा लोके उत्तम अधम मध्यमाःतेषाम् तु समवेतानाम् गुण दोषम् वदामि अहम्
trividhāḥ puruṣā loke uttama adhama madhyamāḥteṣām tu samavetānām guṇa doṣam vadāmi aham
"There are three types of men in the world, namely the foremost the middle most and
the lowest. I am telling their inherent merits and defects."


Word by word
6. triividhaaH= there are three types;purushhaaH= of men;loke= in the world;uttamaadhama madhyamaaH= namely;the foremost;the middle
most and the lowest;aham= I;vadaami= am telling;teshhaam= their;samavetaanaam= inherent;guNadoshhaa= merits and defects.




7Yuddha Kanda 6.7
मन्त्रिभिर् हित सम्युक्तैः समर्थैर् मन्त्र निर्णये
mantribhir hita samyuktaiḥ samarthair mantra nirṇaye
"The wise call him as the foremost among men, who carries through the beginning of
any undertaking after consulting those who are wedded with welfare of others, or with ministers who
are efficient in conferring decisions or with friends having common interests or additionally with
relatives or who try to get a favour from Providence too."


Word by word
7-8. yaH= he who;pravartayet= carries through;karmaarmabhaan= beginning of undertaking;mantrayitvaa= after consulting;sahitaH= collectively with;hitasmyuktaiH= or with ministers;samarthaiH= efficient;mantra nirNaye= in advising decisions;mitrairvaapi= or with friends;samanaarthaiH= having common;baandhavairaapi= or with relatives;adhikaaH= additionally;kurute=
or who does;yatnam= endeavour;daivecha= in the matter of providence too;tam= him;aahuH= (the wise) call;purushhottamam= as the foremost
among men.




8Yuddha Kanda 6.8
मित्रैर् वा अपि समान अर्थैर् बान्धवैर् अपि वा हितैः |सहितो मन्त्रयित्वा यः कर्म आरम्भान् प्रवर्तयेत्दैवे च कुरुते यत्नम् तम् आहुः पुरुष उत्तमम्
mitrair vā api samāna arthair bāndhavair api vā hitaiḥ |sahito mantrayitvā yaḥ karma ārambhān pravartayetdaive ca kurute yatnam tam āhuḥ puruṣa uttamam
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


9Yuddha Kanda 6.9
एको अर्थम् विम्ऱ्शेद् एको धर्मे प्रकुरुते मनःएकः कार्याणि कुरुते तम् आहुर् मध्यमम् नरम्
eko artham vimRśed eko dharme prakurute manaḥekaḥ kāryāṇi kurute tam āhur madhyamam naram
"The wise men call that man as mediocre, who deliberates about an activity
solitarily, applies his mind on law and justice all by himself and performs works singly."


Word by word
9. vimR^ishet= (He who) deliberates;artham= about an
activity;ekaH= solitarily;prakurute= applies;manaH= his mind;dharme= on law and justice;ekaH= all by himself;kurute= performs;kaaryaaNi= the workds;eakH= singly;aahuH= they call;tam
naram= that man;madhyamam= as mediocre.




10Yuddha Kanda 6.10
गुण दोषाव् अनिश्चित्य त्यक्त्वा दैव व्यपाश्रयम्करिष्यामि इति यः कार्यम् उपेक्षेत् स नर अधमः
guṇa doṣāv aniścitya tyaktvā daiva vyapāśrayamkariṣyāmi iti yaḥ kāryam upekṣet sa nara adhamaḥ
"He who does not determine the merits and demerits of an act clearly, having
recourse to Providence and neglects his duty by simply telling �I shall do it', he is the lowest
among men."


Word by word
10. yaH= He who;nanishchitya= does not determine;guNadoshhaa= the merits and demerits;vyaktma= clearly;daivavyapaashreyaH= having recourse to providence;upekshhet= neglects;kaaryam= his duty;karishhyaami iti= telling simply �I shall do';saH= he;naraadhamaH= is the lowest among men.




11Yuddha Kanda 6.11
यथा इमे पुरुषा नित्यम् उत्तम अधम मध्यमाःएवम् मन्त्रो अपि विज्ञेय उत्तम अधम मध्यमः
yathā ime puruṣā nityam uttama adhama madhyamāḥevam mantro api vijñeya uttama adhama madhyamaḥ
"In which manner these men are categorized always as good, bad or mediocre, so also
the resolution in thought is classified as good bad or mediocre."


Word by word
11. yathaa= how;ime= those;purushhaaH= men;nityam= are always;uttamaadhama madhyaaH= either good;bad or mediocre;mantro.api= even the resolution in thought is;evam= thus;viJNeyaH=
known;uttama adhama madhyamaH= as good;bad or mediocre."




12Yuddha Kanda 6.12
ऐकमत्यम् उपागम्य शास्त्र दृष्टेन चक्षुषामन्त्रिणो यत्र निरस्तास् तम् आहुर् मन्त्रम् उत्तमम्
aikamatyam upāgamya śāstra dṛṣṭena cakṣuṣāmantriṇo yatra nirastās tam āhur mantram uttamam
"The wise say that resolution of thought is excellent, in which the thinkers, on a
view perceived by scriptures, obtain consensus and are satisfied with it."


Word by word
12. mantraiNaH= the thinkers;chakshhushhaa= on a view;shaastradR^iSTena= perceived by scriptures;upaagamya= obtain;aikamatyam= consensus;nirataaH= and are satisfied;tam= that;mantram= resolution of thought;aahuH= (the wise) say;uttamam= as
the excellent one.




13Yuddha Kanda 6.13
बह्व्यो अपि मतयो गत्वा मन्त्रिणो हि अर्थ निर्णयेपुनर् यत्र एकताम् प्राप्तः स मन्त्रो मध्यमः स्मृतः
bahvyo api matayo gatvā mantriṇo hi artha nirṇayepunar yatra ekatām prāptaḥ sa mantro madhyamaḥ smṛtaḥ
"Only after deliberating several kinds of opinions, that decision of a matter
obtained finally by a consensus of the counselors, is called mediocre."


Word by word
13. gatvaapi= even after obtaining;bahviiH= several
kinds;matiH= of opinions;yatra= where;arthanirNayaH= the decision
of a matter;mantriNaam= by the counselors;punaH= once more;praaptaH= gets;ekataam= to a consensus;saH= that;mantraH= decision;smR^itaH= is called;madhmaH= mediocre.




14Yuddha Kanda 6.14
अन्योन्य मतिम् आस्थाय यत्र सम्प्रतिभाष्यतेन च ऐकमत्ये श्रेयो अस्ति मन्त्रः सो अधम उच्यते
anyonya matim āsthāya yatra sampratibhāṣyatena ca aikamatye śreyo asti mantraḥ so adhama ucyate
"That resolution is said to be worst in which several arguments are made, employing
one or the other divergent opinions and in which there is no advantage even after a consensus."


Word by word
14. saH= that;mantraH= resolution;uchyate= is
said to be;adhamaH= worst;yatra= in which;sampratibhaashhyate=
arguments are made;aasthaaya= emplying;anyouya matim= one or the other
divergent opinions;naasti= (in which) there is no;shriyaH= advantage;aikamatye= even after a consensus.




15Yuddha Kanda 6.15
तस्मात् सुमन्त्रितम् साधु भवन्तो मन्त्रि सत्तमाःकार्यम् सम्प्रतिपद्यन्ताम् एतत् कृत्यतमम् मम
tasmāt sumantritam sādhu bhavanto mantri sattamāḥkāryam sampratipadyantām etat kṛtyatamam mama
"For that reason, you, having excellent intellect, arrive at a well-thought out
rightful action. To me, this is earnestly to be done."


Word by word
15. tasmaat= for that reason;bhavantaH= you;matisattamaaH= having excellent intellect;sampritipadyantaam= arrive at;sumantritam= a well-thought out;saadhu= rightful;kaaryam= action;etat= this;mama= to me;matam= is earnestly;kR^ityam= to
be done."




16Yuddha Kanda 6.16
वानराणाम् हि वीराणाम् सहस्रैः परिवारितःरामो अभ्येति पुरीम् लंकाम् अस्माकम् उपरोधकः
vānarāṇām hi vīrāṇām sahasraiḥ parivāritaḥrāmo abhyeti purīm laṃkām asmākam uparodhakaḥ
"Rama surrounded by thousands of courageous monkeys, is coming to the City of Lanka,
for the purpose of besieging us."


Word by word
16. raamaH= Rama;parivaaritah= surrounded by;sahasraiH= thousands of;dhiraaNaam= brave;vaanaraaNaam= monkeys;abhyeti= is coming;laN^kaam puriim= to the City of Lanka;uparodhakaH= for besieging;asmaakam= us.




17Yuddha Kanda 6.17
तरिष्यति च सुव्यक्तम् राघवः सागरम् सुखम्तरसा युक्त रूपेण सानुजः सबल अनुगः
tariṣyati ca suvyaktam rāghavaḥ sāgaram sukhamtarasā yukta rūpeṇa sānujaḥ sabala anugaḥ
"Rama, by his be-fitting strength, can certainly cross the ocean easily, with his
brother along with his army and his companions."


Word by word
17. raagahavaH= Rama;yukta ruupeNa= by his befitting;tarasaa= strength;suvyaktam= can certainly;tarishhyati cha= cross;saagaram= the ocean;sukham= easily;saamjaH= with his brother;sabalaamgaH= along with his army and companions.




18Yuddha Kanda 6.18
समुद्रमुच्छोषयति वीर्येणान्यत्करोति वा
samudramucchoṣayati vīryeṇānyatkaroti vā
"He may even get the ocean dried up. He may do any other thing by his valour. The
aforesaid act of enmity with monkeys having commenced in this way, advise me everything that is
good for the city and my army."


Word by word
18-19. samudram uchchhoshhayati= (He may) get the ocean dried up;karoti= (He may) do;anyadvaa= any other thing;viiryeNa= by his
valour;tasmin= that;kaarye= act;viruddhe= of enemity;vaanaraiH saha= with monkeys;evam vidhe= (having commenced) in this way;sammantryataam= advise me;sarvam= everything;hitam= that is good;pure= for the city;mama sainye= and for my army.




19Yuddha Kanda 6.19
तस्मिन्न् एवम् गते कार्ये विरुद्धे वानरैः सह |हितम् पुरे च सैन्ये च सर्वम् सम्मन्त्र्यताम् मम
tasminn evam gate kārye viruddhe vānaraiḥ saha |hitam pure ca sainye ca sarvam sammantryatām mama
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.

    
  
  Ravana recalls the over-powering of Lanka and discovering of Seetha by Hanuman. He calls a meeting of his ministers and invites suggestions from them in view of the latest situation of a probable attack of Rama and his army on the City of Lanka.

title: After hearing the report of Hanuma, Rama fixes an auspicious hour…
text:
Home/Yuddha Kanda/Sarga 4

  Yuddha Kanda · Sarga 4
  After hearing the report of Hanuma, Rama fixes an auspicious hour…
  After hearing the report of Hanuma, Rama fixes an auspicious hour for the departure of his forces to Lanka and perceives good omens. The Army reaches the shores of the sea.
  124 shlokas≈ 68 minDevanagari completeEnglish 86%


  
    Shlokas (124)
  
  Sarga summary
  
    Reading notes
  


  
    
      Jump to a shloka123456789101112131415161718192021222324252627282930313233343536373839404142434445464748495051525354555657585960616263646566676869707172737475767778798081828384858687888990919293949596979899100101102103104105106107108109110111112113114115116117118119120121122123124
      
1Yuddha Kanda 4.1
श्रुत्वा हनूमतो वाक्यम् यथावद् अनुपूर्वशः |ततो अब्रवीन् महातेजा रामः सत्य पराक्रमः
śrutvā hanūmato vākyam yathāvad anupūrvaśaḥ |tato abravīn mahātejā rāmaḥ satya parākramaḥ
Rama, a very bright man and a true warrior, having duly heard the words of Hanuman from
the beginning, thereafter spoke as follows:


Word by word
1. raamaH= Rama;mhaatejaaH= a very bright man;satyaparaakramaH= a true warrior;yathaavat= duly;shrutvaa= having heard;vaakyam= the 
words;hanumataH= of Hanuman;anupuurashaH= from the beginning;tataH= 
thereafter;abraviit= spoke (as follows).




2Yuddha Kanda 4.2
याम् निवेदयसे लंकाम् पुरीम् भीमस्य रक्षसः |क्षिप्रम् एनाम् वधिष्यामि सत्यम् एतद् ब्रवीमि ते
yām nivedayase laṃkām purīm bhīmasya rakṣasaḥ |kṣipram enām vadhiṣyāmi satyam etad bravīmi te
"I shall destroy quickly Lanka, the city of that terrible ogre (Ravana), of which you
just informed I am really telling this."


Word by word
2. mathisya= I shall destroy;kshhipram= quickly;puriim= the city;laN^kaam= of Lanka;bhiimasya= of the terrible;rakshasaH= 
ogre;yaam= of which;nivedayase= you inform;braviimi= I am telling;te= you;etat= this;satyam= really.




3Yuddha Kanda 4.3
अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते सुग्रीव प्रयाणम् अभिरोचये |युक्तो मुहूर्तो विजयः प्राप्तो मध्यम् दिवा करः
asmin muhūrte sugrīva prayāṇam abhirocaye |yukto muhūrto vijayaḥ prāpto madhyam divā karaḥ
"Be pleased to approve our march at this moment, a suitable moment for success. The sun
reached the mid-day.


Word by word
3. Sugreeva= Oh;Sugreeva! Abhirochaya= be pleased;prayaaNam= for our march;asmin= at this;muhuurte= moment;yukto= a suitable;muhuurtaH= moment;vijayaH= for success;divaakaraH= the sun;praaptaH= reached;madhyam= the mid-day.




4Yuddha Kanda 4.4
सीताम् गृत्वा तु तद्यातु क्वासौ यास्यति जीवितः |सीता श्रुत्वाभियानम् मे आशामेष्यति जीवितेजीवितान्तेऽ मृतम् स्पृष्ट्वा पीत्वा विषमिवातुरः
sītām gṛtvā tu tadyātu kvāsau yāsyati jīvitaḥ |sītā śrutvābhiyānam me āśāmeṣyati jīvitejīvitānte.a mṛtam spṛṣṭvā pītvā viṣamivāturaḥ
"Let that ogre go (to his abode) after kidnapping Seetha. Where will he go alive? Hearing
of my march to Lanka, Seetha will get back her hope in life, like a sick man having drunk poison touches
ambrosia at the end of his life."


Word by word
4. tat= let that ogre;yaatu= go (to his abode);hR^itam= after kidnapping;siitaam= Seetha;kva= where;asau yaasyati= will he 
go;jiivitaH= alive? shrutvaa = hearing;me= of my;abhiyaanam= march;siitaa= Seetha;yaasyati= will get back;aashaam= her hope;aashaam= her hope;jiivite= in life;spR^isTvaa iva= like touching;amR^itam= 
ambrosia;aaturaH= by a sick man;piitvaa= having drunk;vishham= poison;jiivitaante= at the end of his life."




5Yuddha Kanda 4.5
उत्तरा फल्गुनी हि अद्य श्वस् तु हस्तेन योक्ष्यतेअभिप्रयाम सुग्रीव सर्व अनीक समावृताः
uttarā phalgunī hi adya śvas tu hastena yokṣyateabhiprayāma sugrīva sarva anīka samāvṛtāḥ
"This northern planet of Phalguni will be in conjunction with the Hasta star tomorrow.
Hence, let us depart today itself with all the troops accompanying us, Oh, Sugreeva!"


Word by word
5. adya= this;uttaraa phalguniihi= northern planet of Phalguni;yokshhyate= will be in conjunction;hastena= with the Hasta star;shvastu= tomorrow;abhiprayaama= let us depart;sarvaaniikasamaavR^itaH= with all the troops 
accompanying us;sugriiva= Oh;Sugreeva!




6Yuddha Kanda 4.6
निमित्तानि च धन्यानि यानि प्रादुर् भवन्ति मेनिहत्य रावणम् सीताम् आनयिष्यामि जानकीम्
nimittāni ca dhanyāni yāni prādur bhavanti menihatya rāvaṇam sītām ānayiṣyāmi jānakīm
"By seeing the omens which are becoming visible, I deduce that I shall bring back Seetha
the daughter of Janaka, by killing Ravana."


Word by word
6. pashyaami= by seeing;nimittaani= the omens;yaani= which;praadurbhavanti= are becoming visible ;aanayishhyaami= I shall bring;siitaam= Seetha;jaanakiim= the daughter of Janaka;nihatya= by killing;raavaNam= Ravana.




7Yuddha Kanda 4.7
उपरिष्टाद्द् हि नयनम् स्फुरमाणम् इदम् ममविजयम् समनुप्राप्तम् शंसति इव मनो रथम्
upariṣṭādd hi nayanam sphuramāṇam idam mamavijayam samanuprāptam śaṃsati iva mano ratham
"My eye which is twitching on the upper lid, is proclaiming as it were, my desire of
victory coming nearer."


Word by word
7. idam= this;mama= my;nayanam= eye;sphuramaaNam= which is twitching;uparishhTaat= is proclaiming as it were;manoratham= my desire;vijayam= of victory;samanupraaptam= coming nearer."




8Yuddha Kanda 4.8
ततो वाबरराहेब कज्श्मणेन सुपूजितःउवाच रामो धर्मात्मा पुनरप्यर्थकोविदः
tato vābararāheba kajśmaṇena supūjitaḥuvāca rāmo dharmātmā punarapyarthakovidaḥ
Then Rama the virtuous man versed in moral law, who was well-adored by Sugreeva the king
of monkeys and Lakshmana, again spoke as follows:-


Word by word
8. tataH= Then;raamaH= Rama;dharmaatmaa= the virtuous 
man;arthakovidaH= versed in moral law;supuujitaaH= well adored;vaanararaajena= by Sugreeva the king of monkeys;lakshmaNena= and Lakshmana;punarapi= again;uvaacha= spoke (as follows).




9Yuddha Kanda 4.9
अग्रे यातु बलस्य अस्य नीलो मार्गम् अवेक्षितुम्वृतः शत सहस्रेण वानराणाम् तरस्विनाम्
agre yātu balasya asya nīlo mārgam avekṣitumvṛtaḥ śata sahasreṇa vānarāṇām tarasvinām
"Let general Nila accompanied by strength of hundred thousand warriors go before the
army, to explore the way."


Word by word
9. niilaH= (let) Nila;vR^itaH= accompanied by;shatasahasreNa= a hundred thousand;tarasvinaam= strength;vaanaraaNaam= of monkeys;yaatu= go;agre= before;asya= this;balasya= army;avekshhitum= 
to explore;maargam= the way.




10Yuddha Kanda 4.10
फल मूलवता नील शीत कानन वारिणा |पथा मधुमता च आशु सेनाम् सेना पते नय
phala mūlavatā nīla śīta kānana vāriṇā |pathā madhumatā ca āśu senām senā pate naya
"Oh Nila the chief of Army! Steer the army speedily by the path, abound with fruits and
roots, cool woods and fresh water and honey."


Word by word
10. niila= Oh;Nila;senaapate= the army-general! naya = steer;senaam= the army;aashu= speedily;pathaa= by the path;phalamuulavataa= abound with fruits and roots;shiitakaananavaariNaa= cool woods and fresh water;madhumataa= and honey.




11Yuddha Kanda 4.11
दूषयेयुर् दुरात्मानः पथि मूल फल उदकम्राक्षसाः परिरक्षेथास् तेभ्यस् त्वम् नित्यम् उद्यतः
dūṣayeyur durātmānaḥ pathi mūla phala udakamrākṣasāḥ parirakṣethās tebhyas tvam nityam udyataḥ
"The evil-minded demons may spoil the roots, fruits and water in the path-way. You always
try to be on you guard."


Word by word
11. raakshhaasaaH= the demons;duraatmanaH= who are evil minded;duushhayeyuH= will spoil;muulaphalodakam= the roots;fruits and water;pathi= in the path;tvam= you;nityam= always;udyataH= try;parirakshhedhaaH= to protect;tebhyaH= from them.




12Yuddha Kanda 4.12
निम्नेषु वन दुर्गेषु वनेषु च वन ओकसःअभिप्लुत्य अभिपश्येयुः परेषाम् निहतम् बलम्
nimneṣu vana durgeṣu vaneṣu ca vana okasaḥabhiplutya abhipaśyeyuḥ pareṣām nihatam balam
"Let the monkeys jump into law grounds, into places made inaccessible by forest-grores
and into thickets and notice whether any rival forces are stationed there."


Word by word
12. vanaukasaH= (let) the monkeys;abhiplutya= jump;nimneshhu= into low grounds;vanadurgeshhu= into places made inaccessible by forest-grores;vaneshhu 
cha= and into thickets;abhipashyeyuH= and notice;balam= the army;pareshhaam= of the enemies;nihitam= stationed there.




13Yuddha Kanda 4.13
यत्तु फल्गु बलम् किंचित्तदत्रैवोपपद्यताम्एतद्धि कृत्यम् घोरम् नो विक्रमेण प्रयुज्यताम्
yattu phalgu balam kiṃcittadatraivopapadyatāmetaddhi kṛtyam ghoram no vikrameṇa prayujyatām
"Let whatever little of feeble forces stay back in Kishkindha, as our operation will
indeed be dreadful. It has to be discharged daringly."


Word by word
13. yat kimchit= whatever little;phalgu= of feeble;balam= force;tat= let it;upapadyataat= be present;atraiva= here itself;etat= this;naH= our;kR^ityam= operation;ghoram hi= is indeed 
dreadful;prayujyataam= let is be discharged;vikrameNa= daringly."




14Yuddha Kanda 4.14
सागर ओघ निभम् भीमम् अग्र अनीकम् महाबलाःकपि सिम्हा प्रकर्षन्तु शतशो अथ सहस्रशः
sāgara ogha nibham bhīmam agra anīkam mahābalāḥkapi simhā prakarṣantu śataśo atha sahasraśaḥ
"Let the best of monkeys with great strength in hundreds and thousands lead the formidable
of the army, which is akin to an oceanic stream."


Word by word
14. kapisimhaaH= let the best of monkeys;mahaabalaaH= with 
great strength;shatashaH= in hundreds;atha= and;sahasrashaH= in thousands;prakarshhantu= lead;bhiimam= the formidable;agraaniikam= front of the 
army;saagaraughanibham= which is akin to an oceanic stream."




15Yuddha Kanda 4.15
गजः च गिरि सम्काशो गवयः च महाबलःगव अक्षः च अग्रतो यान्तु गवाम् दृप्ता इव ऋषभाः
gajaḥ ca giri samkāśo gavayaḥ ca mahābalaḥgava akṣaḥ ca agrato yāntu gavām dṛptā iva ṛṣabhāḥ
"Let Gaja, equal to a mountain, Gavaya a very strong warrior and Gavaksha march in front,
as a majestic bull marches in front of a cow-herd."


Word by word
15. gajashcha= (Let) Gaja;girisamkaashaH= who is equal to 
a mountain;gavayashcha= Gavaya;mahaabalaH= a very strong man;gavaakshhashcha= and Gavaksha;yaatu= march;agrataH= in front;gavaam iva= as in front 
of cows;dR^ipataH= a majestic;R^ishhabhaH= full.




16Yuddha Kanda 4.16
यातु वानर वाहिन्या वानरः प्लवताम् पतिःपालयन् दक्षिणम् पार्श्वम् ऋषभो वानर ऋषभः
yātu vānara vāhinyā vānaraḥ plavatām patiḥpālayan dakṣiṇam pārśvam ṛṣabho vānara ṛṣabhaḥ
"Let the monkey called Rishabha, Lord of the simians and the best of the primates march
forward, duly guarding the right side of the army of the simians."


Word by word
16. R^ishhabhaH vaanaraH= Let the monkey called Rishabha;plavataam 
patiH= lord of the simians;vaanararshhabhaH= and the best of the primates;yaatu= march forward;paalayan= guarding;dakshhinam= the right;paarshvam= 
side;vaanaravaahinyaaH= of the army of simians.




17Yuddha Kanda 4.17
गन्ध हस्ती इव दुर्धर्षस् तरस्वी गन्ध मादनःयातु वानर वाहिन्याः सव्यम् पार्श्वम् अधिष्ठितः
gandha hastī iva durdharṣas tarasvī gandha mādanaḥyātu vānara vāhinyāḥ savyam pārśvam adhiṣṭhitaḥ
"Let Gandhamadana, with a strength unconquerable like an elephant in rut, proceed duly
guarding the left side of the army of monkeys."


Word by word
17. gandhamaadanaH= Let Gandhamaadna;tarasvii= with a strength;durdharshhaH= unconquerable;gandhahastiiva= like an elephant in rut;yaatu= proceed;adhishhThitaH= duly guarding;savyam= the left;paarshvam= 
side;vaanaravaahinyaaH= of the army of monkeys.




18Yuddha Kanda 4.18
यास्यामि बल मध्ये अहम् बल ओघम् अभिहर्षयन्अधिरुह्य हनूमन्तम् ऐरावतम् इव ईश्वरः
yāsyāmi bala madhye aham bala ogham abhiharṣayanadhiruhya hanūmantam airāvatam iva īśvaraḥ
"I myself, mounted on the shoulders of Hanuman, like Indra on Airavata, will march in
the centre of my troops, duly cheering the multitude of army."


Word by word
18. aham= I;adhiruhya= mounted;hanuumantam= on 
(the shoulders of) Hanuman;airaavatamiva= like on Airavata;iishvaraH= Indra;yaasyaami= will march;balamadhye= in the centre of my troops;abhiharshhayan= cheering balangham = the multitude of army.




19Yuddha Kanda 4.19
अन्गदेन एष सम्यातु लक्ष्मणः च अन्तक उपमःसार्वभौमेन भूत ईशो द्रविण अधिपतिस् यथा
angadena eṣa samyātu lakṣmaṇaḥ ca antaka upamaḥsārvabhaumena bhūta īśo draviṇa adhipatis yathā
"Let this Lakshmana, resembling the lord of Death, march on the shoulders of Angada like
Kubera the lord of riches and the sovereign of beings marches on an elephant called Sarvabhauma."


Word by word
19. eshhaH lakshhmaNashcha= Let this Lakshmana;antakopamaH= like of the lord of Death;samyaatu= march;aNgadena= on the shoulders of Angada;saarvabhaumena yathaa= like on an elephant called Sarvabhauma;draviNaadhipatiH= 
Kubera the lord of Riches;bhuteshaH= and the sovereign of beings.




20Yuddha Kanda 4.20
जाम्बवामः च सुषेणः च वेग दर्शी च वानरःऋक्ष राजो महासत्त्वः कुक्षिम् रक्षन्तु ते त्रयः
jāmbavāmḥ ca suṣeṇaḥ ca vega darśī ca vānaraḥṛkṣa rājo mahāsattvaḥ kukṣim rakṣantu te trayaḥ
Let the highly strong, Jambavan with Sushena and the monkey called Vegadarshi, all three,
guard the middle part of the army."


Word by word
20. mahaasattvaH= let the highly strong;jaambavaanshcha= Jambavan;R^iksharaajaH= the lord of the bears;sushhenashcha= Sushena;vaanaraashcha= and the monkey;vegadarshhii= called Vegadarshi;te= those;trayaH= 
three;rakshhantu= guard;kukshim= the middle part.




21Yuddha Kanda 4.21
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो वाहिनी पतिःव्यादिदेश महावीर्यान् वानरान् वानर ऱ्षभः
rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā sugrīvo vāhinī patiḥvyādideśa mahāvīryān vānarān vānara Rṣabhaḥ
"Hearing the words of Rama, Sugreeva with great valour, the commander of forces and the
lion among monkeys gave orders to the monkeys accordingly."


Word by word
21. shrutvaa= having heard;vachaH= the words;raaghavasya= of Rama;sugriivaH= Sugreeva;vaahiniipatiH= commander of the forces;vaanararshhabhaH= the lion among monkeys;mahaaviiryaH= with great valour;vyaadidesha= gave orders;vaanaraam= to the monkeys.




22Yuddha Kanda 4.22
ते वानर गणाः सर्वे समुत्पत्य युयुत्सवःगुहाभ्यः शिखरेभ्यः च आशु पुप्लुविरे तदा
te vānara gaṇāḥ sarve samutpatya yuyutsavaḥguhābhyaḥ śikharebhyaḥ ca āśu pupluvire tadā
Then, all those troops of monkeys with great speed together raised up and quickly bounced
from caves and mountain-tops.


Word by word
22. tadaa= then;sarve= all;te= those;vanaragaNaaH= troops of monkeys;mahaujanaaH= with great speed;samutpatya= together raised

विरराज समीपस्थम् सागरस्य तु तद् बलम् |मधु पाण्डु जलः श्रीमान् द्वितीय इव सागरः
virarāja samīpastham sāgarasya tu tad balam |madhu pāṇḍu jalaḥ śrīmān dvitīya iva sāgaraḥ

108Yuddha Kanda 4.108
वेला वनम् उपागम्य ततस् ते हरि पुम्गवाः |विनिविष्टाः परम् पारम् कान्क्षमाणा महाउदधेः
velā vanam upāgamya tatas te hari pumgavāḥ |viniviṣṭāḥ param pāram kānkṣamāṇā mahāudadheḥ
There, those foremost of monkeys reached the woodlands at the shore and settled down,
desiring to reach the other shore of the vast sea.

तेषाम् निविशमानानाम् सैन्यसम्नाहनिःस्वनः |अन्तर्धाय महानादमर्णवस्य प्रशुश्रुवे

While all the monkeys were halting there, the noise created out of their movement was

110Yuddha Kanda 4.110
सा महाअर्णवम् आसाद्य ह्ऱ्ष्टा वानर वाहिनी |त्रिधा निविष्टा महती रामस्यार्थपराभवत्
sā mahāarṇavam āsādya hRṣṭā vānara vāhinī |tridhā niviṣṭā mahatī rāmasyārthaparābhavat
That army of the monkeys ruled by Sugreeva, stationed as three divisios (viz. 1. bears
2. long tailed monkes and 3. monkeys) looked fully dedicated to the cause of Rama.

111Yuddha Kanda 4.111
सा महार्णवमासाद्य हृष्टा वानरवाहिनी |वायु वेग समाधूतम् पश्यमाना महाअर्णवम्
sā mahārṇavamāsādya hṛṣṭā vānaravāhinī |vāyu vega samādhūtam paśyamānā mahāarṇavam
That army of monkeys reached the mighty ocean and was delighted to behold the mighty
ocean being diffused by the velocity of wind.

112Yuddha Kanda 4.112
दूर पारम् असम्बाधम् रक्षो गण निषेवितम् |पश्यन्तो वरुण आवासम् निषेदुर् हरि यूथपाः
dūra pāram asambādham rakṣo gaṇa niṣevitam |paśyanto varuṇa āvāsam niṣedur hari yūthapāḥ
Seeing the sea, the abode of Varuna, which was boundless and having the opposite shore

चण्ड नक्र ग्रहम् घोरम् क्षपा आदौ दिवस क्षये |हसन्तमिव फेनौघैर्नृत्यन्तमिव चोर्मिभिः
caṇḍa nakra graham ghoram kṣapā ādau divasa kṣaye |hasantamiva phenaughairnṛtyantamiva cormibhiḥ
Rendered appalling by the ferocity of fierce alligators and crocodiles, that ocen with
its foaming waves at the end of the day and at the beginning of the night, appeared to laugh and dance.

चन्द्र उदये समाधूतम् प्रतिचन्द्र समाकुलम् |चण्ड अनिल महाग्राहैः कीर्णम् तिमि तिमिम्गिलैः

115Yuddha Kanda 4.115
दीप्त भोगैर् इव आक्रीर्णम् भुजम्गैर् वरुण आलयम् |अवगाढम् महासत्तैर् नाना शैल समाकुलम्सुदुर्गम् द्रुगम् अमार्गम् तम् अगाधम् असुर आलयम्
dīpta bhogair iva ākrīrṇam bhujamgair varuṇa ālayam |avagāḍham mahāsattair nānā śaila samākulamsudurgam drugam amārgam tam agādham asura ālayam
That sea, the abode of Varuna was filled with serpents bestowed with flaming hoods, plunged
with mighty aquatic creatures, abounding in various types of mountains, too difficult to cross, with
an inaccessible path, suffocationly fathomless and an abode of demons.

116Yuddha Kanda 4.116
मकरैर् नाग भोगैः च विगाढा वात लोहिताःउत्पेतुः च निपेतुः च प्रवृद्धा जल राशयः

117Yuddha Kanda 4.117
अग्नि चूर्णम् इव आविद्धम् भास्कर अम्बु मनो रगम्सुर अरि विषयम् घोरम् पाताल विषमम् सदा
agni cūrṇam iva āviddham bhāskara ambu mano ragamsura ari viṣayam ghoram pātāla viṣamam sadā
Emitting whirled sparkles, shining with large water-snakes, a fearful abode of enemies

117. aaviddha agnichuurNamiva= emitting (whirled) sparkles;bhaasvaraambumahoragam= shining with large water-snakes;sadaa= forever;suraarinilayam= abode of enemies

118Yuddha Kanda 4.118
सागरम् च अम्बर प्रख्यम् अम्बरम् सागर उपमम् |सागरम् च अम्बरम् च इति निर्विशेषम् अदृश्यत
sāgaram ca ambara prakhyam ambaram sāgara upamam |sāgaram ca ambaram ca iti nirviśeṣam adṛśyata
The ocean looked like the sky. The sky looked like the ocean. The ocean and the sky looked
alike without any distinction.


Word by word
118. saagaram= the ocean;ambaraprakhyam= looked like the sky;ambaram= the sky;saagaropamam= looked like the ocean;saagaram cha= the 
ocean;adR^ishyata= appeared;ambaramcheti= like the sky;nirvisheshham= without distinction.




119Yuddha Kanda 4.119
सम्पृक्तम् नभसा हि अम्भः सम्प्ऱ्क्तम् च नभो अम्भसाताद्ऱ्ग् रूपे स्म द्ऱ्श्येते तारा रत्न समाकुले
sampṛktam nabhasā hi ambhaḥ sampRktam ca nabho ambhasātādRg rūpe sma dRśyete tārā ratna samākule
The water blended with sky and the sky blended with water. Filled with stars above and
the pearls below, both the sky and the sea looked with the same splendour.

sea;dR^ishyate= looked;tadR^igruupe= with the same splendour.




120Yuddha Kanda 4.120
समुत्पतित मेघस्य वीच्चि माला आकुलस्य च |विशेषो न द्वयोर् आसीत् सागरस्य अम्बरस्य च
samutpatita meghasya vīcci mālā ākulasya ca |viśeṣo na dvayor āsīt sāgarasya ambarasya ca
There was no distinction between the two, of the sea filled with a row of waves and of
the sky with a row of falling clouds.

120. naasiit= there was no;visheshhaH= distinction;dvayoH= between the two;saagarasya= of the sea;viichimaalaakulasya= filled with a row 
of waves;ambarasyacha= and of the sky;samitpatitameghasya= with a row of falling

121Yuddha Kanda 4.121
अन्योन्यैर् आहताः सक्ताः सस्वनुर् भीम निह्स्वनाःऊर्मयः सिन्धु राजस्य महाभेर्य इव आहवे
anyonyair āhatāḥ saktāḥ sasvanur bhīma nihsvanāḥūrmayaḥ sindhu rājasya mahābherya iva āhave
The waves of the ocean together banging one another with a terrific resonance, sounded
like a kettle-drum in the sky.

121. uurmayaH= the waves;sindhuraajasya= of the ocean;saktaaH= together;aahataaH= banging;anyonyaiH= one another;bhiimaniHsvanaaH= with a terrific resonce;sasvanuH= sounded;mahaabherya iva= like a kettle drum;ambare= in the sky.




122Yuddha Kanda 4.122
रत्न ओघ जल सम्नादम् विषक्तम् इव वायुना
ratna ogha jala samnādam viṣaktam iva vāyunā
Those high-souled monkeys saw the sea lashed with winds, resonating with abundance of
precious stones and water, rising high as if enraged in a grip of hurricane, filled with a number of
aquatic creatures and tossed by them in the air by seemingly murmuring waves.


Word by word
122;123. mahaatmanaH= the high-souled;te= those (monkeys) 
dadR^ishuH = saw;vaataahata jalaashayam= the sea lashed with winds;ratnaughajalasamnaadam= resonating with abundance of precious stones and water;vishhaktamiva= as in a grip;vaayunaa= of hurricane;utpatantam= rising high;kruddhamiva= as if enraged;yaadogaNasamaakulam= filled with a number of aquatic creatures;aniloddhuutam= tossed 
by them;aakaashe= in the air;pralapantam iva= by seemingly murmering;uurmibhiH= waves.




123Yuddha Kanda 4.123
उत्पतन्तम् इव क्रुद्धम् यादो गण समाकुलम् |ददृशुस् ते महात्मानो वात आहत जल आशयम्अनिल उद्धूतम् आकाशे प्रवल्गतम् इव ऊर्मिभिः
utpatantam iva kruddham yādo gaṇa samākulam |dadṛśus te mahātmāno vāta āhata jala āśayamanila uddhūtam ākāśe pravalgatam iva ūrmibhiḥ
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


124Yuddha Kanda 4.124
ततो विस्मयामापन्ना हरयो ददृशुः स्थिताःब्रान्त ऊर्मि जल सम्नादम् प्रलोलम् इव सागरम्
tato vismayāmāpannā harayo dadṛśuḥ sthitāḥbrānta ūrmi jala samnādam pralolam iva sāgaram
The standing monkeys were struck with amazement to see the ocean seemed moving, full
of resonance produced by a multitude of dashing waves rolling to and fro.


Word by word
124. tataH= then;sthitaaH= the standing;harayaH= monkeys;aapannaH= were struck;vismayam= with astonishment;dadR^ishuH= (and) saw;saagaram= the sea;pralolamiva= seemed moving;bhraantormijaalasamnaadam= full of resonance produced by a multitude of dashing waves rolling to and fro.



    
  
  After hearing the report of Hanuma, Rama fixes an auspicious hour for the departure of his forces to Lanka and perceives good omens. The Army reaches the shores of the sea.

text:
Home/Yuddha Kanda/Sarga 2

  Yuddha Kanda · Sarga 2
  Sugreeva comforts Rama, who is tormented with grief…
  Sugreeva comforts Rama, who is tormented with grief, asking him to keep away from apprehensive mind and to think of ways and means to cross the ocean.

1Yuddha Kanda 2.1
तम् तु शोकपरिद्यूनम् रामम् दशरथात्मजम् |उवाच वचनम् श्रीमान् सुग्रीवह् शोकनाशनम्
tam tu śokaparidyūnam rāmam daśarathātmajam |uvāca vacanam śrīmān sugrīvah śokanāśanam
The glorious Sugreeva made the following reply, which was intended to expel his
grief, to Rama the son of Dasaratha who felt miserable with anguish.


Word by word
1. shriimaan= the glorious;sugriivaH= Sugreeva;uvaacha= spoke;shokanaashanam= (these) grief-removing;vachanam=
words;tu= then;tam raamam\ to that Rama;dasharathaatmajam= the son of
Dasaratha;shokaparidyuunam= felt miserable by grief.




2Yuddha Kanda 2.2
किम् त्वया तप्यते वीर यथान्यः प्राकृतस्तथा |मैवम् भूस्त्यज सतापम् कृतघ्न इव सौहृदम्
kim tvayā tapyate vīra yathānyaḥ prākṛtastathā |maivam bhūstyaja satāpam kṛtaghna iva sauhṛdam
"Oh, hero! Why are you lamenting thus, as any other ordinary man? Do not be
sorrowful like this. Abandon your grief, as an ungrateful man abandons friendship."


Word by word
2. viira= "Oh;hero! Kim= why;tapyate= is it
lamented;tvayaa= by you;tathaa= thus;yathaa= as;anyaH=
any other;prakR^itaH= ordinary man? maa bhuuH = do not be(sorrowful);evam=
like this;tyaja= abandon;santaapam= grief;sauhR^idam iva= as
abandoning friendship;kR^itaghnaH= by an ungrateful man.




3Yuddha Kanda 2.3
सम्तापस्य च ते स्थानम् न हि पश्यामि राघव |प्रवृत्तामुपलब्धायाम् ज्ञाते च निलये रिपोः
samtāpasya ca te sthānam na hi paśyāmi rāghava |pravṛttāmupalabdhāyām jñāte ca nilaye ripoḥ
"As the information about Seetha has since been gathered, I do not indeed see any
scope for your grief Oh, Rama!"


Word by word
3. pravR^ittau= "As the information (about Seetha);upalabdhaayaam= has been procured;na pashyaami hi= I do not indeed see;
sthaanam;any scope for;te= your;samtaapasya= grief;raaghava= Oh;
Rama!"




4Yuddha Kanda 2.4
मतिमान् शास्त्रवित्प्राज्ञः पण्डितश्चासि राघव |त्यजेमाम् प्राकृताम् उद्धिं कृतात्मेवार्थदूषणीम्
matimān śāstravitprājñḥ paṇḍitaścāsi rāghava |tyajemām prākṛtām uddhiṃ kṛtātmevārthadūṣaṇīm
"Oh, Rama! You are a wise person, a knower of sacred works, an intellectual and a
learned man. Give up these ordinary apprehensions like a man whose spirit is disciplined gives up
ideas which spoil the purpose.


Word by word
4. raaghava= "Oh;Rama! asi= you are;matimaan=
a wise man;shaastravit= a knower of sacred works;praajJNaH= an intellectual;paNDitashchaasi= and a learned man;tyaja= give up;imam= these;prakR^itaam= ordinary;buddhim= conjectures;arthaduushhiNiim buddhim
iva= like giving up conjectures which spoil the purpose;kR^itaatmaa= by one whose

5Yuddha Kanda 2.5
संद्रम् लङ्घयित्वा तु महानक्रसमाकुलम् |लङ्कामारोहयिष्यामो हनिष्यामश्च ते रिपुम्
saṃdram laṅghayitvā tu mahānakrasamākulam |laṅkāmārohayiṣyāmo haniṣyāmaśca te ripum
"We shall make our way up to Lanka, by crossing the ocean filled with large
crocodiles. We shall destroy your enemy."


Word by word
5. aarohayishhyaamaH= "we shall make our way up;laN^kaam=
to Lanka;laN^ghayitvaa= by crossing;samudram= the ocean;mahaa nakra
samaakulam= which is filled with large crocodiles;hanishhyaamashcha= we shall
destroy;te= your;ripum= enemy.




6Yuddha Kanda 2.6
निरुत्साहस्य दीनस्य शोकपर्याकुलात्मनः |सर्वार्था व्यवसीदन्ति व्यसनम् चाधिगच्छति
nirutsāhasya dīnasya śokaparyākulātmanaḥ |sarvārthā vyavasīdanti vyasanam cādhigacchati
"All action get dissipated by a person who is non-enthusiastic, depressed and
disturbed with grief. Such a person gets into troubles too."

dissipated;nirutsaahasya= by a non-enthusiastic person;diinasya= a depressed

7Yuddha Kanda 2.7
इमे शूराः समर्थाश्च सर्वतो हरियूथपाः |त्वत्प्रियार्थम् कृतोत्साहाः प्रवेष्टुमपि पावकम्एषाम् हर्षेण जानामि तर्कश्चापि दृढो मम
ime śūrāḥ samarthāśca sarvato hariyūthapāḥ |tvatpriyārtham kṛtotsāhāḥ praveṣṭumapi pāvakameṣām harṣeṇa jānāmi tarkaścāpi dṛḍho mama
"These leaders of monkey squads are gallant and efficient in all ways. They are
enthusiastic even to enter a fire for your sake. I understand this from their joy and my reasoning
too is sound."


Word by word
7. ime= "These;hariyuuthapaaH= leaders of monkey troops;shuuraaH= are gallant;samarthaashcha= and efficient;sarvataH= in
every way;kR^itotsaahaaH= they are made of enthusiasm;praveshhTum api= even

evam uktaḥ tu hanumān rāghaveṇa mahātmanā |sītāyā bhāṣitam sarvam nyavedayata rāghave

by Seetha.

The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.

    
  
  Hanuma narrates at length an incident connected with a crow that occured during the sojourn of Seetha with Rama at Chitrakuta, which was related by Seetha by way of a token of remembrance. Seetha then describes her miserable state to Hanuma and requests him to ask Rama, Lakshmana and Sugreeva to came to Lanka to destroy Ravana together with his army. Hanuma consoles Seetha, saying that Rama and Lakshmana would reduce Lanka to ashes and take her back to Ayodhya. When Hanuma further requests Seetha to give a token of remembrance to be handed over to Rama, she gives him a jewel for the head as a token.Hanuma narrates at length an incident connected with a crow that occurred during the sojourn of Seetha with Rama at Chitrakuta, which was related by Seetha by way of a token of remembrance. Seetha then describes her miserable state to Hanuma and requests him to ask Rama, Lakshmana and Sugreeva to come to Lanka to destroy Ravana together with his army. Hanuma consoles Seetha, saying that Rama and Lakshmana would reduce Lanka to ashes and take her back to Ayodhya. When Hanuma further requests Seetha to give a token of remembrance to be handed over to Rama, she gives him a jewel for the head as a token.

1Sundara Kanda 65.1
ततः प्रस्रवणम् शैलम् ते गत्वा चित्र काननम् |प्रणम्य शिरसा रामम् लक्ष्मणम् च महाबलम्
tataḥ prasravaṇam śailam te gatvā citra kānanam |praṇamya śirasā rāmam lakṣmaṇam ca mahābalam
Keeping Angada the prince in their forefront those monkeys, on reaching Mount Prasravana
having forests of variegated appearance, offered their salutation by bowing their heads in reverence
to Rama and the mighty Lakshmana, greeting Sugreeva respectfully. Then, they started narrating the news
of Seetha.

ततः सम्भाषिता देवी सर्वम् अर्थम् च दर्शिता
tataḥ sambhāṣitā devī sarvam artham ca darśitā
"Thereafter, I spoke and explained to Seetha, about the entire significance of my arrival
there. On hearing about the alliance between Rama and Sugreeva, she was quite pleased. Her morality
as well as her devotion in you are steadfast."


Word by word
16;17. tataH= thereafter;devii= Seetha the princess;sambhaaSitaa= was spoken;darshitaa= and explained;sarvam artham= about all 
the significance (of my arrival);shrutvaa= on hearing;raama sugriivasakhyam= about 
the friendship between Rama and Sugreeva;upaagataa= she obtained;priitim= satisfaction;asyaaH= her;samudaachaaraH= right practice of conduct;niyataH= is constant;tathaa= and;bhaktishcha= her devotion;tvayi= in you;is also constant.




17Sundara Kanda 65.17
राम सुग्रीव सख्यम् च श्रुत्वा प्रीतिम् उपागता |नियतः समुदाचारो भक्तिः च अस्याः तथा त्वयि
rāma sugrīva sakhyam ca śrutvā prītim upāgatā |niyataḥ samudācāro bhaktiḥ ca asyāḥ tathā tvayi
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


18Sundara Kanda 65.18
एवम् मया महाभागा दृष्टा जनक नन्दिनी |उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता त्वत् भक्त्या पुरुष ऋषभ
evam mayā mahābhāgā dṛṣṭā janaka nandinī |ugreṇa tapasā yuktā tvat bhaktyā puruṣa ṛṣabha
"O, the foremost of men! I thus saw that illustrious Seetha, endowed with severe penance
and devotion towards you."


Word by word
18. puruSarSabha= O foremost of men!;mahaabhaagaa= the illustrious;janakanandinii= Seetha;dR^ShiTaa= was seen;evam= thus;mayaa= by me;(Seetha) yuktaa ugreNa tapasaa= was endowed with severe penance;tvadbhaktyaa= and devotion towards you.




19Sundara Kanda 65.19
अभिज्ञानम् च मे दत्तम् यथा वृत्तम् तव अन्तिके |चित्र कूटे महाप्राज्ञ वायसम् प्रति राघव
abhijñānam ca me dattam yathā vṛttam tava antike |citra kūṭe mahāprājña vāyasam prati rāghava
"O Rama, of great intelligence! To me, she gave as a token of remembrance, a previous
event of a crow occurred at your vicinity in Mount Chitrakuta."


Word by word
19. raaghava= O Rama;mahaapraajJNa= of great intelligence!;abhijJNaanam= a token of remembrance;dattam= was given;me= to me;yathaa vR^ittam= a previous event;vaayasam prati= about a crow;tava antike= at your vicinity;chitrakuuTe= in Mount Chitrakuta.




20Sundara Kanda 65.20
विज्ञाप्यः च नर व्याघ्रो रामो वायु सुत त्वया |अखिलेन इह यत् दृष्टम् इति माम् आह जानकी
vijñāpyaḥ ca nara vyāghro rāmo vāyu suta tvayā |akhilena iha yat dṛṣṭam iti mām āha jānakī
"Seetha spoke to me saying, 'O Hanuma! Inform Rama, the foremost among men, all that
you have seen here."


Word by word
20. jaanakii= Seetha;saha= spoke;maam= to me;iti= saying;vaayusut= "O Hanuma!;raamaH= Rama;nara vyaaghraH= the foremost of men;vijJNaapya= is to be informed;akhilena= all;yat= of which;dR^iShTam= seen;tvayaa= by you;iha= here."




21Sundara Kanda 65.21
अयम् च अस्मै प्रदातव्यम् यत्नात् सुपरिरक्षितम् |ब्रुवता वचनानि एवम् सुग्रीवस्य उपशृण्वतः
ayam ca asmai pradātavyam yatnāt suparirakṣitam |bruvatā vacanāni evam sugrīvasya upaśṛṇvataḥ
"While Sugreeva is hearing nearby and while you are telling the words in this way, let
this jewel, which is deliberately well-guarded, be given to Rama."


Word by word
21. sugriivasya= (while) Sugreeva;upashR^iNvataH= is hearing;bruvataa= and while you are telling;vachanaani= the words;evam= in this 
way;ayam cha= (let) this jewel;suparikShitaH yatnaat= well-guarded deliberately;pradaatavyaH ayam cha= be given;asmai= to this Rama.




22Sundara Kanda 65.22
एष चूडा मणिः श्रीमान् मया ते यत्न रक्षितः |मनः शिलायाः तिकलः तम् स्मरस्व इति च अब्रवीत्त्वया प्राष्टे तिम्के तम् किल स्मर्तुमर्हसि
eṣa cūḍā maṇiḥ śrīmān mayā te yatna rakṣitaḥ |manaḥ śilāyāḥ tikalaḥ tam smarasva iti ca abravīttvayā prāṣṭe timke tam kila smartumarhasi
"This beautiful jewel for the head has been well-guarded by me. You also ought to recall
a mark indeed painted by you (by slip) on the curve of my cheek with powder of an orange-red rock, when
my former mark on my forehead got effaced."


Word by word
22. eSaH= this;shriimaan= beautiful;chuuDaa maNiH= jewel for the head;suparirakSitaH= has been well-guarded;mayaa= by me;arhasi= you ought;smartum= to recall;niveshitaH kila tilakaH= a mark indeed painted;tvayaa= by you (by a slip);gaN^Dapaarshve= on the curve of my cheek;orange-red;tilake= when my former mark on my forehead;praNaShTe= got effaced.




23Sundara Kanda 65.23
एष निर्यातितः श्रीमान् मया ते वारि सम्भवःएतम् दृष्ट्वा प्रमोदिष्ये व्यसने त्वाम् इव अनघ
eṣa niryātitaḥ śrīmān mayā te vāri sambhavaḥetam dṛṣṭvā pramodiṣye vyasane tvām iva anagha
"This beautiful jewel, which has its origin in sea-water, has been sent to you. Seeing
this in my grief, I am feeling always happy as though I am seeing you."


Word by word
23. eSaH shriimaan= this beautiful jewel;vaari sambhavaH= 
which has its origin in sea-water;niryaatitaH= has been sent;te= to you;dR^iSTvaa= seeing;etam= this vyasahe = in my grief;pramodiShye= I am feeling happy;tvaaniiva= as though I am seeing you.




24Sundara Kanda 65.24
जीवितम् धारयिष्यामि मासम् दशरथ आत्मजऊर्ध्वम् मासान् न जीवेयम् रक्षसाम् वशम् आगता
jīvitam dhārayiṣyāmi māsam daśaratha ātmajaūrdhvam māsān na jīveyam rakṣasām vaśam āgatā
"O Rama! I shall be sustaining my life for a month. Having come into the control of demons,
I cannot survive beyond one month."


Word by word
24. dasharaatmaja= O Rama!;dhaarayiShyaami= I shall be sustaining;jiivitam= my life;maasam= for a mouth;aagataa= having come into;vasham= the control;rakShasaam= of demons;na jiivayam= I cannot survive;uurdhvam= above;maasaat= one month.




25Sundara Kanda 65.25
इति माम् अब्रवीत् सीता कृश अन्गी धर्म चारिणीरावण अन्तः पुरे रुद्धा मृगी इव उत्फुल्ल लोचना
iti mām abravīt sītā kṛśa angī dharma cāriṇīrāvaṇa antaḥ pure ruddhā mṛgī iva utphulla locanā
"Seetha, with her emaciated body, practicing virtue, confined in Ravana's gynaecium and
with her wide-open eyes like that of a doe, spoke to me the following words:


Word by word
25. siitaa= Seetha;kR^isha aNgii= with her emaciated body;dharma chaariNii= practising virtue;ruddhaa= confined;raavaNaantaH pure= in Ravana's gynaceium;utphulla lochanaa= with her wide-open eyes;mR^igiiva= 
like that of a doe;abraviit= spoke;iti= as following;maam= to me.




26Sundara Kanda 65.26
एतत् एव मया आख्यातम् सर्वम् राघव यत् यथासर्वथा सागर जले सम्तारः प्रविधीयताम्
etat eva mayā ākhyātam sarvam rāghava yat yathāsarvathā sāgara jale samtāraḥ pravidhīyatām
"O Rama! I have narrated to you whatever has occurred, in its entirety. Let a bridge
be constructed, by all means, across the waters of the ocean."


Word by word
26. raaghava= O Rama!;etat= this;sarvam eva= exactly 
in its entirety;khyaatam= has been narrated;mayaa= by me;yat yathaa= as it occurred;samtaaraH pravidhiiyataam= let a bridge by constructed;sarvathaa= by all means;saagara jale= in the waters of the ocean.




27Sundara Kanda 65.27
तौ जात आश्वासौ राज पुत्रौ विदित्वा |तच् च अभिज्ञानम् राघवाय प्रदाय |देव्या च आख्यातम् सर्वम् एव आनुपूर्व्यात् |वाचा सम्पूर्णम् वायु पुत्रः शशंस
tau jāta āśvāsau rāja putrau viditvā |tac ca abhijñānam rāghavāya pradāya |devyā ca ākhyātam sarvam eva ānupūrvyāt |vācā sampūrṇam vāyu putraḥ śaśaṃsa
Coming to know that the two princes, Rama and Lakshmana have become confident and having
given that token of remembrance to Rama, Hanuma apprised completely in so many words, in regular succession,
all that was conveyed by Seetha, the princess.


Word by word
27. viditvaa= coming to know;tau raaja putrau= that the two 
princes;Rama and Lakshmana;jaata aashvaasau= have become confident;pradaaya= 
and having given;tat abhijJNaanam= that token of remembrance;raaghavaaya= to Rama;vaayu putraH= Hanuma;shashamsa= apprised;vaachaa= in words;sampuurNam= completely;anupuurvyaat= in regular succession;sarvameva= all that;aakhyaatam= was conveyed;devyaa= by Seetha the princess.



    
  
  Angada, Hanuma and other monkeys approach Rama, Lakshmana and Sugreeva at Mount Prasravana. When monkeys start narrating the news of Seetha, Rama asks further details of Seetha. Then, the monkeys request Hanuma to explain the occurrences to Rama in detail. Then, Hanuma appraises Rama of Seetha's presence at the foot of a Simsupa tree in the midst of female-demons. After narrating the incidents related by her and delivering to Rama the jewel for the head, earlier handed-over by Seetha as a token, Hanuma conveys her message to Rama.

  Dadhimukha comes to Sugreeva and reports that Madhuvana, the grove abounding in honey, has been damaged by monkeys headed by Angada and Hanuma.

1Sundara Kanda 63.1
ततो मूर्ध्ना निपतितम् वानरम् वानर ऋषभः |दृष्ट्वा एव उद्विग्न हृदयो वाक्यम् एतत् उवाच ह
tato mūrdhnā nipatitam vānaram vānara ṛṣabhaḥ |dṛṣṭvā eva udvigna hṛdayo vākyam etat uvāca ha
Just on seeing Dadhimukha, who fell touching his feet with his head, Sugreeva the chief
of monkeys, with an agitated mind, spoke the following words:


Word by word
1. dR^iShTvaiva= just after seeing;vaanaram= Dadhimukha;nipatitam= who fell;muurdhnaa= touching the head (on his feet);vaanaram R^iShabhaH= Sugreeva the chef of monkeys;tataH= there;uvaacha ha= spoke;etat= 
these;vaakyam= words;udvigna hR^idayaH= with an agitated mind.




2Sundara Kanda 63.2
उत्तिष्ठ उत्तिष्ठ कस्मात् त्वम् पादयोः पतितो मम |अभयम् ते भवेत् वीर सत्यम् एव अभिधीयताम्
uttiṣṭha uttiṣṭha kasmāt tvam pādayoḥ patito mama |abhayam te bhavet vīra satyam eva abhidhīyatām
"O valiant monkey! Stand up, rise! Why have you fallen on my feet? I grant you immunity
from fear. Let the entire truth be spoken!"


Word by word
2. viira= O valiant monkeys!;uttiShTha uttiShTha= stand up;
rise!;kasmaat= for what reason;tvam= have you;patitaH= fallen;mama paadayoH= on my feet?;te abhayam bhavet= I grant you immunity from fear;sarvameva 
abhidhiiyataam= Let the entire truth be spoken!.




3Sundara Kanda 63.3
स तु विश्वासितः तेन सुग्रीवेण महात्मना |उत्थाय च महाप्राज्ञो वाक्यम् दधि मुखो अब्रवीत्
sa tu viśvāsitaḥ tena sugrīveṇa mahātmanā |utthāya ca mahāprājño vākyam dadhi mukho abravīt
Thus inspired by the high-souled Sugreeva with confidence, that highly intelligent Dadhimukha,
rising up, spoke the following words:


Word by word
3. vishvaasitaH= thus inspired with confidence;mahaatmanaa tena 
sugreevaNa= by that high-souled Sugreeva;saH sumahaa praaJNaH dadhimukhaH= that vastly 
intelligent Dadhimukha;utthaaya= rising up;abraviit= spoke;vaakyam= 
(the following) words:




4Sundara Kanda 63.4
न एव ऋक्ष रजसा राजन् न त्वया न अपि वालिना |वनम् निसृष्ट पूर्वम् हि भक्षितम् तत् तु वानरैः
na eva ṛkṣa rajasā rājan na tvayā na api vālinā |vanam nisṛṣṭa pūrvam hi bhakṣitam tat tu vānaraiḥ
"O king! Madhuvana was indeed not set free previously at any time by Riksharajas, your
father, or by you, or by even Vali. That Madhuvana has been consumed away by the monkeys."


Word by word
4. raajaa= O king!;vanam= Madhuvana;naiva nispR^iSTa 
puurvam hi= was not indeed set free previously at any time;R^ikSha raajasaa= by Riksharajas;
your father;na= nor;tvayaa= by you;na= nor vaalina api = by Vali eve;tachcha= It;bhakShitam= has been consumed;vaanaraiH= by the monkeys.




5Sundara Kanda 63.5
एभिः प्रधर्षिताः च एव वारिता वन रक्षिभिः |मधूनि अचिन्तयित्वा इमान् भक्षयन्ति पिबन्ति च
ebhiḥ pradharṣitāḥ ca eva vāritā vana rakṣibhiḥ |madhūni acintayitvā imān bhakṣayanti pibanti ca
"When these guards of the grove obstructed the monkeys, they disregarded the guards and
continue to eat the fruits and drink the honey too."


Word by word
5. vaanaraaH= the monkeys;pradharShitaaH cha eva= when frightened;ebhiH vana rakShibhiH= by these guards of the grove;achintayitvaa= disregarding;imaan= then;bhakShayanti= (they) continue to eat (the fruits);pibanti cha= and drink;madhuuni= the honey.




6Sundara Kanda 63.6
शिष्टम् अत्र अपविध्यन्ति भक्षयन्ति तथा अपरे |निवार्यमाणाः ते सर्वे भ्रुवौ वै दर्शयन्ति हि
śiṣṭam atra apavidhyanti bhakṣayanti tathā apare |nivāryamāṇāḥ te sarve bhruvau vai darśayanti hi
"Some are throwing away a remnant of honey, after drinking it there and some others are
consuming that remnant. When prevented by us, all of them are indeed exhibiting their eye-brows to us
(in anger)."


Word by word
6. apavidhyanti= some are throwing away;shiShTam= the remnant 
(after drinking) of the honey;atra= there;tathaa= and;apare= some others;bhakShayanti= are consuming (that remnant);nivaaryamaaNaaH= (when) prevented (by 
us);te sarve= all of them;darshayanti hi= are indeed showing;bhruvaH= their eye-brows.




7Sundara Kanda 63.7
इमे हि सम्रब्धतराः तथा तैः सम्प्रधर्षिताः |वारयन्तो वनात् तस्मात् क्रुद्धैः वानर पुम्गवैः
ime hi samrabdhatarāḥ tathā taiḥ sampradharṣitāḥ |vārayanto vanāt tasmāt kruddhaiḥ vānara pumgavaiḥ
"When these guards of the grove became angry and tried to keep them off from the grove,
those enraged monkeys threatened them."


Word by word
7. ime= (when) these guards of the grove;samrabdhataraaH= 
are more angry;tathaa= and;vaarayantaH= keeping them off;tasmaat vaanaat= from that grove;sampradharShitaaH= they were threatened;taiH kruddhaiH vaanarapuN^gavaiH= by those enraged monkeys.




8Sundara Kanda 63.8
ततः तैः बहुभिः वीरैः वानरैः वानर ऋषभाः |सम्रक्त नयनैः क्रोधाद्त् हरयः सम्प्रचालिताः
tataḥ taiḥ bahubhiḥ vīraiḥ vānaraiḥ vānara ṛṣabhāḥ |samrakta nayanaiḥ krodhādt harayaḥ sampracālitāḥ
"O chief of monkeys! Then, those valiant monkeys in large numbers, having their red eyes
in anger, drove away these monkeys."


Word by word
8. vaanara R^iShabhaaH= O chief of monkeys!;taiH viiraiH bahubhiH 
vaanaraiH= eyes;by those valiant monkeys in large numbers;samrakta nayanaiH= having 
red-eyes;harayaH= these monkeys;tataH= then;pravichaalitaaH= were driven 
away;krodhaat= with anger.




9Sundara Kanda 63.9
पाणिभिः निहताः केचित् केचिज् जानुभिः आहताः |प्रकृष्टाः च यथा कामम् देव मार्गम् च दर्शिताः
pāṇibhiḥ nihatāḥ kecit kecij jānubhiḥ āhatāḥ |prakṛṣṭāḥ ca yathā kāmam deva mārgam ca darśitāḥ
"Those monkeys struck some of the guards with their hands. They beat some of them with
their knees. They dragged some of them and tossed them into air."


Word by word
9. kechit= some;nihataaH= were struck down;paaNibhiH= with their hands;kechit= some;aahataaH= were beaten;jaanubhiH= with 
their knees;prakR^iShTaaH= being dragged;yathaa kaamam= as liked by them;darshitaaH cha= they were tossed into;deva maargam= air.




10Sundara Kanda 63.10
एवम् एते हताः शूराः त्वयि तिष्ठति भर्तरि |कृत्स्नम् मधु वनम् चैव प्रकामम् तैः प्रभक्ष्यते
evam ete hatāḥ śūrāḥ tvayi tiṣṭhati bhartari |kṛtsnam madhu vanam caiva prakāmam taiḥ prabhakṣyate
"While you are in the position of a king, those monkeys have beaten these valiant guards
and are eating away the entire Maduvana too."


Word by word
10. tvayi tiShThati bhartari= while you are in the position of a king;ete= these;shuuraaH= valiant guards;hataaH= were beaten;taiH= by those monkeys;kR^itsnam= the entire;madhu vanam chaiva= Madhuvana too;prakaamam prabhakSyate= is being eaten completely.




11Sundara Kanda 63.11
एवम् विज्ञाप्यमानम् तु सुग्रीवम् वानर ऋषभम् |अपृच्छत् तम् महाप्राज्ञो लक्ष्मणः पर वीरहा
evam vijñāpyamānam tu sugrīvam vānara ṛṣabham |apṛcchat tam mahāprājño lakṣmaṇaḥ para vīrahā
Lakshmana, the killer of hostile heroes and a very wise man, asked that Sugreeva, the
excellent of monkeys (as follows) while Dadhimukha was thus reporting to him:


Word by word
11. tam sugriivam= to that Sugreeva;vaanara R^Shabham= the 
excellent of monkeys;vijJNaapyamaanam= who was being reported;evam= thus;(by 
Dadhimukha);lakShmaNaH= Lakshmana;para viirahaa= the killer of hostile heroes;mahaapraajJNaH= and a very wise man;apR^ichchhat= asked (as follows):




12Sundara Kanda 63.12
किम् अयम् वानरो राजन् वनपः प्रत्युपस्थितः |कम् च अर्थम् अभिनिर्दिश्य दुह्खितो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
kim ayam vānaro rājan vanapaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ |kam ca artham abhinirdiśya duhkhito vākyam abravīt
"O king! Why has this monkey the garden-protector, come here?' Pointing out what matter
has this monkey in grief, spoken these words to you?"


Word by word
12. raajam= O king!;kim= why;ayam vaanaraH= has 
this monkey;vanapaH= the garden-protector;pratyupasthitaH= come (here)?;abhinirdishya= pointing out;kam= what;artham= matter;duHkhitaH= has this monkey 
in grief;abraviit= spoken;vaakyam= some words (to you)?




13Sundara Kanda 63.13

Hearing the words of the high-souled Lakshmana, the eloquent Sugreeva replied to him
as follows:

आर्य लक्ष्मण सम्प्राह वीरो दधि मुखः कपिः |अन्गद प्रमुखैः वीरैः भक्षितम् मधु वानरैःविचित्य दक्षिणामाशामागतैर्हरिपुङ्गवैः

17Sundara Kanda 63.17
वनम् यथा अभिपन्नम् तैः साधितम् कर्म वानरैः |दृष्टा देवी न संदेहो न च अन्येन हनूमता
vanam yathā abhipannam taiḥ sādhitam karma vānaraiḥ |dṛṣṭā devī na saṃdeho na ca anyena hanūmatā
"When those monkeys have overpowered Madhuvana, then it means that our task has been
accomplished by the monkeys. Seetha was found. There is no doubt. None other than Hanuma must have seen
Seetha."

न हि अन्यः साधने हेतुः कर्मणो अस्य हनूमतः |कार्य सिद्धिः हनुमति मतिः च हरि पुम्गवव्यवसायः च वीर्यम् च श्रुतम् च अपि प्रतिष्ठितम्
na hi anyaḥ sādhane hetuḥ karmaṇo asya hanūmataḥ |kārya siddhiḥ hanumati matiḥ ca hari pumgavavyavasāyaḥ ca vīryam ca śrutam ca api pratiṣṭhitam
"There is none other than, Hanuma who is the executor in accomplishing this work. In
that Hanuma, the foremost among the monkeys, capacity to accomplish any object; intelligence; strenuous,
vigour effort; and learning are well established in his life."

जाम्बवान् यत्र नेता स्यात् अन्गदस्य बल ईश्वरः |हनूमान् च अपि अधिष्ठाता न तस्य गतिः अन्यथा

angada pramukhaiḥ vīraiḥ hatam madhu vanam kilavāritāḥ sahitāḥ pālāḥ tathā jānubhiḥ āhatāḥ
"It is so reported that Madhuvana has been destroyed by the heroes with Angada as the

etat artham ayam prāpto vaktum madhura vāg ihanāmnā dadhi mukho nāma hariḥ prakhyāta vikramaḥ
"To tell this matter in sweet words, the monkey renowned by Dadhimukha by name, with

22Sundara Kanda 63.22
दृष्टा सीता महाबाहो सौमित्रे पश्य तत्त्वतःअभिगम्य यथा सर्वे पिबन्ति मधु वानराः
dṛṣṭā sītā mahābāho saumitre paśya tattvataḥabhigamya yathā sarve pibanti madhu vānarāḥ
"O the long-armed Lakshmana! Perceive the truth that Seetha has been seen and see that

23Sundara Kanda 63.23
न च अपि अदृष्ट्वा वैदेहीम् विश्रुताः पुरुष ऋषभवनम् दात्त वरम् दिव्यम् धर्षयेयुः वन ओकसः
na ca api adṛṣṭvā vaidehīm viśrutāḥ puruṣa ṛṣabhavanam dātta varam divyam dharṣayeyuḥ vana okasaḥ
"O Lakshmana, the foremost among men! If the renowned monkeys have not seen Seetha, they

24Sundara Kanda 63.24
ततः प्रहृष्टो धर्म आत्मा लक्ष्मणः सह राघवः
tataḥ prahṛṣṭo dharma ātmā lakṣmaṇaḥ saha rāghavaḥ
Then, the righteous Lakshmana, together with Rama, felt delighted. Hearing the words

26Sundara Kanda 63.26
श्रुत्वा दधि मुखस्य इदम् सुग्रीवः तु प्रहृष्य च |वन पालम् पुनः वाक्यम् सुग्रीवः प्रत्यभाषत

and further spoke to Dadhimukha, the guardian of the grove (as follows):

much pleased;punaH= and further;pratyabhaaShataH= spoke;vaakyam= the 
following words;vana paalam= to the guardian of the grove.




27Sundara Kanda 63.27
प्रीतो अस्मि सौम्य यत् भुक्तम् वनम् तैः कृत कर्मभिः |मर्षितम् मर्षणीयम् च चेष्टितम् कृत कर्मणाम्
prīto asmi saumya yat bhuktam vanam taiḥ kṛta karmabhiḥ |marṣitam marṣaṇīyam ca ceṣṭitam kṛta karmaṇām
"I am happy that Madhuvana has been enjoyed by those monkeys, who have accomplished their
act. Since the act (damage to the grove) done by those monkeys, who have accomplished their purpose
is fit to be forgiven, I pardon them.


Word by word
27. saH aham= I;priitaH asmi= am pleased;yat= that;vanam= Madhuvana;bhuktam= has been enjoyed;taiH= by those monkeys;kR^ita karmabhiH= who have accomplished their act;cheShTitam= the act (damage to 
the grove);kR^ita karmaNaam= done by those monkeys who have accomplished their purpose;marShaNiiyam= is fit to be forgiven;marShitam= and it is pardoned.




28Sundara Kanda 63.28
इच्छामि शीघ्रम् हनुमत् प्रधानान् |शाखा मृगान् तान् मृग राज दर्पान् |द्रष्टुम् कृत अर्थान् सह राघवाभ्याम् |श्रोतुम् च सीता अधिगमे प्रयत्नम्
icchāmi śīghram hanumat pradhānān |śākhā mṛgān tān mṛga rāja darpān |draṣṭum kṛta arthān saha rāghavābhyām |śrotum ca sītā adhigame prayatnam
"I, together with Rama and Lakshmana, soon desire to see those monkeys, with Hanuma as
their chief, who having acquired the pride of a lion and who attained his purpose; and also to hear
about their effort in finding out Seetha."


Word by word
28. raaghavaabhyaam saha= I;along with Rama and Lakshmana;shiighram= soon;ichchhami= desire;draShTum= to see;taan= those;shaakhaa 
mR^igaan= monkeys;hanumat pradhaanaan= with Hanuma as their chief;mR^iga raaja 
darpaan= having the pride of a lion;kR^ita arthaan= and who attained their object;shrotum cha= and to hear;prayatnam= about their effort;siitaa adhigame= in finding out Seetha.




29Sundara Kanda 63.29
प्रीतिस्फीताक्षौ सम्प्रहृष्टौ कुमारौ |दृष्ट्वा सिद्धार्थौ वानराणाम् च राजा |अङ्गैः सम्हृष्टैः कर्मसिद्धिम् विदित्वा |बाह्वोओरासन्नाम् सोऽतिमात्रम् ननन्द
prītisphītākṣau samprahṛṣṭau kumārau |dṛṣṭvā siddhārthau vānarāṇām ca rājā |aṅgaiḥ samhṛṣṭaiḥ karmasiddhim viditvā |bāhvoorāsannām so.atimātram nananda
Seeing Rama and Lakshmana with their eyes filled with ecstatic delight, the princes,
who were thrilled with joy and who accomplished their aim, Sugreeva that king of the monkeys was very
much delighted, knowing that accomplishment of their work is coming close to their hands and his limbs
were thrilled with joy.


Word by word
29. dR^iShTvaa= seeing;kumaarau= these princes;priitisphiitaakShau= with their delighted expansive eyes;samprahR^iShTau= who are thrilled with joy;siddhaarthau= and who accomplished their aim;saH= that;vaanaraaNaam raajaa= king of the monkeys;atimaatram nananda= was very much pleased;viditvaa= knowing;karmasiddhim= that accomplishment of their work;aasannaam= is coming close;baahvoH= to their 
hands;aN^gaiH= and with his limbs;samhR^iShTaiH= thrilled with joy.



    
  
  Dadhimukha comes to Sugreeva and reports that Madhuvana, the grove abounding in honey, has been damaged by monkeys headed by Angada and Hanuma. When Lakshmana in the vicinity enquires Sugreeva about the matter, Sugreeva says that by hearing about the jubilation of the monkeys, it can be concluded that Seetha has been traced out. Assuaging Dadhimukha, Sugreeva asks him to send without delay, Hanuma, Angada and others to him, so as to hear about their efforts in tracing out Seetha.

  Sundara Kanda · Sarga 61
  Leaving Mount Mahendra and leaping ahead towards Kishkindha…
  Leaving Mount Mahendra and leaping ahead towards Kishkindha, the monkeys on their way halt at Madhuvana, a protected grove abounded in honey which was dear to Sugreeva and guarded by the monkey, Dahimukha.

1Sundara Kanda 61.1
ततो जाम्बवतो वाक्यम् अगृह्णन्त वन ओकसः |अन्गद प्रमुखा वीरा हनूमान् च महाकपिः
tato jāmbavato vākyam agṛhṇanta vana okasaḥ |angada pramukhā vīrā hanūmān ca mahākapiḥ

the monkeys accepted the words of Jambavan.

2Sundara Kanda 61.2
प्रीतिमन्तः ततः सर्वे वायु पुत्र पुरः सराः |महाइन्द्र अग्रम् परित्यज्य पुप्लुवुः प्लवग ऋषभाः
prītimantaḥ tataḥ sarve vāyu putra puraḥ sarāḥ |mahāindra agram parityajya pupluvuḥ plavaga ṛṣabhāḥ
Then, the excellent monkeys, resembling Meru and Mandara mountains, like elephants in
rut, as if covering the sky, having huge bodies and colossal strength, keeping Hanuma in their front,
leaving Mount Mahendra, went ahead leaping delightfully. They looked as though conducted by the mind's
eyes of Hanuma, who is adored by living beings as having good stupendous swiftness, they having resolved
to fulfill the purpose of Rama and to attain a great glory, having accomplished the purpose and duly
determined to complete the task. All of them were looking up at narrating the previous pleasant tidings
and taking delight in war. All of them, in high spirits, were judging rightly the vengeance of Rama
against the evil-minded Ravana.

7Sundara Kanda 61.7
प्लवमानाः खम् आप्लुत्य ततः ते कानन ओक्सकः |नन्दन उपमम् आसेदुः वनम् द्रुम लता युतम्

Then, those monkeys, leaping into the sky and floating in the air, reached a garden looking
like Nandanavana the divine grove filled with trees and creepers.

grove, unapproachable for all and looking fascinated to the soul of all beings.

drumāt drumam kecit abhiplavante |kṣitau naga agrān nipatanti kecit |mahī talāt kecit udīrṇa vegā |mahādruma agrāṇi abhisampatante

गायन्तम् अन्यः प्रहसन्न् उपैति |हसन्तम् अन्यः प्रहसन्न् उपैति |रुदन्तम् अन्यः प्ररुदन्न् उपैति |नुदन्तम् अन्यः प्रणुदन्न् उपैति

18Sundara Kanda 61.18
समाकुलम् तत् कपि सैन्यम् आसीन् |मधु प्रपान उत्कट सत्त्व चेष्टम् |न च अत्र कश्चिन् न बभूव मत्तो |न च अत्र कश्चिन् न बभूव तृप्तो

None in that army was not drunk. None in that army was not satiated.
