1Ayodhya Kanda 65.1
अथ रात्र्याम् व्यतीतायाम् प्रातर् एव अपरे अहनि |वन्दिनः पर्युपातिष्ठंस् तत् पार्थिव निवेशनम्
atha rātryām vyatītāyām prātar eva apare ahani |vandinaḥ paryupātiṣṭhaṃs tat pārthiva niveśanam
While the night passed away, there arrived at the residence of the emperor, at the
dawn of the next day, highly cultured and excellently learned bards who were pronouncers of
benedictions and whose custom was to eulogize the king, as well as singers and panegyrists uttering
recitations in different styles.


Word by word
1;2. atha= thereafter;raatryaam vyatiitaayaam= while the
night passed away;praataH eva= at the dawn itself;apare= of the following;ahari= day;paryupaatishhThan= there approached;tat= that;paarthiva niveshanam= residence of the emperor;paramasamskaaraaH= highly
cultured;uttamashrutaaH= excellently learned;suutaaH= bards;maNgaLaashcha= who were pronouncers of benedictions;stutishiilaaH= and whose
custom was to eulogize the king;gaayakaaH= as well as singers;vandinaH= and
panegyrists;nigadantaH= pronouncing ;pR^ithak pR^ithak= in different
styles.




2Ayodhya Kanda 65.2
सूताः परमसंस्काराः मङ्गळाश्चोओत्तमश्रुताः |गायकाः स्तुतिशीलाश्च निगदन्तः पृथक् पृथक्
sūtāḥ paramasaṃskārāḥ maṅgaldāścoottamaśrutāḥ |gāyakāḥ stutiśīlāśca nigadantaḥ pṛthak pṛthak
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


3Ayodhya Kanda 65.3
राजानम् स्तुताम् तेषामुदात्ताभिहिताशिषाम् |प्रासादाभोगविस्तीर्णः स्तुतिशब्दो ह्यवर्तत
rājānam stutām teṣāmudāttābhihitāśiṣām |prāsādābhogavistīrṇaḥ stutiśabdo hyavartata
Their sounds of praises, uttering benedictions in a loud voice and pronouncing
accolades of the king, pervaded in full the interior area of the palace.


Word by word
3. teshhaam= their;stutishabdaH= sounds of praises;udattaabhitaashishhaa= uttering benedictions in a loud voice;stuvataam= and
pronouncing accolades;raajaanan= of the king;aavartatahi= pervaded;praasaadaabhogavistiirNaH= in full;the interior area of the palaces.




4Ayodhya Kanda 65.4
ततस्तु स्तुवताम् तेषाम् सूतानाम् पाणिवादकाः |अवदानान्युदाहृत्य पाणिवादा नवादयन्
tatastu stuvatām teṣām sūtānām pāṇivādakāḥ |avadānānyudāhṛtya pāṇivādā navādayan
While those bards are uttering praises, others who make a bang of claps, patted the
claps, eulogizing the previous glorious acts of Dasaratha.


Word by word
4. tataH= then;teshhaam suutaanaam= while those bards;stuvataam= were uttering praises;paaNivaadakaaH= some others who make noises
of claps;avaadayaan= pronounced claps;udaahR^itya= illustrating;avadaanaami= the glorious acts (of Dasaratha).




5Ayodhya Kanda 65.5
तेन शब्देन विहगाः प्रतिबुद्धा विसस्वनुः |शाखास्थाः पञ्जरस्थाश्च ये राजकुलगोचराः
tena śabdena vihagāḥ pratibuddhā visasvanuḥ |śākhāsthāḥ pañjarasthāśca ye rājakulagocarāḥ
The birds dwelling in royal palaces perched on the branches of trees and others in
cages were awakened by that sound and began to twitter.


Word by word
5. ye= which;vihagaaH= birds;raajakula
gocharaaH= dwelling in the royal palaces;shaakhaasthaaH= on the branches of trees;panjarasthaaHcha= and in cages;pratibuddhaaH= were awakened;tena
shabdena= by that sound;visasvanuH= began to twitter.




6Ayodhya Kanda 65.6
व्याहृताः पुण्य्शब्दाश्च वीणानाम् चापि निस्स्वनाः |आशीर्गेयम् च गाथानाम् पूरयामास वेश्म तत
vyāhṛtāḥ puṇyśabdāśca vīṇānām cāpi nissvanāḥ |āśīrgeyam ca gāthānām pūrayāmāsa veśma tata
The auspicious words uttered by bards parrots etc and the notes of Vina as well as
blissful songs of the metric verses filled that palace.


Word by word
6. puNya shabdaashcha= the auspicious words;vyaahR^taaH=
uttered;nissvanaaHcha= and the notes;viiNaanaam= of Vina;aashiirgeyamcha= as well as blissful songs;gaathaanaam= of the metric verses;puurayaamaasa= filled;tat= that;veshma= palace.




7Ayodhya Kanda 65.7
ततः शुचि समाचाराः पर्युपस्थान कोविदः |स्त्री वर्ष वर भूयिष्ठाउपतस्थुर् यथा पुरम्
tataḥ śuci samācārāḥ paryupasthāna kovidaḥ |strī varṣa vara bhūyiṣṭhāupatasthur yathā puram
Then, as before, persons who maintain pure practices and those who were skilled in
the services to the king, most of whom were women and eunuchs, arrived there to serve the king.


Word by word
7. tataH= then;yathaa puram= as before;shuchi
samaachaaraaH= those who maintain pure practices;paryupasthaana kovidaaH= and
those who were skilled in the services to the king;striivarshhavarabhuuyishhThaaH= most
of whom were women and eunuchs ;upatasthuH= arrived to serve(the king).




8Ayodhya Kanda 65.8
हरि चन्दन सम्पृक्तम् उदकम् कान्चनैः घटैः |आनिन्युः स्नान शिक्षा आज्ञा यथा कालम् यथा विधि
hari candana sampṛktam udakam kāncanaiḥ ghaṭaiḥ |āninyuḥ snāna śikṣā ājñā yathā kālam yathā vidhi
Those who took care of royal ablutions brought water sprinkled with yellow sandal in
golden pitchers in accordance with appropriate time and the set procedures.


Word by word
8. snaana shikshhaajJNaaH= those who took care of royal ablutions;aaninyuH= brought;udakam= water;harichandana samvR^iktam= spinkled
with yellow sandal;kaaNchanaiH= in golden;ghaTaiH= pitchers;yathaakaalam= in accordance with the appropriate time;yathaavidhi= and
according to the set procedures.




9Ayodhya Kanda 65.9
मन्गल आलम्भनीयानि प्राशनीयान् उपस्करान् |उपनिन्युस् तथा अपि अन्याः कुमारी बहुलाः स्त्रियः
mangala ālambhanīyāni prāśanīyān upaskarān |upaninyus tathā api anyāḥ kumārī bahulāḥ striyaḥ
In that manner, women too most of whom were virgins brought all that were pleasing
to the touch, eatables, decorative clothing and ornaments.


Word by word
9. tathaa= in that manner;striyaHapi= women too;kumariibahuLaaH= most of whom were virgins;upaninyuH= brought;maNgaLaalamba niiyaani= all that were pleasing to touch praashaniiyaan = eatables;upaskaraan= decorations and ornaments.




10Ayodhya Kanda 65.10
सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नम् सर्वम् विधिवदर्चितम् |सर्वम् सुगुणलक्स्मीवत्तद्भभूवाभिहारिकम्
sarvalakṣaṇasampannam sarvam vidhivadarcitam |sarvam suguṇalaksmīvattadbhabhūvābhihārikam
All that was brought near him was endowed with all auspicious characteristics
offered with reverence as per prescribed scriptures. All that was extremely graceful.


Word by word
10. sarvam= all;tat= that;abhihaarikam= which
was brought near him;abhuut= was;sarva lakshhaNasampannam= rich with all
auspicious characteristics;architam= was offered with reverence;vidhivat= as
per prescribing scriptures;sarvam= all that;suguNa lakshhmiivat= was
extremely graceful.




11Ayodhya Kanda 65.11
ततः सूर्योदयम् यावत्सर्वम् परिसमुत्सुकम् |तस्थावनुपसम्प्राप्तम् किम् स्विदित्युपश्
tataḥ sūryodayam yāvatsarvam parisamutsukam |tasthāvanupasamprāptam kim svidityupaś
All that retinue, greatly excited as they were, without coming near to the king and
with a suspicion as to what was it, stayed thus till sunrise.


Word by word
11. tataH= thereafter;sarvam= all that retinue;parisamutsukam= greatly excited;anupasampraaptam= without coming near to the
king;upashaNkitam= with a suspicion;kim svit iti= as to what was it;tasthou= stayed thus;suuryodayam yaavat= till sun rise.




12Ayodhya Kanda 65.12
अथ याः कोसल इन्द्रस्य शयनम् प्रत्यनन्तराः |ताः स्त्रियः तु समागम्य भर्तारम् प्रत्यबोधयन्
atha yāḥ kosala indrasya śayanam pratyanantarāḥ |tāḥ striyaḥ tu samāgamya bhartāram pratyabodhayan
The women who were empowered to go near the bed of Dasaratha went in proximity to
him and woke him up.


Word by word
12. atha= then;yaaH striyaH= which women;anantaraaH= have no hindrance;shayanam prati= towards the bed;kosalendraaya= of Dasaratha;taaH tu= those women only;samaagamya=
approached;bhartaaram= their lord;pratyabodhayan= and woke him up.




13Ayodhya Kanda 65.13
तथाप्युचितवृत्तास्ता विनयेन नयेन च |न ह्यस्य शयनम् स्पृष्ट्वा किम् चिदप्युपलेभिरे
tathāpyucitavṛttāstā vinayena nayena ca |na hyasya śayanam spṛṣṭvā kim cidapyupalebhire
Even so, those modest and prudent women with proper conduct, touched Dasaratha's bed
and could not detect any sign of life whatsoever in him.


Word by word
13. tathaapi= even so;taaH= those women;uchitavR^ttaaH= having proper conduct;vinayena= by their modesty;nayena= (and) by their prudence;spR^ishhTvaa= touched;shayanam= the
bed;asya= of Dasaratha;na upalebhire= and could not detect;kimchit
api= anything either.




14Ayodhya Kanda 65.14
ताः स्त्रीयः स्वप्नशीलज्ञास्चेष्टासंचलनादिषु |ता वेपथु परीताः च राज्ञः प्राणेषु शन्किताःप्रतिस्रोतः तृण अग्राणाम् सदृशम् संचकम्पिरे
tāḥ strīyaḥ svapnaśīlajñāsceṣṭāsaṃcalanādiṣu |tā vepathu parītāḥ ca rājñaḥ prāṇeṣu śankitāḥpratisrotaḥ tṛṇa agrāṇām sadṛśam saṃcakampire
Those women knew the condition of a body in sleep, by its gestures, movements and
others. As such, they were possessed of tremor apprehensive as they were about the king's life and
they resembled like tips of reeds standing against a stream.


Word by word
14. taaH striiyaH= those women;svapnashiilajJNaaH= knew
the condition of a body in sleep;cheshhTaa samchalanaadishhu= by its gestures;movements
and others;taaH= those women as such;shaNkitaH= were apprehensive;raajJNaH= of the king`s;praaNeshhu= life;vepathupariitaaHcha=
possessed of tremor;samchakaashire= and were revealing;pratisrotastR^iNaagraaNaam= like tips of reeds standing against a stream.




15Ayodhya Kanda 65.15
अथ सम्वेपमनानाम् स्त्रीणाम् दृष्ट्वा च पार्थिवम्यत् तत् आशन्कितम् पापम् तस्य जज्ञे विनिश्चयः
atha samvepamanānām strīṇām dṛṣṭvā ca pārthivamyat tat āśankitam pāpam tasya jajñe viniścayaḥ
Now, seeing the king, certainty arose in the minds of those doubting women about the
calamity (of death) that was apprehended.


Word by word
15. atha= now;dR^ishhTvaacha= on seeing;paarthivam= the king;tasya= its;vinishchayaH= certainty;jaG^ye= arose;sandehamaanaanaam= in the minds of doubting;striiNaam= women;yat= of which;paapam= calamity;aashaNkitam= that was
apprehended.




16Ayodhya Kanda 65.16
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च पुत्रशोकपराजितेप्रसुप्ते न प्रबुध्येते यथा कालसमन्विते
kausalyā ca sumitrā ca putraśokaparājiteprasupte na prabudhyete yathā kālasamanvite
Overpowered by grief for their sons, the slumbering Kausalya and Sumitra did not
wake up, as though they were completely overtaken by death.


Word by word
16. putra shoka paraajite= overpowered by grief for their sons;prasupte= the slumbering;kausalyaacha= Kausalya;sumitraacha= and
Sumitra;na prabudhyate= did not wake up;kaalasamanvite yathaa= as if they
were completely possessed of death.




17Ayodhya Kanda 65.17
निष्प्रभा च विवर्णा च सन्ना शोकेन सन्नतान व्यराजत कौसल्या तारेव तिमिरावृता
niṣprabhā ca vivarṇā ca sannā śokena sannatāna vyarājata kausalyā tāreva timirāvṛtā
Kausalya bereft of luster, pale faced, emaciated with grief and dispirited, did not
shine brightly (as before) like a star hidden away in darkness.


Word by word
17. kausalya= Kausalya;nishhprabhaacha= bereft of luster;vivarNaa= pale faced;sannaa= emaciated;shokena= by grief;sannataa= and dispirited;na vyaraajata= did not shine brightly;taareva= like a star;timiraavR^itaa= hidden away in darkness.




18Ayodhya Kanda 65.18
कौसल्यानन्तरम् राज्ञः सुमित्रा तदन्तनरम्न स्म विभ्राजते देवी शोकाश्रुलुलितानना
kausalyānantaram rājñaḥ sumitrā tadantanaramna sma vibhrājate devī śokāśrululitānanā
The queen Kausalya, immediately close to the king and with Sumitra on her side, was
not shining as before with her face ruffled by tears of grief.


Word by word
18. devii= the queen;kausalyaa= Kausalya;anantaram= immediately close;raajJNaH= to the king;sumitraa= and
sumitra;tadanantaram= on her side;na sma vibhraajate= was not shining (as
before);shokaashru lulitaananaa= with her face ruffled by tears of grief.




19Ayodhya Kanda 65.19
ते च दृष्ट्वा तथा सुप्ते शुभे देव्यौ च तम् नृपम्सुप्तमे वोद्गतप्राणमन्तः पुरमन्यत
te ca dṛṣṭvā tathā supte śubhe devyau ca tam nṛpamsuptame vodgataprāṇamantaḥ puramanyata
The persons in the gynaecium, having seen those distinguished queens in slumber and
also the king in that manner, thought that the king had lost his life while just sleeping.


Word by word
19. antaHpuram= the gynaecium;dR^ishhTvaa= having seen;te devyon shubhe= those distinguished queens;supte= sleeping;tam=
and that;nR^ipam= king;tathaa= in that manner;aamanyata= thought;udgatapraaNam= that the king had lost his life;suptameva= while merely
sleeping.




20Ayodhya Kanda 65.20
ततः प्रचुक्रुशुर् दीनाः सस्वरम् ता वर अन्गनाःकरेणवैव अरण्ये स्थान प्रच्युत यूथपाः
tataḥ pracukruśur dīnāḥ sasvaram tā vara anganāḥkareṇavaiva araṇye sthāna pracyuta yūthapāḥ
Then, those beautiful women miserably cried loudly with their voice, like female
elephants crying when their group leader an elephant was removed from their place in the
forest.


Word by word
20. tataH= then;taaH varaaNganaaH= those beautiful women;diinaH= miserably;prachukrushuH= cried loudly;sasvaram= with their
voice;kareNavaH iva= like female elephants crying;sthaana prachyuta yuuthapaaH= removed from their place;araNye= in the forest.




21Ayodhya Kanda 65.21
तासाम् आक्रन्द शब्देन सहसा उद्गत चेतनेकौसल्या च सुमित्राच त्यक्त निद्रे बभूवतुः
tāsām ākranda śabdena sahasā udgata cetanekausalyā ca sumitrāca tyakta nidre babhūvatuḥ
Kausalya and Sumitra suddenly obtained consciousness by the sound of their cries and
woke up from sleep.


Word by word
21. kausalyaacha= Kausalya and;sumitraacha= Sumitra;sahasaa= suddenly;udgatachetane= obtained consciousness;taasaam aakranda
shabdena= by their sound of cries;babhuuvatuH= and became;tyakta nidre=
relieved of sleep.




22Ayodhya Kanda 65.22
कौसल्या च सुमित्रा च दृष्ट्वा स्पृष्ट्वा च पार्थिवम्हा नाथ इति परिक्रुश्य पेततुर् धरणी तले
kausalyā ca sumitrā ca dṛṣṭvā spṛṣṭvā ca pārthivamhā nātha iti parikruśya petatur dharaṇī tale
Kausalya and Sumitra, on seeing and touching king Dasaratha, cried �O, Lord!' and
fell on the ground.


Word by word
22. kausalyaacha= Kausalya;sumitraacha= and Sumitra;dR^ishhTvaa= on seeing;spR^ishhTvaacha= and touching;paarthivam=
the king;parikrushya= cried;haanaathaa iti= as �O;lord!' patatuH=
and fell;dharaNiitala= on the ground.




23Ayodhya Kanda 65.23
सा कोसल इन्द्र दुहिता वेष्टमाना मही तलेन बभ्राज रजो ध्वस्ता तारा इव गगन च्युता
sā kosala indra duhitā veṣṭamānā mahī talena babhrāja rajo dhvastā tārā iva gagana cyutā
Rolling on the floor and covered by dust, Kausalya the daughter of Kosala king was
not shining as before and resembled a star falling down from the sky.


Word by word
23. veshhTamaanaa= rolling;mahiitale= on the floor;rajodhvastaa= and covered by dust;saa= that;kausalyendra duhitaa=
daughter of Kosala king;Kausalya;na babhraaja= was not shining;taareva= like
a star;chyutaa= slipped down;gaganaat= from the sky.




24Ayodhya Kanda 65.24
नृपे शान्तगुणे जाते कौसल्याम् पतिताम् भुविआपश्यंस्ताः स्त्रियः सर्वा हताम् नागवधूमिव
nṛpe śāntaguṇe jāte kausalyām patitām bhuviāpaśyaṃstāḥ striyaḥ sarvā hatām nāgavadhūmiva
While the king was deceased, all the women saw Kausalya who fell on the floor
appearing as a female elephant, which was killed and felled on the ground.


Word by word
24. nR^ipe= the king;jaate= became;shaantaguNe= one whose virtues were destroyed;ie. Deceased;taaHstriyaH= all the women;apashyan= saw;kausalya= Kausalya;patitaam= who fell;bhuvi= on the ground;naagavadhuu miva= like a female elephant;hataam= which was
killed (and felled on ground).




25Ayodhya Kanda 65.25
ततः सर्वा नरेन्द्रस्य कैकेयीप्रमुखाः स्त्रियःरुदन्त्यः शोकसन्तप्ता निपेतुर्गतचेतनाः
tataḥ sarvā narendrasya kaikeyīpramukhāḥ striyaḥrudantyaḥ śokasantaptā nipeturgatacetanāḥ
Kaikeyi and all other wives of king Dasaratha were weeping afflicted by grief and
fell unconscious.


Word by word
25. tataH= thereafter;kaikeyiipramukhaaH= Kaikeyi and
others;sarve= all;narendrasya= the king`s;striyaH= women;rudantyaH= were weeping;shokasantaptaaH= being afflicted by grief;nipetuH= fell;gatachetanaaH= unconscious.




26Ayodhya Kanda 65.26
ताभिः स बलवान्नादः क्रोशन्तीभिरनुद्रुतःयेन स्फीतीकृतो भूयस्तद्गृहम् समनादयत्
tābhiḥ sa balavānnādaḥ krośantībhiranudrutaḥyena sphītīkṛto bhūyastadgṛham samanādayat
That great noise was supplemented by those wailing women, bloated by which, it
rendered the house all the more noisy.


Word by word
26. balavaan= great;saHnaadaH= that noise;anudrutaH= = supplemented;taabhiH= by those women;kroshantiibhiH=
wailing;sphiitiikR^itaH= was made greater;bhuuyaH= more;yena= by
which;tat= that;gR^iham= house;




27Ayodhya Kanda 65.27
तत् समुत्त्रस्त सम्भ्रान्तम् पर्युत्सुक जन आकुलम्
tat samuttrasta sambhrāntam paryutsuka jana ākulam
That gynaecium of the king who met his appointed end was filled with people who felt
bewildered with fear and restlessness, with tumultuous wail all around, and crowded with relatives
disturbed by sorrow, with happiness withered away in it suddenly and became a sight of misery and
despondency.


Word by word
27;28. tatsadma= that gynoecium;naradevasya= of the
king;iiyushhaH= who met;dishhTaantam= the appointed end (death);santrapta sambhraanta paryutsaka janaakulam= was filled with people bewildered with fear
and restlessness;tumulaakrandam= with tumultuous wailing;sarvataaH= all
around;paritaapaartabaandhavan= having relatives disturbed by sorrow;nipatitaanandam= with its happiness withered away;sadyaH= suddenly;babhuuva= and became;diinaviklaba darshanam= a sight of misery and
despondency.




28Ayodhya Kanda 65.28
सर्वतः तुमुल आक्रन्दम् परिताप आर्त बान्धवम् |सद्यो निपतित आनन्दम् दीन विक्लव दर्शनम्बभूव नर देवस्य सद्म दिष्ट अन्तम् ईयुषः
sarvataḥ tumula ākrandam paritāpa ārta bāndhavam |sadyo nipatita ānandam dīna viklava darśanambabhūva nara devasya sadma diṣṭa antam īyuṣaḥ
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


29Ayodhya Kanda 65.29
अतीतम् आज्ञाय तु पार्थिव ऋषभम् |यशस्विनम् सम्परिवार्य पत्नयः |भृशम् रुदन्त्यः करुणम् सुदुह्खिताः |प्रगृह्य बाहू व्यलपन्न् अनाथवत्.
atītam ājñāya tu pārthiva ṛṣabham |yaśasvinam samparivārya patnayaḥ |bhṛśam rudantyaḥ karuṇam suduhkhitāḥ |pragṛhya bāhū vyalapann anāthavat.
Knowing that the glorious king of excellence had passed away, the king's wives
surrounded him with great sorrow; pitiably wailing profusely and lamented, grasping their hands one
another, like orphans.


Word by word
29. aajJNaaya= knowing;yashasvinam= the glorious;paarthivarshhabham= king of excellence;atiitam= had passed away;(his wives);samparivaarya= surrounded him;suduHkhitaaH= with great sorrow;karuNam= pitiably;rudantyaH= wailing;bhrusham= profusely;vylapan= and lamented;pragR^ihya= grasping;baahum= their hands;
(one another);anaathavaat= like orphans.



    
  
  At the dawn of the next day, panergysts and servants arrived at the palace to serve the king. Some women, who were empowered to go near the bed, detected the king's death and started crying loudly. Kausalya and Sumitra suddenly woke up from their slumber and came to know of the king's death. All the wives of Dasaratha wept miserably. The gynaecium was filled with men and women who felt bewildered with fear and restlessness; when the king met with his appointed end.

1Ayodhya Kanda 63.1
प्रतिबुद्धो मुहुर् तेन शोक उपहत चेतनः |अथ राजा दशरथः स चिन्ताम् अभ्यपद्यत
pratibuddho muhur tena śoka upahata cetanaḥ |atha rājā daśarathaḥ sa cintām abhyapadyata
The king, awakened after some time, with his mind afflicted with grief, got into an
anxious thinking.


Word by word
1. atha= then;saH raajaa= that king;pratibuddhaH= awakened;muhuurtena= after some time;shokopahata
chetanaH= with mind affiliated with grief;abhyapadyata= got into;chintaam= anxious thought.




2Ayodhya Kanda 63.2
राम लक्ष्मणयोः चैव विवासात् वासव उपमम् |आविवेश उपसर्गः तम् तमः सूर्यम् इव आसुरम्
rāma lakṣmaṇayoḥ caiva vivāsāt vāsava upamam |āviveśa upasargaḥ tam tamaḥ sūryam iva āsuram
Due to banishing of Rama and Lakshmana, a great calamity befell on Dasaratha who was
equal in strength to Indra like sun seized by obscurity, which is attributed to the demon Rahu.


Word by word
2. vivaasaat= due to the exile;raama lakSmaNayoH= of Rama
and Lakshmana;upasargaH= a great calamity;aavivesha= befell;tam=
on that Dasaratha;vaasavopamam= who is equal to Indra;suuryamiva= like sun
(seized);tamaH= by obscurity;asuram= which is attributed to the demon
Rahu.




3Ayodhya Kanda 63.3
सभार्ये निर्गते रामे कौसल्याम् कोसलेश्वरः |विवक्षुरसितापाङ्गाम् स्मृवा दुष्कृतमात्मनः
sabhārye nirgate rāme kausalyām kosaleśvaraḥ |vivakṣurasitāpāṅgām smṛvā duṣkṛtamātmanaḥ
After Rama along with his wife departed to the forest, Dasaratha the king of Kosala
recalling his earlier sin, wanted to tell Kausalya, whose eye-corners were dark in colour all about
it.


Word by word
3. raame= after Rama;nirgate sati= having departed (to
the forest);sabhaarye= along with his wife;kosaleshvaraH= Dasaratha the king
of Kosala;smR^itvaa= recalling aatmanaH = his;duSkR^itam= sin;vivakSuH= wanted to speak;kausalyaam= to Kausalya;astaapaaNgaam=
whose eye-corners were dark in colour.




4Ayodhya Kanda 63.4
स राजा रजनीम् षष्ठीम् रामे प्रव्रजिते वनम् |अर्ध रात्रे दशरथः संस्मरन् दुष्कृतम् कृतम्
sa rājā rajanīm ṣaṣṭhīm rāme pravrajite vanam |ardha rātre daśarathaḥ saṃsmaran duṣkṛtam kṛtam
After Rama was sent into exile to the forest, King Dasaratha, on the sixth night at
mid-night, was recalling his sin done (long ago).


Word by word
4. raame= after Rama;pravraajite= was sent into exile;vanam= to the forest;raajaa= king;dasharathaH= Dasaratha;SaSThiim= on the sixth;rajaniim= night;arthavaatra= at mid-night;samsmavan= was recalling;duSkR^itam= his sin;kR^itam= done (long
ago).




5Ayodhya Kanda 63.5
स राजा पुत्रशोकार्तः स्मरन् दुष्कृतमात्मनः |कौसल्याम् पुत्र शोक आर्ताम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
sa rājā putraśokārtaḥ smaran duṣkṛtamātmanaḥ |kausalyām putra śoka ārtām idam vacanam abravīt
King Dasaratha, afflicted by grief for his son, recalling his sin, spoke the
following words to Kausalya who was suffering from sorrow for her son.


Word by word
5. saH raajaa= that king;putrashokaartaH= afflicted by
grief for his son;smaram= recalling;aatmanaH= his;duSkR^itam= sin;abraviit= spoke;idam= these;vachanam= words;kausalyaam=
to Kausalya;putrashokaartaam= who was suffering from sorrow for her son.




6Ayodhya Kanda 63.6
यद् आचरति कल्याणि शुभम् वा यदि वा अशुभम् |तत् एव लभते भद्रे कर्ता कर्मजम् आत्मनः
yad ācarati kalyāṇi śubham vā yadi vā aśubham |tat eva labhate bhadre kartā karmajam ātmanaḥ
"O, blessed lady! O gracious one! A doer reaps surely the fruit of his own deeds
corresponding to the nature of work either good or bad, of that which he does!"


Word by word
6. kalyaaNi= O;blessed lady!;bhadre= O;gracious one!;yat= whatever;kartaa= a doer of an act;shubham vaa= either good;yadi vaa= or;ashubham= bad;kurute= does;labhate= (he)
obtains;tadeva= it surely;aatmanaH= his own;karmajam= result.




7Ayodhya Kanda 63.7
गुरु लाघवम् अर्थानाम् आरम्भे कर्मणाम् फलम् |दोषम् वा यो न जानाति स बालैति ह उच्यते
guru lāghavam arthānām ārambhe karmaṇām phalam |doṣam vā yo na jānāti sa bālaiti ha ucyate
"He who does not consider, while undertaking actions, the relative value of their
fruits as well as the utilities or defects accruing from them, is surely called a fool."


Word by word
7. yaH= who;aarambhe= while undertaking;karmaNaam= actions;najaanaati= does not know;gurulaaghavam= the
relative value;arthaanaam= of their utilities phalam = (or) their fruit;doSam
vaa= (or) their defect;saH= he;uchoyate ha= is surely called;baalaH iti= as a boy (fool).




8Ayodhya Kanda 63.8
कश्चित् आम्र वणम् चित्त्वा पलाशामः च निषिन्चति |पुष्पम् दृष्ट्वा फले गृध्नुः स शोचति फल आगमे
kaścit āmra vaṇam cittvā palāśāmḥ ca niṣincati |puṣpam dṛṣṭvā phale gṛdhnuḥ sa śocati phala āgame
"Anyone, who after seeing their (charming and big) flowers, greedily desires their
(large and luscious) fruits and nourishes Palasa trees, by cutting off a mongo grove, he will come
to grief after bearing of their fruit."


Word by word
8. kashchit= anyone;dR^iSTvaa= seeing;puSpam=
their flowers;gR^idhnuH= and greedily desirous of;phale= their;fruits;niSiNchati= nourishes;palaashran= Palasa trees;chhittvaa= by
cutting off;aamravanam= mango groves;saH= he;shochati= will come
to grief;phalaagame= after arrival of fruit."




9Ayodhya Kanda 63.9
अविज्ञाय फलम् यो हि कर्म त्वेवानुधावति |स शोचेत्फलवेळायाम् यथा किंशुकसेचकः
avijñāya phalam yo hi karma tvevānudhāvati |sa śocetphalaveldāyām yathā kiṃśukasecakaḥ
"He who without knowing the result goes running towards action, will come to grief
as a nourisher of Kimsuka trees coming to grief at the time of their fruit-bearing."


Word by word
9. yaH= who;avijJNaaya= without knowing;phalam= the fuit;anudhaavati= follows running;karmatu eva= towards action;saH= he kimshukaschakaH iva = as a nourisher of Kimsuka trees;phalavelaayaam=
at the time of fruit-bearing;shochet= will come to grief.




10Ayodhya Kanda 63.10
सो अहम् आम्र वणम् चित्त्वा पलाशामः च न्यषेचयम् |रामम् फल आगमे त्यक्त्वा पश्चात् शोचामि दुर्मतिः
so aham āmra vaṇam cittvā palāśāmḥ ca nyaṣecayam |rāmam phala āgame tyaktvā paścāt śocāmi durmatiḥ
"I nourished Palasa trees, by cutting off mango grove. Being wicked-minded in
abandoning Rama at the time of arrival of fruit, I am lamenting thereafter."


Word by word
10. saH aham= I as such;nyaSachayam= nourished;palashaan cha= Palasa trees;chhitvaa= by cutting off;aamravaNam=
mango grove. durmatiH = being wicked-minded;tyaktvaa= leaving;raamam= Rama;phalaagame= at the time of arrival of fruit;shochaami= I am lamenting;pashchaat= afterwards.




11Ayodhya Kanda 63.11
लब्ध शब्देन कौसल्ये कुमारेण धनुष्मता |कुमारः शब्द वेधी इति मया पापम् इदम् कृतम्
labdha śabdena kausalye kumāreṇa dhanuṣmatā |kumāraḥ śabda vedhī iti mayā pāpam idam kṛtam
"This sin was done by me while I was young and wielding a bow. At that time, I was
famous as a young man, who can shoot heard (but unseen) object by an arrow, O Kausalya!"


Word by word
11. kausalye= O Kausalya!;mayaa= by me;labdhashabdena= who has obtained a name;kumaaraH iti= as a youth;shabdavedhii= shooting a heard;but unseen object;dhanuSmataa= (and) wielding
a bow;idam= this;paapam= sin;kR^itam= was done;kumaareNa= while I was young."




12Ayodhya Kanda 63.12
तत् इदम् मे अनुसम्प्राप्तम् देवि दुह्खम् स्वयम् कृतम् |सम्मोहात् इह बालेन यथा स्यात् भक्षितम् विषम्
tat idam me anusamprāptam devi duhkham svayam kṛtam |sammohāt iha bālena yathā syāt bhakṣitam viṣam
"This grief, obtained by my own accord, has befallen me, as by a boy in ignorance
eating poison in the world; O, Kausalya!"


Word by word
12. tatidam= such of this;duHkham= grief;svayam
kR^itam= obtained by my own accord;samanupraaptam= has befallen;me= to
me;yathaa syaat= perhaps as;viSam= a poison;bhakSitam= eaten;baalena= by a boy;sammohaat= in ignorance;iha= in this world;devi= O;Kausalya!"




13Ayodhya Kanda 63.13
यथान्यः पुरुषः कश्चित्पलाशैर्मोओहितो भवेत् |एवम् मम अपि अविज्ञातम् शब्द वेध्यमयम् फलम्
yathānyaḥ puruṣaḥ kaścitpalāśairmoohito bhavet |evam mama api avijñātam śabda vedhyamayam phalam
"How the other man became disillusioned by Palasa trees, I also became disillusioned
in the same manner, without knowing accurately the correct result of hitting a target by means of
sound only."


Word by word
13. yathaa= How;kashchit= some;anyaH= other;puruSaH= man;bhavet= became;mohitaH= disillusioned;phalaashaiH= by Palasa trees;evam= in the same manner;phalam= the
(correct) result;shabdavedhyamayam= of hitting a target by sound only;apravijJnatam= was not known accurately;mayaapi= by me also."




14Ayodhya Kanda 63.14
देव्य् अनूढा त्वम् अभवो युव राजो भवाम्य् अहम् |ततः प्रावृड् अनुप्राप्ता मद काम विवर्धिनी
devy anūḍhā tvam abhavo yuva rājo bhavāmy aham |tataḥ prāvṛḍ anuprāptā mada kāma vivardhinī
"O, Kausalya! You were unmarried till then and I was the Prince Regent. Then came
the rainy season which enhanced excitement and desire (for hunting)."


Word by word
14. devi= O;Kausalya!;tvam= you;abhavaH=
were;anuuDhaa= unmarried (till then);aham= I;bhavaami= was;yuvaraajaH= a prince Regent;tataH= then;anupraaptaa= came;praavR^iT= the rainy season;madakaama vivardhinii= which enhanced excitement
and desire (for hunting).




15Ayodhya Kanda 63.15
उपास्यहि रसान् भौमांस् तप्त्वा च जगद् अंशुभिः |परेत आचरिताम् भीमाम् रविर् आविशते दिशम्
upāsyahi rasān bhaumāṃs taptvā ca jagad aṃśubhiḥ |pareta ācaritām bhīmām ravir āviśate diśam
"The sun, partaking fluids from earth and warming the world with its rays, entered
the terrible southern quarter haunted by spirits."


Word by word
15. raviH= the Sun;upaasya= partaking;rasaan=
the fluid;bhaumaan= relating to earth;taptvaacha= and warming;jagat= the world;amshubhiH= with its rays;aavishat= entered;bhiimaam=
the terrible;disham= (southern) quarter;paretaacharitaam= haunted by
spirits.




16Ayodhya Kanda 63.16
उष्णम् अन्तर् दधे सद्यः स्निग्धा ददृशिरे घनाः |ततः जहृषिरे सर्वे भेक सारन्ग बर्हिणः
uṣṇam antar dadhe sadyaḥ snigdhā dadṛśire ghanāḥ |tataḥ jahṛṣire sarve bheka sāranga barhiṇaḥ
"Heat disappeared suddenly. Resplendent clouds appeared in the sky. All frogs,

  Dasaratha woke up with anxious thoughts. Recalling his earlier sin, he starts recounting the story of a young ascetic to Kausalya. He says that while he was Prince Regent of Ayodhya, he went out for hunting in a forest one day and heard the sound of a hermit-boy filling his pitcher with water by suberging it into Sarayu River. Mistaking the gurgling sound for trumpeting of an elephant the prince hit the boy with an arrow, which went deep into the body and mortally wounded him. On approaching the victim, he discovered the fatal blunder and tendered his heart felt apologies to the hermit boy, who asked him to extract the arrow from his body and inform his parents. The boy died soon after the arrow was drawn out from the body.

भोजयन्ति किल श्राद्धे केचित्स्वनेव बान्धवान् |ततः पश्चात्समीक्षन्ते कृतकार्या द्विजर्षभान्
bhojayanti kila śrāddhe kecitsvaneva bāndhavān |tataḥ paścātsamīkṣante kṛtakāryā dvijarṣabhān
"There are those who in a ceremony in hour of dead relatives, first feed their
relatives and thereafter, to fulfill their duty, remember to invite the illustrious Twice-born.


Word by word
12. kechit= some;shraadhhe= in a ceremony in honour of
dead relative;bhojayanti kila= indeed feed;svaan= their won;baandhavaan
iva= relatives only;kR^itakaaryaaH= having completed the ceremony;tataH
pashchaat= thereafter;samiikSante= they look for;dvijarshhabhaan= the

13Ayodhya Kanda 61.13
तत्र ये गुणवन्तश्च विद्वांसश्च द्विजातयः |न पश्चात्तेऽभिमन्यन्ते सुधामपि सुरोपमाः
tatra ye guṇavantaśca vidvāṃsaśca dvijātayaḥ |na paścātte.abhimanyante sudhāmapi suropamāḥ
"The virtuous and the learned Brahmins, who are like unto gods, do not accept
afterwards even food as delicious as ambrosia."

virtuous;vidvaamsashca= and the learned dvija tayaH = Brahmanas;suropamaaH=
who are like unto gods;te= they;na abhimanyante= do not accept;pashcaatt= afterwards;sudhaamapi= even ambrosia.




14Ayodhya Kanda 61.14
ब्राह्मणेष्वपि तृप्तेषु पश्चाद्भोक्तुम् द्विजर्षभाः |नाभ्युपैतुमलम् प्राज्ञाः शृङ्गच्चेदमिवर्ष्भाः
brāhmaṇeṣvapi tṛpteṣu paścādbhoktum dvijarṣabhāḥ |nābhyupaitumalam prājñāḥ śṛṅgaccedamivarṣbhāḥ
"The best of Brahmins in their wisdom, will not accept what remains of the food of
which other Brahmins have partaken, regarding it as a bull shorn of its horns."


Word by word
14. tR^ipteSu= the contented;braahmaNeSvapi= even if they
are Brahmanas;praaJNaaH= wise;dvijarSabhaaH= and the best of Brahmanas;naabhyupaitumalam= cannot agree;bhoktum= to eat;pashcaat=
afterwards;shR^iN^gacchedamiva= as splitting of thorns;R^iSabhaaH= of a
bull.




15Ayodhya Kanda 61.15
एवम् कनीयसा भ्रात्रा भुक्तम् राज्यम् विशाम् पते |भ्राता ज्येष्ठा वरिष्ठाः च किम् अर्थम् न अवमंस्यते
evam kanīyasā bhrātrā bhuktam rājyam viśām pate |bhrātā jyeṣṭhā variṣṭhāḥ ca kim artham na avamaṃsyate
"O, king! Why not the eldest and the best brother refuse to accept the kingdom
enjoyed by the younger brother?"


Word by word

16Ayodhya Kanda 61.16
न परेण आहृतम् भक्ष्यम् व्याघ्रः खादितुम् इच्चति |एवम् एव नर व्याघ्रः पर लीढम् न मंस्यते
na pareṇa āhṛtam bhakṣyam vyāghraḥ khāditum iccati |evam eva nara vyāghraḥ para līḍham na maṃsyate
"A tiger does not wish to share a part of food eaten by another animal. In the same
manner, Rama the tiger among men may not accept that which has been enjoyed by another."

men;na manyate= does not accept;paraliiDham= that which has been enjoyed by

17Ayodhya Kanda 61.17
हविर् आज्यम् पुरोडाशाः कुशा यूपाः च खादिराः |न एतानि यात यामानि कुर्वन्ति पुनर् अध्वरे
havir ājyam puroḍāśāḥ kuśā yūpāḥ ca khādirāḥ |na etāni yāta yāmāni kurvanti punar adhvare
"Oblations, clarified butter, leavings of an offering, sacred grass and sacrificial
posts made of trunk of Khadira tree, once used, are not put to use again in a sacrifice."

18Ayodhya Kanda 61.18
तथा हि आत्तम् इदम् राज्यम् हृत साराम् सुराम् इव |न अभिमन्तुम् अलम् रामः नष्ट सोमम् इव अध्वरम्
tathā hi āttam idam rājyam hṛta sārām surām iva |na abhimantum alam rāmaḥ naṣṭa somam iva adhvaram
"Thus, Rama cannot accept the kingdom taken away by other, as those not accepting an
ambrosia whose essence has been taken away or as in a sacrifice, stalks of Soma plant (from which a

Word by word
18. tathaa= thus;raamaH= Rama;naalam= cannot;abhimantum= accept;idam raajyam= this kingdom;attam= taken away by
others;suraamiva= as an ambrosia;hR^itasaaram= whose essence has been taken
away;adhvaramiva= and as in a sacrifice;naSTa somam= when the stalks of Soma
plant (from which a beverage called Soma is prepared) are lost.




19Ayodhya Kanda 61.19
न एवम् विधम् असत्कारम् राघवो मर्षयिष्यति |बलवान् इव शार्दूलो बालधेर् अभिमर्शनम्
na evam vidham asatkāram rāghavo marṣayiṣyati |balavān iva śārdūlo bāladher abhimarśanam
"Rama will not go through such a type of dishonour, as a strong tiger does not
endure even touching of its tail."


Word by word
19. raaghavaH= Rama;na marSayiSyati= will not go through;evam vidham= such a type;astakaaram= of dishonour;avamarshanam iva=
as touching;vaaladhe= of the tail;balavaan= by a strong;shaarduulaH= tiger.




20Ayodhya Kanda 61.20
नैतस्य सहिता लोका भयम् कुर्युर्महामृधे |अधर्मम् त्विह धर्मात्मा लोकम् धर्मेण योजयेत्
naitasya sahitā lokā bhayam kuryurmahāmṛdhe |adharmam tviha dharmātmā lokam dharmeṇa yojayet
"Even if all the worlds combine together in a great battle, they cannot stir up fear
in him. The virtuous minded Rama will provide righteousness to the people with
unrighteousness."


Word by word
20. lokaaH= even if the worlds;sahitaaH= get together;mahaa mR^idhe= in a great battle;nakuryuH= they cannot stir up;bhayam= fear;etasya= in him;dharmaatma= the virtuous minded Rama;yojayat= will provide;dharmeNa= righteousness;lokam= to people;adharmam= with unrighteousness.




21Ayodhya Kanda 61.21
नन्वसौ काञ्चनैर्बाणैर्महावीर्यो महाभुजः |युगान्त इव भूतानि सागरानपि निर्दहेत्
nanvasau kāñcanairbāṇairmahāvīryo mahābhujaḥ |yugānta iva bhūtāni sāgarānapi nirdahet
"Rama with great prowess and with his mighty arms can surely burn up all beings and
even the ocean itself by his golden arrows; like at the time of destruction of the world."


Word by word
21. asau= this Rama;mahaaviiryaH= with great prowess;mahaabhujaH= and with mighty arms;nanu nirdahet= can surely burn up;bhuutaani= all beigns;saagaraanapi= and even the ocean;kaancanaiH
baaNaiH= like at the time of destruction of the world.




22Ayodhya Kanda 61.22
स तादृशः सिम्ह बलो वृषभ अक्षो नर ऋषभः |स्वयम् एव हतः पित्रा जलजेन आत्मजो यथा
sa tādṛśaḥ simha balo vṛṣabha akṣo nara ṛṣabhaḥ |svayam eva hataḥ pitrā jalajena ātmajo yathā
"That excellent man with such a lion's strength and with eyes like those of a bull
was ruined indeed by his own father, like killing its child-fish by an adult fish."


Word by word
22. saH naraSabhaH= that excellent man;taadR^iS\shaH= of
such;simhabalaH= strength of a lion;vR^iSabhaakSaH= and with eyes like those
of a bull;hataH= was mined;pitraa iva= indeed by father;svayam= of
his own;aatmajoyathaa= like (killing) its child;jalajena= by a fish.




23Ayodhya Kanda 61.23
द्विजाति चरितः धर्मः शास्त्र दृष्टः सनातनः |यदि ते धर्म निरते त्वया पुत्रे विवासिते
dvijāti caritaḥ dharmaḥ śāstra dṛṣṭaḥ sanātanaḥ |yadi te dharma nirate tvayā putre vivāsite
"A son, who is devoted to righteousness, has been sent to exile by you. Is it a
right thing for you, as seen by scriptures or is it an eternal conduct as practiced by the Twice
born?"


Word by word
23. putre= a son;dharma nirate= who is devoted to
righteousness;nirvaasite= being sent to exile;tvayaa= by you;dharmaH

for you;sanaatanaH= or an eternal thing;dvijaaticaritaH= practised by the

24Ayodhya Kanda 61.24
गतिर् एवाक् पतिर् नार्या द्वितीया गतिर् आत्मजः |तृतीया ज्ञातयो राजमः चतुर्थी न इह विद्यते
gatir evāk patir nāryā dvitīyā gatir ātmajaḥ |tṛtīyā jñātayo rājamḥ caturthī na iha vidyate
"O, king! A husband is a chief refuge for a woman. Her second refuge is a son. The
third refuge is her near-relative. There is no fourth one here."


Word by word
24. raajan= O;king;patiH= husband;ekaa= is a
chief;gatiH= refuge;naaryaaH= for a womn;dvitiiyaa gatiH= her
second refuge;aatmajaH= is a son;tR^iiyaa= the third refuge;GYaatayH= is a near relative;na vidyate= there is no;chaturdhii=
fourth one;iha= here.




25Ayodhya Kanda 61.25
तत्र त्वम् चैव मे न अस्ति रामः च वनम् आश्रितः |न वनम् गन्तुम् इच्चामि सर्वथा हि हता त्वया
tatra tvam caiva me na asti rāmaḥ ca vanam āśritaḥ |na vanam gantum iccāmi sarvathā hi hatā tvayā
"Among those three refuges, you do not indeed exist. Rama on his part took refuge in
a forest and I do not wish to go there. Thus, I have been ruined in all ways, by you."


Word by word
25. tatra= in those three refuges;tvam= you;naiva
asi= do not indeed exist;raamastu= Rama on his part;aashritaH= took
refuge;vanam= in a forest;na icchaami= I do not wish;gantum= to
go;vanam= to the forest;nihataa= I have been mined;sarvathaa= in
all ways;tvayaa= b you.




26Ayodhya Kanda 61.26
हतम् त्वया राज्यम् इदम् सराष्ट्रम् |हतः तथा आत्मा सह मन्त्रिभिः च |हता सपुत्रा अस्मि हताः च पौराः |सुतः च भार्या च तव प्रहृष्टौ
hatam tvayā rājyam idam sarāṣṭram |hataḥ tathā ātmā saha mantribhiḥ ca |hatā saputrā asmi hatāḥ ca paurāḥ |sutaḥ ca bhāryā ca tava prahṛṣṭau
"This kingdom along with neighboring states has been ruined by you. You yourself
along with ministers have been ruined. I along with my son are ruined. Citizens too are ruined.
Your son Bharata and your wife Kaikeyi only are delighted."


Word by word
26. idam= this;raajyam= kingdom;saraaSTram=
along with neighbouring states;hatam= have been ruined;tvayaa= by you;tathaa= and;aatmaa= you yourself;mantribhiH saha= along with
ministers;hataaH= have been ruined;saputraasmi= I along with my son;hataa= are ruined;puraashcha= citizens too;hataaH= have got ruined;tavaa= your;sutashcha= son and;bhaaryaa= your wife Kaikeyi =
prahR^iSTaa = delight.




27Ayodhya Kanda 61.27
इमाम् गिरम् दारुण शब्द संश्रिताम् |निशम्य राजा अपि मुमोह दुह्खितः |ततः स शोकम् प्रविवेश पार्थिवः |स्वदुष्कृतम् च अपि पुनः तदा अस्मरत्
imām giram dāruṇa śabda saṃśritām |niśamya rājā api mumoha duhkhitaḥ |tataḥ sa śokam praviveśa pārthivaḥ |svaduṣkṛtam ca api punaḥ tadā asmarat
Hearing the aforesaid voice of Kausalya, consisting of her cruel words, the king
also being distressed, became disillusioned. Thereafter, the king then looking back on his own evil
act, was entangled in grief


Word by word
27. nishamya= hearing;imaam= this;giram=
voice;daaruNa shabda samshritaam= consisting of cruel words;raajaapi= the
king also;duhkhitaH= being distress;mumoha= became;disillusioned;tataH= thereafter;paarthivaH= the king;tadaa= then;s;ara;=
remembering;smaraH= again;svaduSkR^itam= his own evil act;pravivesha= was entangled in;shokam= grief.



    
  
  Kausalya, while weeping, rebukes Dasaratha for his evil act of sending Rama to exile. She explains various difficulties being faced by Rama, Lakshmana and Seetha in their forest-life. She says that even if Rama returns to Ayodhya in the fifteenth year, he may not accept the kingdom since enjoyed by Bharata.

  Ayodhya Kanda · Sarga 59
  Sumantra narrates the ghastly fate of Ayodhya…
  Sumantra narrates the ghastly fate of Ayodhya, both its animate and inanimate beings. Dasaratha laments and soon falls unconscious.

1Ayodhya Kanda 59.1
मम तु अश्वा निवृत्तस्य न प्रावर्तन्त वर्त्मनि |उष्णम् अश्रु विमुन्चन्तः रामे सम्प्रस्थिते वनम्
mama tu aśvā nivṛttasya na prāvartanta vartmani |uṣṇam aśru vimuncantaḥ rāme samprasthite vanam
"Rama having departed to the forest, horses on the return path however, shedding
warm tears, did not proceed further on the way."


Word by word
1.raame= Rama;samprasthite= having departed;vanam= to the forest;nivR^ittasya= the returning;ashvaaH tu=
horses;however;mama= of mine;pramuNcantaH shedding;uSNam= warm;ashru= tears;na praavartanta= did not proceed;vartmani= on the
way.




2Ayodhya Kanda 59.2
उभाभ्याम् राज पुत्राभ्याम् अथ कृत्वा अहम् ज्ञलिम् |प्रस्थितः रथम् आस्थाय तत् दुह्खम् अपि धारयन्
ubhābhyām rāja putrābhyām atha kṛtvā aham jñalim |prasthitaḥ ratham āsthāya tat duhkham api dhārayan
"I, on my part, offering salutation with joined palms to both the princes and
keeping back from that grief, ascended the chariot and moved on."


Word by word
2. atha= thereafter;aham= I;kR^itvaa= offering
(salutation);aJNjalim= with joined palms;ubhaabhyaam= to both;raaja
putraabhyaam= the princes;dhaarayan= keeping back;tat= that;duHkham api= grief;aasthaaya= ascended;ratham= the chariot;prasthitaH= and moved on.




3Ayodhya Kanda 59.3
गुहा इव सार्धम् तत्र एव स्थितः अस्मि दिवसान् बहून् |आशया यदि माम् रामः पुनः शब्दापयेद् इति
guhā iva sārdham tatra eva sthitaḥ asmi divasān bahūn |āśayā yadi mām rāmaḥ punaḥ śabdāpayed iti
"With the hope that I shall be called again by Rama, I stayed there along with Guha
for three days."


Word by word
3. aashayaa= with the hope;iti= that;shabdaapayed
dyadi= I shall be called;punaH= again;raamaH- (by) Rama;sthitaH asmi=
I stayed;tatraiva= there only;guhena saartham= along with Guha;bahuun= for many (three);divasaan= days.




4Ayodhya Kanda 59.4
विषये ते महा राज माम व्यसन कर्शिताः |अपि वृक्षाः परिम्लानः सपुष्प अन्कुर कोरकाः
viṣaye te mahā rāja māma vyasana karśitāḥ |api vṛkṣāḥ parimlānaḥ sapuṣpa ankura korakāḥ
"Oh, emperor! Even trees in your domain have withered, without giving flowers
sprouts and buds, having emaciated due to Rama's separation."


Word by word

korakaaH= without flowers;sprouts and buds;raama vyasana karshitaaH= having

5Ayodhya Kanda 59.5
उपतप्तोदका नद्यः पल्वलानि सरांसि च |परिष्कुपलाशानि वनान्युपवनानि च
upataptodakā nadyaḥ palvalāni sarāṃsi ca |pariṣkupalāśāni vanānyupavanāni ca
"Rivers, pools and lakes were with hot water. Groves and gardens were with their
leaves, parched up."

cha= and gardens;pariSkupalaashaani= were with their leaves;parched up.




6Ayodhya Kanda 59.6
न च सर्पन्ति सत्त्वानि व्याला न प्रसरन्ति च |राम शोक अभिभूतम् तन् निष्कूजम् अभवद् वनम्
na ca sarpanti sattvāni vyālā na prasaranti ca |rāma śoka abhibhūtam tan niṣkūjam abhavad vanam
"Living beings are not moving. Wild animals too are not roaming around. That forest
became silent, predominated by grief towards Rama."


Word by word
6. sattvaani= Living beings;na ca sarpanti= are not
moving;vyaalaaH ca= wild animals too;na prasaranti= are not roaming around;tat vanam= that forest;abhavad= became;niSkuujam= silent;raama
shoka abhibhuutam= predominated by grief towards Rama




7Ayodhya Kanda 59.7
लीन पुष्कर पत्राः च नर इन्द्र कलुष उदकाः |सम्तप्त पद्माः पद्मिन्यो लीन मीन विहम्गमाः
līna puṣkara patrāḥ ca nara indra kaluṣa udakāḥ |samtapta padmāḥ padminyo līna mīna vihamgamāḥ
"Oh, emperor! Lotus-lakes were with lotus-leaves hiding under water pressing
themselves closely together, with muddy waters, with parched lotus-flowers and in which fish and
water fowls have completely disappeared."

7. narendram= Oh;emperor;padminyaH= lotus-lakes (were);liina puSkara patraaH ca= with lotus-leaves hiding under water;having pressed themselves
closely together;kaluSa udakaaH= with muddy waters;samtapta padmaaH= with

8Ayodhya Kanda 59.8
जलजानि च पुष्पाणि माल्यानि स्थलजानि च |न अद्य भान्ति अल्प गन्धीनि फलानि च यथा पुरम्
jalajāni ca puṣpāṇi mālyāni sthalajāni ca |na adya bhānti alpa gandhīni phalāni ca yathā puram
"Water-born flowers and flowers living on dry lands now give very little fragrance
and fruits do not have a luscious look as before."


Word by word
8. jalajaani= water-born;puSpaaNi= flowers;maalyaani= flowers;sthalajaani= living on dry land;adya= now;alpa gandhiini= giving very little fragrance;phalaani ca= and fruits;na

1Ayodhya Kanda 57.1
कथयित्वा सुदुह्ख आर्तः सुमन्त्रेण चिरम् सह |रामे दक्षिण कूलस्थे जगाम स्व गृहम् गुहः
kathayitvā suduhkha ārtaḥ sumantreṇa ciram saha |rāme dakṣiṇa kūlasthe jagāma sva gṛham guhaḥ
While Rama landed upon the southern shore, Guha conversed for a long time with
Sumantra and with much distress, went to his house.


Word by word
1. raame= (when) Rama;dakshhiNa kuulasthe= landed upon
the southern shore;guhaH= Guha;kathayitvaa= talked;chiram= for a
long time;sumantreNa saha= with Sumantra;suduHkhaartaH= and with much
distress;jagaama= went;svagR^iham= to his house.




2Ayodhya Kanda 57.2
भरद्वाजाभिगमनम् प्रयागे च सहासनम् |आगिरेर्गमनम् तेषाम् तत्रस्थैरभिलक्षितम्
bharadvājābhigamanam prayāge ca sahāsanam |āgirergamanam teṣām tatrasthairabhilakṣitam
It was gathered by those who were there (Guha and others) about Seetha, Rama and
Lakshmana coming to sage Bharadwaja, their staying with him in Prayaga and their departure to
Chitrakuta Mountain.


Word by word
2. abhilakshhitam= It was gathered;tatrasthaiH= by those
(Guha and others) who were there;teshhaam= about their;bharadvaajaagamanam=
coming to sage Bharadwaja;sahaasanam= about staying with him;prayaage= in
Prayaga;gamanam= and about their going;agire= to Chitrakuta mountain.




3Ayodhya Kanda 57.3
अनुज्ञातः सुमन्त्रः अथ योजयित्वा हय उत्तमान् |अयोध्याम् एव नगरीम् प्रययौ गाढ दुर्मनाः
anujñātaḥ sumantraḥ atha yojayitvā haya uttamān |ayodhyām eva nagarīm prayayau gāḍha durmanāḥ
Sumantra, being allowed to depart by Rama, tied excellent horses to the chariot and
with intense anguish, rode towards the very city of Ayodhya.


Word by word
3. atha= then;sumantraH= Sumantra;anuGYaataH=
allowed to depart by Rama;yojayitvaa= tied;haya uttamaan= the excellent
horses (to the chariot);gaaDha durmanaaH= and with intense anguish;prayayau=
rode towards;ayodhyaam nagariim eva= the very city of Ayodhya.




4Ayodhya Kanda 57.4
स वनानि सुगन्धीनि सरितः च सरांसि च |पश्यन्न् अतिययौ शीघ्रम् ग्रामाणि नगराणि च
sa vanāni sugandhīni saritaḥ ca sarāṃsi ca |paśyann atiyayau śīghram grāmāṇi nagarāṇi ca
Sumantra, seeing the sweet-smelling woods, rivers, lakes, villages and towns on the
way, soon crossed them.


Word by word
4. saH= He;pashyan= seeing;sugandhiini= the
sweet smelling vanaani = woods;saritaH cha= rivers;saraamsi cha= lakes;graamaaNi= villages;nagaraaNi= (and) towns;atiyayau= crossed (them)
shiighram = quickly.




5Ayodhya Kanda 57.5
ततः साय अह्न समये तृतीये अहनि सारथिः |अयोध्याम् समनुप्राप्य निरानन्दाम् ददर्श ह
tataḥ sāya ahna samaye tṛtīye ahani sārathiḥ |ayodhyām samanuprāpya nirānandām dadarśa ha
Reaching Ayodhya in the evening time of the third day Sumantra saw that city,
joyless.


Word by word
5. tataH= thereafter;samanupraapya= reaching;ayodhyaam= Ayodhya;saaya ahna samaye= in the evening-time;tR^itiiye
ahani= of the third day;saarathiH= the charioteer;dadarsha ha= saw
(it);niraanandaam= joyless.




6Ayodhya Kanda 57.6
स शून्याम् इव निह्शब्दाम् दृष्ट्वा परम दुर्मनाः |सुमन्त्रः चिन्तयाम् आस शोक वेग समाहतः
sa śūnyām iva nihśabdām dṛṣṭvā parama durmanāḥ |sumantraḥ cintayām āsa śoka vega samāhataḥ
Beholding Ayodhya as if deserted in silence, Sumantra becoming very much distressed
in mind and having afflicted with intense anguish, surmised as follows:


Word by word
6. dR^ishhTvaa= beholding;shuunyaam iva= Ayodhya as
deserted;nishshabdaam= in silence;sumantraH= Sumantra;parama
durmanaaH= becoming very much distressed in mind;shoka vega samaahataH= and having
afflicted with intense anguish;chintayaamaasa= surmised (as follows).




7Ayodhya Kanda 57.7
कच्चिन् न सगजा साश्वा सजना सजन अधिपा |राम सम्ताप दुह्खेन दग्धा शोक अग्निना पुरी
kaccin na sagajā sāśvā sajanā sajana adhipā |rāma samtāpa duhkhena dagdhā śoka agninā purī
"I hope the city of Ayodhya with its elephants, horses, people and the kings was not
burnt away by a fire of sorrow and blazing grief towards Rama.


Word by word
7. purii kaccin na= was not the city;sagajaa= with
elephants;saashvaa= with horses;sajanaa= with people;sajana adhipaa= and with kings;dagdhaa= burnt away;raama samtaapa duHkhena= by blazing
grief towards Rama;shoka agninaa= and the fire of sorrow?




8Ayodhya Kanda 57.8
इति चिन्ता परः सूतः वाजिभिः श्रीघ्रपातिभिः |नगरद्वारमासाद्य त्वरितः प्रविवेश ह
iti cintā paraḥ sūtaḥ vājibhiḥ śrīghrapātibhiḥ |nagaradvāramāsādya tvaritaḥ praviveśa ha
Sumantra, thus lost in thought, reaching the city-gate through the fast-running
horses, entered the city quickly.


Word by word
8. suutaH= the charioteer;iti= thus;cintaa
paraH= lost in thought;aasaadya= reaching;nagaradvaaram= the city-gate;shiighrapaatibhiH= by the fast-running;vaajibhiH= horses;praviveshaha= entered (the city) tvaritaaH = quickly.




9Ayodhya Kanda 57.9
सुमन्त्रम् अभियान्तम् तम् शतशो अथ सहस्रशः |क्व रामैति पृच्चन्तः सूतम् अभ्यद्रवन् नराः
sumantram abhiyāntam tam śataśo atha sahasraśaḥ |kva rāmaiti pṛccantaḥ sūtam abhyadravan narāḥ
Meanwhile, seeing Sumantra the charioteer approaching, hundreds and thousands of
people ran towards him asking, "Where is Rama?"


Word by word
9. atha= thereafter;(seeing) tam= that;sumantram= Sumantra;suutam= the charioteer;abhiyaantam=
approaching;shatashaH= hundreds;sahasrashaH= and thousands;naraaH=
of people;abhyadravan= ran towards him;pR^icchantaH= asking;iti=
thus;kva= where is;raamaH= Rama?




10Ayodhya Kanda 57.10
तेषाम् शशंस गङ्गायाम् अहम् आपृच्च्य राघवम् |अनुज्ञातः निवृत्तः अस्मि धार्मिकेण महात्मना
teṣām śaśaṃsa gaṅgāyām aham āpṛccya rāghavam |anujñātaḥ nivṛttaḥ asmi dhārmikeṇa mahātmanā
He replied them thus: "Bidding farewell to Rama at the shore of Ganga when sent back
by that virtuous and high-souled Rama, I returned here."


Word by word
10. shashamsa= he replied;teshhaam= them;aapR^ichchhya= bidding farewell;raaghavam= to Rama;gaN^gaayaam= (at
the shore) of Ganga;anuj~NaataH= when sent back;dhaarmikeNa= by that
virtuous;mahaatmanaH= and high-souled Rama;aham= I;nivR^ittaH asmi= returned.




11Ayodhya Kanda 57.11
ते तीर्णाइति विज्ञाय बाष्प पूर्ण मुखा जनाः |अहो धिग् इति निश्श्वस्य हा राम इति च चुक्रुशुः
te tīrṇāiti vijñāya bāṣpa pūrṇa mukhā janāḥ |aho dhig iti niśśvasya hā rāma iti ca cukruśuḥ
Hearing that Seetha, Rama and Lakshmana had crossed River Ganga, the people with
their faces filled with tears sighed, "Oh, fie upon us! And cried aloud, "Alas, Rama!"


Word by word
11. vij~Naaya= knowing;te= (that) Seetha Rama and
Lakshmana;tiirNaaH iti= had crossed (Ganga);janaH= the people;baashhpapuurNamukhaaH= with their faces filled with tears;nishshvasya= sighed;iti= thus;aho= Oh;dhik= fie upon us! cukrushuH cha = and cried
aloud;haa raama iti= thus = "Alas! Rama!




12Ayodhya Kanda 57.12
शुश्राव च वचः तेषाम् बृन्दम् बृन्दम् च तिष्ठताम् |हताः स्म खलु ये न इह पश्यामैति राघवम्
śuśrāva ca vacaḥ teṣām bṛndam bṛndam ca tiṣṭhatām |hatāḥ sma khalu ye na iha paśyāmaiti rāghavam
Sumantra also heard the words of those people standing in groups and telling, "Lost
indeed are we, who do not see Rama here!"


Word by word
12. shushraava cha= (Sumantra) also heard;vachaH= words;teshhaam= of those people;tiSThataam= standing;bR^indam bR^idam= in
groups;iti= and telling thus;hataaH sma khalu= lost indeed are we;ye= who;na pashyaamaH= do not see;raaghavam= Rama;iha=
here!




13Ayodhya Kanda 57.13
दान यज्ञ विवाहेषु समाजेषु महत्सु च |न द्रक्ष्यामः पुनर् जातु धार्मिकम् रामम् अन्तरा
dāna yajña vivāheṣu samājeṣu mahatsu ca |na drakṣyāmaḥ punar jātu dhārmikam rāmam antarā
"Never again can we see the pious Rama on the occasions of bestowing gifts,
sacrificial performances or marriages or in large meetings.


Word by word
13. najaatu= never;punaH= again;drakshhyaamaH=
we can see;dhaarmikam= the pious;raamam= Rama;antaraa= on the
occasions of;daana yaGYa vivaaheSu= bestowing gifts;sacrificial performances and
marriages;mahatsu= large;samaajeshhu cha= meetings.




14Ayodhya Kanda 57.14
किम् समर्थम् जनस्य अस्य किम् प्रियम् किम् सुख आवहम् |इति रामेण नगरम् पितृवत् परिपालितम्
kim samartham janasya asya kim priyam kim sukha āvaham |iti rāmeṇa nagaram pitṛvat paripālitam
The city of Ayodhya was protected by Rama, as by a father, with due regard to what
was appropriate, what was congenial and what brought happiness to its people.


Word by word
14. nagaram= the city of Ayodhya;paripaalitam= was
protected;raameNa= by Rama;pitR^ivat= as by a father;iti= in this
manner;kim= what was;samartham= appropriate;asya janasya= to these
people;kim= what was;priyam= congenial;kim= what;sukhaavaham= brought happiness.




15Ayodhya Kanda 57.15
वात अयन गतानाम् च स्त्रीणाम् अन्वन्तर आपणम् |राम शोक अभितप्तानाम् शुश्राव परिदेवनम्
vāta ayana gatānām ca strīṇām anvantara āpaṇam |rāma śoka abhitaptānām śuśrāva paridevanam
While driving through bazaars, Sumantra heard the sounds of lamentation of women,
coming forth from windows, consumed by anguish on account of Rama's exile.


Word by word
15. anvantara aapaNam= while driving through bazaars;shushraava= (Sumantra) hard;paridevanam= the lamentation;striiNaam=
of women;vaata ayana gataanaam= coming forth from windows;raama shoka
abhitaptaanaam= consumed by anguish on account of Rama's exile.




16Ayodhya Kanda 57.16
स राज मार्ग मध्येन सुमन्त्रः पिहित आननः |यत्र राजा दशरथः तत् एव उपययौ गृहम्
sa rāja mārga madhyena sumantraḥ pihita ānanaḥ |yatra rājā daśarathaḥ tat eva upayayau gṛham
Going through the middle of the royal highway, Sumantra by covering his face,
reached the house of Dasaratha.


Word by word
16. saH sumantraH= That Sumantra;pihita aananaH= by
covering his face;upayayau= reached;tat= that;gR^iham eva= house;yatra= where;raajaa= king;dasharathaH= Dasaratha (was there);raaja maarga madhyena= going through the middle of the royal highway.




17Ayodhya Kanda 57.17
सो अवतीर्य रथात् शीघ्रम् राज वेश्म प्रविश्य च |कक्ष्याः सप्त अभिचक्राम महा जन समाकुलाः
so avatīrya rathāt śīghram rāja veśma praviśya ca |kakṣyāḥ sapta abhicakrāma mahā jana samākulāḥ
Sumantra descended from the chariot, entered quickly the royal palace and traversed
the seven inner apartments of the palace, filled with a large number of people.


Word by word
17. saH= He;avatiirya= descended;rathaat= from
the chariot;pravishya cha= entered;shiighram= quickly;raaja veshma= the royal palace;abhicakraama= and traversed;sapta= the seven;kakSyaaH= inner apartments of the palace;mahaa jana samaakulaaH= filled with a
large number of people.




18Ayodhya Kanda 57.18
हर्म्यैर्विमानैः प्रासादैरवेक्ष्याथ समागतम् |हाहाकारकृता नार्यो रामदर्शनकर्शिताः
harmyairvimānaiḥ prāsādairavekṣyātha samāgatam |hāhākārakṛtā nāryo rāmadarśanakarśitāḥ
Then, finding the forthcoming Sumantra from their large mansions, from seven-storied
buildings and from royal palaces, the women who had been emaciated in not being able to see Rama,
cried "Alas! Alas".


Word by word
18. atha= then;avekshhya= seeing;samaagatam=
(Sumantra) coming;naaryaH= the women;harmaiH= from large mansions;vimaanaiH= from seven-storied buildings;praasaadaiH= and from royal palaces;raamadarshanakarshitaaH= who had been emaciated in not seeing Rama;haahaakaarakR^itaH= cried "Alas! Alas"




19Ayodhya Kanda 57.19
आयतैर्विमलैर्नेत्रैरश्रुवेगपरिप्लुतैः |अन्योन्यमभिवीक्षन्तेऽव्यक्तमार्ततराः स्त्रीयः
āyatairvimalairnetrairaśruvegapariplutaiḥ |anyonyamabhivīkṣante.avyaktamārtatarāḥ strīyaḥ
Those women, extremely confounded with grief with their long and bright eyes filled
with a stream of tears, looked at each other imperceptibly.


Word by word
19. striyaH= the women;aartataraaH= extremely confounded
with grief;netraiH= with eyes;aayataiH= bright;ashruvegapariplutaiH= filled with a stream of tears;abhiviikshhante= looked at;anyoyam= each
other;avyaktam= imperceptibly.




20Ayodhya Kanda 57.20
ततः दशरथ स्त्रीणाम् प्रासादेभ्यः ततः ततः |राम शोक अभितप्तानाम् मन्दम् शुश्राव जल्पितम्
tataḥ daśaratha strīṇām prāsādebhyaḥ tataḥ tataḥ |rāma śoka abhitaptānām mandam śuśrāva jalpitam
Sumantra also heard the feeble conversation of Dasaratha's wives absorbed in anguish
on account of Rama's exile, from their respective inner apartments.


Word by word
20. tataH= then;shushraava= (Sumantra) heard;mandam= the feeble;jalpitam= conversation;Dasharatha striiNaam= of
Dasaratha's wives;raama shoka abhitaptaanam= absorbed of anguish on account of Rama's
exile;tataH tatatH= from their respective;praasaadebhyaH= inner
apartments.




21Ayodhya Kanda 57.21
सह रामेण निर्यातः विना रामम् इह आगतः |सूतः किम् नाम कौसल्याम् शोचन्तीम् प्रति वक्ष्यति
saha rāmeṇa niryātaḥ vinā rāmam iha āgataḥ |sūtaḥ kim nāma kausalyām śocantīm prati vakṣyati
"What Sumantra will reply to the lamenting Kausalya, when he now returns here
without Rama while he formerly went out with Rama?"


Word by word
21. kim naama= what;suutaH= Sumantra;prati
vakshhyati= will reply;kausalyaam= to Kausalya;shocantiim= who is
lamenting;niryaataH= (when he) went out;raameNa saha= with Rama;aagataH= and returned;iha= here;vinaa raamam= without Rama?




22Ayodhya Kanda 57.22
यथा च मन्ये दुर्जीवम् एवम् न सुकरम् ध्रुवम् |आच्चिद्य पुत्रे निर्याते कौसल्या यत्र जीवति
yathā ca manye durjīvam evam na sukaram dhruvam |āccidya putre niryāte kausalyā yatra jīvati
"In spite of her son (Rama) having left Ayodhya, Kausalya continues to survive. I
think that surely it is difficult thus to live and it is not so easy to preserve it too!"


Word by word
22. yathaa= In which manner;kausalyaa= Kausalya;yatra jiivati= survives wherever;aachchhidya= in spite of;putre=
her son (Rama);niryaate= having left;manye= I think that;dhruvam=
surely;na= it is not;sukaram= easy;evam= thus;durjiivitam= a difficult living.




23Ayodhya Kanda 57.23
सत्य रूपम् तु तत् वाक्यम् राज्ञः स्त्रीणाम् निशामयन् |प्रदीप्तम् इव शोकेन विवेश सहसा गृहम्
satya rūpam tu tat vākyam rājñaḥ strīṇām niśāmayan |pradīptam iva śokena viveśa sahasā gṛham
Hearing those credible words of Dasaratha's wives, Sumantra all at once entered the
house, that appeared to be set ablaze with grief.


Word by word
23. nishaamayan= reaching to;tat vaakyam= those words;satya ruupam= so credible;raaGYaH= of king Dasaratha's;striiNaam=
wives;sahasaa= (Sumantra) quickly;vivesha= entered;gR^iham= the
house;pradiiptim iva= appeared like burning;shokena= with grief.




24Ayodhya Kanda 57.24
स प्रविश्य अष्टमीम् कक्ष्याम् राजानम् दीनम् आतुलम् |पुत्र शोक परिम्लानम् अपश्यत् पाण्डुरे गृहे
sa praviśya aṣṭamīm kakṣyām rājānam dīnam ātulam |putra śoka parimlānam apaśyat pāṇḍure gṛhe
Sumantra entered the eighth inner apartment and saw in that white house, King
Dasaratha the miserable the sick and the exhausted man on account of the exhausted man on account
of the grief for his son.


Word by word
24. saH= that Sumantra;pravishya= entered;aSTamiim= the eighth;kakSyaam= inner apartment;apashyat= (and) saw;raajaanam= king Dasaratha;diinaam= the miserable;aatulam= the sick;putra shoka parimlaanam= and the exhausted man;due to grief for his son;paaNDure= in that white;gR^ihe= house.




25Ayodhya Kanda 57.25
अभिगम्य तम् आसीनम् नर इन्द्रम् अभिवाद्य च |सुमन्त्रः राम वचनम् यथा उक्तम् प्रत्यवेदयत्
abhigamya tam āsīnam nara indram abhivādya ca |sumantraḥ rāma vacanam yathā uktam pratyavedayat
Sumantra approached that king who was seated, offered his salutation and presented
Rama's message as told.


Word by word
25. sumantraH= Sumantra;abhigamya= approached;tam
narendram= the distressed king;aasiinam= who was seated;abhivaadya cha=
offered his salutation;pratyavedayat= and presented;raamavachanam= Rama's
message;yathoktam= as told.




26Ayodhya Kanda 57.26
स तूष्णीम् एव तत् श्रुत्वा राजा विभ्रान्त चेतनः |मूर्चितः न्यपतत् भूमौ राम शोक अभिपीडितः
sa tūṣṇīm eva tat śrutvā rājā vibhrānta cetanaḥ |mūrcitaḥ nyapatat bhūmau rāma śoka abhipīḍitaḥ
That king heard silently the message of Rama, was bewildered, afflicted by grief,
for his son, became fainted and fell on the ground.


Word by word
26. saH raajaa= that king;shrutvaa= heard;tuushhNiim
eva= silently;tat= that message of Rama;vibhraanta chetasaH= was
afflicted by grief for his son;muurchitaH= became fainted;nyapatat= and fell;bhuumau= on the ground.




27Ayodhya Kanda 57.27
ततः अन्तः पुरम् आविद्धम् मूर्चिते पृथिवी पतौ |उद्धृत्य बाहू चुक्रोश नृपतौ पतिते क्षितौ
tataḥ antaḥ puram āviddham mūrcite pṛthivī patau |uddhṛtya bāhū cukrośa nṛpatau patite kṣitau
The king thus having fainted, the gynaeceum was hurt. While the king was falling on
the ground, the inmates of gynaeceum wept, raising their hands in distress.

28Ayodhya Kanda 57.28
सुमित्रया तु सहिता कौसल्या पतितम् पतिम् |उत्थापयाम् आस तदा वचनम् च इदम् अब्रवीत्
sumitrayā tu sahitā kausalyā patitam patim |utthāpayām āsa tadā vacanam ca idam abravīt

Kausalya also spoke these words to Dasaratha.

29Ayodhya Kanda 57.29
इमम् तस्य महा भाग दूतम् दुष्कर कारिणः |वन वासात् अनुप्राप्तम् कस्मान् न प्रतिभाषसे

30Ayodhya Kanda 57.30
अद्य इमम् अनयम् कृत्वा व्यपत्रपसि राघव |उत्तिष्ठ सुकृतम् ते अस्तु शोके न स्यात् सहायता

"Oh, Dasaratha! After doing an evil act, you are now feeling shameful. Rise up! Let

31Ayodhya Kanda 57.31

deva yasyā bhayāt rāmam na anupṛccasi sārathim |na iha tiṣṭhati kaikeyī viśrabdham pratibhāṣyatām
"Oh, king! On whose fear, you are not enquiring with Sumantra about the welfare of
Rama, that Kaikeyi is not here. Speak fearlessly."

32Ayodhya Kanda 57.32
सा तथा उक्त्वा महा राजम् कौसल्या शोक लालसा |धरण्याम् निपपात आशु बाष्प विप्लुत भाषिणी
sā tathā uktvā mahā rājam kausalyā śoka lālasā |dharaṇyām nipapāta āśu bāṣpa vipluta bhāṣiṇī
Kausalya, speaking excitedly in tears and entirely given up to anguish uttered thus
to the monarch and soon fell to the ground.

33Ayodhya Kanda 57.33
एवम् विलपतीम् दृष्ट्वा कौसल्याम् पतिताम् भुवि |पतिम् च अवेक्ष्य ताः सर्वाः सुस्वरम् रुरुदुः स्त्रियः
evam vilapatīm dṛṣṭvā kausalyām patitām bhuvi |patim ca avekṣya tāḥ sarvāḥ susvaram ruruduḥ striyaḥ
All those women cried in loud voice, seeing Kausalya fallen on the ground weeping as
aforesaid and gazing their husband too (lying unconscious).

34Ayodhya Kanda 57.34
ततः तम् अन्तः पुर नादम् उत्थितम् |समीक्ष्य वृद्धाः तरुणाः च मानवाः |स्त्रियः च सर्वा रुरुदुः समन्ततः |पुरम् तदा आसीत् पुनर् एव सम्कुलम्
tataḥ tam antaḥ pura nādam utthitam |samīkṣya vṛddhāḥ taruṇāḥ ca mānavāḥ |striyaḥ ca sarvā ruruduḥ samantataḥ |puram tadā āsīt punar eva samkulam
Hearing that crying sound raised in gynaeceum, all aged and young men and women on
all sides gathered around weeping. The city then again became disturbed.


Word by word

that;antaH pura naadam= noise in gynaeceum;maanavaaH= persons;vR^iddhaaH= aged;taruNaaH cha= and young;sarvaaH= all;striyaH
cha= the women;samantataH= on all sides;ruruduH= cried;tadaa= then;puram= the city;punar eva= again;aasiit= became;samkulam= agitated.



    
  
  Sumantra takes leave from Guha, who learns from his spies that Rama departed for Chitrakuta. Sumantra drives back to Ayodhya. Entering the royal gynaeceum, he submits to the emperor what he earlier reported to the citizens who followed his chariot. Dasaratha and Kausalya fall into a faint to hear about Rama's departure for Chitrakuta. All the inmates of gynaeceum weep loudly in anguish.

1Ayodhya Kanda 55.1
उषित्वा रजनीम् तत्र राजपुत्रावरिंदमौ |महर्षिमभिवाद्याथ जग्मतुस्तम् गिरिम् प्रति
uṣitvā rajanīm tatra rājaputrāvariṃdamau |maharṣimabhivādyātha jagmatustam girim prati
Having stayed that night there, those princes the annihilators of enemies,
thereafter offered salutation to the sage Bharadwaja and proceeded towards that mountain of
Chitrakuta.


Word by word

2Ayodhya Kanda 55.2
तेषाम् चैव स्वस्त्ययनम् महर्षिः स चकार ह |प्रस्थितांश्चैव तान् प्रेक्ष्यपिता पुत्रानिवान्वगात्
teṣām caiva svastyayanam maharṣiḥ sa cakāra ha |prasthitāṃścaiva tān prekṣyapitā putrānivānvagāt
That great sage Bharadwaja performed a religious rite ensuring a sage journey
(scattering boiled rice on the ground and invoking blessing through the repetition of certain
sacred texts0 for them. Perceiving them setting out for the journey, the sage accompanied them for
a distance, as a father would do for his sons (and daughter-in-law).

3Ayodhya Kanda 55.3
ततः प्रचक्रमे वक्तुम् वचनम् स महामुनिः |भर्द्वाजो महातेजा रामम् सत्यपराक्रमम्
tataḥ pracakrame vaktum vacanam sa mahāmuniḥ |bhardvājo mahātejā rāmam satyaparākramam
Bharadwaja the great sage with a remarkable splendour began to speak the following
words to Rama the truly brave man.

4Ayodhya Kanda 55.4
गङ्गायमुनयोः सन्धिमासाद्य मनुजर्षभौ |काळिन्दीमनुगच्छेताम् नदीम् पश्चान्मुखाश्रिताम्
gaṅgāyamunayoḥ sandhimāsādya manujarṣabhau |kāldindīmanugacchetām nadīm paścānmukhāśritām
"After approaching Oh, the best of men! The confluence of Ganga and Yamuna, follow
the river Yamuna which takes to the direction of west."

5Ayodhya Kanda 55.5
अथासाद्य तु काळिन्न्धीम् शीघ्रस्रोतसमापगाम् |तस्यास्तीर्थम् प्रचरितम् पुराणम् प्रेक्ष्य राघवौतत्र यूयम् प्लवम् कृत्वा तरतांशुमतीम् नदीम्
athāsādya tu kāldinndhīm śīghrasrotasamāpagām |tasyāstīrtham pracaritam purāṇam prekṣya rāghavautatra yūyam plavam kṛtvā taratāṃśumatīm nadīm
"Reaching the River Yamuna belonging to olden times, having a rapid stream and
perceiving in it a passage for descent into the river, which is too much frequented the river,
which is too much frequented, you cross the River Yamuna (the daughter of the sun-god) by preparing
a raft there, Oh Rama!"

the River;kaaLindiim= Yamuna;puraaNam= belonging to olden times;shiighra

6Ayodhya Kanda 55.6
ततो न्यग्रोधमासाद्य महान्तम् हरितच्छदम्
tato nyagrodhamāsādya mahāntam haritacchadam
After crossing the river Yamuna and approaching a large banyan tree named Syama
(dark-green) having green leaves surrounded by many tress and visited by Siddhas, Seetha should,
joining her palms, recite her auspicious prayers to the tree."

recite;shivaaH= auspicious;aashishhaH= prayers;tasmai= to the

7Ayodhya Kanda 55.7
विवृद्धम् बहुभिर्वऋक्षैह् श्यामम् सिद्धोपसेवितम् |तस्मै सीताञ्जलिम् कृत्वा प्रयुञ्जीताशिषः शिवाः
vivṛddham bahubhirvaṛkṣaih śyāmam siddhopasevitam |tasmai sītāñjalim kṛtvā prayuñjītāśiṣaḥ śivāḥ

8Ayodhya Kanda 55.8
समासाद्य तु तम् वृक्षम् वसेद्वातिक्रमेत वा |क्रोशमात्रम् ततो गत्वा नीलम् द्रक्ष्यथ काननम्पलाशबदरीमिश्रम् रम्यम् वंशैश्च यामुनैः
samāsādya tu tam vṛkṣam vasedvātikrameta vā |krośamātram tato gatvā nīlam drakṣyatha kānanampalāśabadarīmiśram ramyam vaṃśaiśca yāmunaiḥ
"Having approached that tree, you can stay there or go beyond it. After going only
for two miles from there, you will see a beautiful forest blue in colour with bamboo trees touching
upon Yamuna river and interspersed with Sallaka and jujube trees."

forest;niilam= blue in colour;vamshaiH cha= with bamboo trees;yaamunaiH= touching upon Yamuna river;palaashabadariimishram= interspersed

9Ayodhya Kanda 55.9
स पन्थाश्चित्रकूटस्य गतः सुबहुशो मयारम्ये मार्दवयुक्तश्च वनदावैर्विपर्जितः
sa panthāścitrakūṭasya gataḥ subahuśo mayāramye mārdavayuktaśca vanadāvairviparjitaḥ
"It is the way to Chitrakuta. I visited that place many times. It is beautiful,
endowed with serenity and free from forest-fire."

10Ayodhya Kanda 55.10
इति पन्थानमावेद्य महर्षः स न्यवर्ततअभिवाद्य तथेत्युक्त्वा रामेण विनिवर्तितः
iti panthānamāvedya maharṣḥ sa nyavartataabhivādya tathetyuktvā rāmeṇa vinivartitaḥ
Having thus informed the way and ebbing urged by Rama to return after he had paid
obeisance to the sage and Rama having replied �so be it', the great sage Bharadwaja returned.

11Ayodhya Kanda 55.11
उपावृत्ते मुनौ तस्मिन् रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्कृतपुण्याः स्म सौमित्रे मुनिर्यन्नोऽनुकम्पते

That sage having returned, Rama spoke to Lakshmana as follows: "Oh Lakshmana! We are
fortunate that the sage has shown compassion towards us."

12Ayodhya Kanda 55.12
इति तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ मन्त्रयित्वा मनस्विनौसीतामेवाग्रतः कृत्वा काळिन्दीम् जग्मतुर्नदीम्
iti tau puruṣavyāghrau mantrayitvā manasvinausītāmevāgrataḥ kṛtvā kāldindīm jagmaturnadīm
Deliberating thus, Rama and Lakshmana the tigers among men who were highly
intelligent, headed for the river Yamuna guarding Seetha still in front.

those;purushhavyaaghrau= tigers among men;manasvinau= who were highly wise;jagmatuH= headed for;kaaLindiim= the river Yamuna;kR^itvaa=

13Ayodhya Kanda 55.13
अथा साद्य तु काळिन्दीम् शीघ्रस्रोतोवहाम् नदीम्चिन्तामापेदिरे सर्वे नदीजलतितीर्षवः
athā sādya tu kāldindīm śīghrasrotovahām nadīmcintāmāpedire sarve nadījalatitīrṣavaḥ
Having reached the River Yamuna, running with rapid stream, all of them then plunged
into a thought of how to cross those river-waters.

14Ayodhya Kanda 55.14
तौ काष्ठसम्घातमथो चक्रतुस्तु महाप्लवम्शुष्कैर्वंशैः समास्तीर्णमुळीरैश्च समावृतम्

Then, Rama and Lakshmana prepared a big raft with pieces of timber fastened
together, covered with a kind of grass and spread over with dry bamboo canes.

ततो वेतसशाखाश्च जम्बूशाखाश्च वीर्यवान्चकार लक्ष्मणश्छित्वा सीतायाः सुखमासनम्
tato vetasaśākhāśca jambūśākhāśca vīryavāncakāra lakṣmaṇaśchitvā sītāyāḥ sukhamāsanam
Thereafter, the valiant Lakshmana made for Seetha a comfortable seat, after chopping
branches of reeds and of rose apple tree.

tatra śriyamivācintyām rāmo dāśarathiḥ priyāmīṣtsankahhanābān tānagtārioatat plavam
Then Rama the son of Dasaratha helped Seetha his beloved consort who was
unimaginable like the goddess of fortune and who was feeling shy a little- to mount the raft.


Word by word

आरोप्य प्रथमम् सीताम् सम्घाटम् प्रतिगृह्य तौततः प्रतेरतुर्य त्तौ वीरौ दशरथात्मजौ

taraami= I am crossing;tvaam= you;svasti= Adieu! Me = (May) my;patiH= husband;paarayet= complete;vratam= his vow;raame=

21Ayodhya Kanda 55.21
काळिन्दीमथ सीता तु याचमाना कृताञ्जलिःतीरमेवाभिसम्प्राप्ता दक्षिणम् वरवर्णिनी
kāldindīmatha sītā tu yācamānā kṛtāñjaliḥtīramevābhisamprāptā dakṣiṇam varavarṇinī
Seetha of excellent complexion thus praying with joined palms to Yamuna River,

Word by word

ततः प्लवेनांशुमतीम् शीघ्रगामूर्मिमालिनीम्तीरजैर्बहुभिर्वृक्षैः सम्तेरुर्यमुनाम् नदीम्
tataḥ plavenāṃśumatīm śīghragāmūrmimālinīmtīrajairbahubhirvṛkṣaiḥ samteruryamunām nadīm

nygrodham tamupāgamya vaidehi vākyamabravīt

banyan tree;vaidehii= Seetha;abraviit= spoke;vaakyam= these words;mahaavR^ikshha= "Oh;great tree! Me patiH= let my husband;paarayet=
complete;vratam= his vow! pashyeyam = let me see again;kausalyaam cha=
Kausalya and;yashasviniim= the illustrious;sumitraam cha= Sumitra;siitaa= Seetha;iti= thus speaking;paryagachchhat= circumambulated;vanaspatim= that tree;aJNjalim kR^itvaa= with joined palms.

नमस्तेऽन्तु महावृक्ष पारयेन्मे पतिर्वतम् |कौसल्याम् चैव पश्येयम् सुमित्राम् च यशस्विनीम्इति सीताञ्जलिम् कृत्वा पर्यगच्छद्वनस्पतिम्
namaste.antu mahāvṛkṣa pārayenme patirvatam |kausalyām caiva paśyeyam sumitrām ca yaśasvinīmiti sītāñjalim kṛtvā paryagacchadvanaspatim
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


26Ayodhya Kanda 55.26
अवलोक्य ततः सीतामायाचन्तीमनिन्दिताम्दयिताम् च विधेयम् च रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्
avalokya tataḥ sītāmāyācantīmaninditāmdayitām ca vidheyam ca rāmo lakṣmaṇamabravīt
Seeing the irreproachable Seetha, who was beloved and obedient to him thus praying,
Rama spoke to Lakshmana as follows:


Word by word
26. tataH= then;raamaH= Rama;avalokya= seeing;siitaam= Seetha;ayaachantiim= who was thus praying;aninditaam= who
was beloved;vidheyaameha= and who was obedient;abraviit= spoke;lakshhmaNam= to Lakshmana.




27Ayodhya Kanda 55.27
सीतामादाय गच्छ त्वमग्रतो भरतानुजपृष्ठतोऽहम् गमिष्यामि सायुधो द्विपदाम् वर
sītāmādāya gaccha tvamagrato bharatānujapṛṣṭhato.aham gamiṣyāmi sāyudho dvipadām vara
"Oh, Lakshmana, the excellent of men! You take Seetha and proceed in the front. I,
along with weapons, will follow you behind."


Word by word
27. bharatanuja= "Oh;Lakshmana;vara= the best;dvipadaam= among men! Tvam = you;aadaaya= take;siitaam= Seetha;gachchha= and proceed;agrataH= in front;aham= I;saayudhaH= along with weapons;gamishhyaami= will move;pR^ishhTataH= behind."




28Ayodhya Kanda 55.28
यद्यत्फलम् प्रार्थयते पुष्पम् वा जनकात्मजातत्तत्प्रदद्या वैदेह्या यत्रास्य रमते मनः
yadyatphalam prārthayate puṣpam vā janakātmajātattatpradadyā vaidehyā yatrāsya ramate manaḥ
"Give to Seetha whatever fruit or flower she desires it and wherever this Seetha's
mind finds delight."

गच्चतोस्तु तयोर्मध्ये बभूव जनकात्मजामातङ्गयोर्मद्यगता शुभा नागवधूरिव
gaccatostu tayormadhye babhūva janakātmajāmātaṅgayormadyagatā śubhā nāgavadhūriva
Seetha who was walking in the middle of both of them was like an auspicious female
elephant in the middle of two elephants.

29. janakaatmajaa= Seetha;gachchhate= who was walking;madhyagataa= in the middle;taayoH= of both of them;babhuuva= was;shubhaa naaga vadhuuriva= like an auspicious female elephant;madhyagataa= in

30Ayodhya Kanda 55.30
एकैकम् पादपम् गुल्मम् लताम् वा पुष्पशालिनीम्अदृष्टपूर्वाम् पश्यन्ती रामम् पप्रच्छ साऽबला
ekaikam pādapam gulmam latām vā puṣpaśālinīmadṛṣṭapūrvām paśyantī rāmam papraccha sā.abalā
That Seetha asked Rama whenever she saw the one or the other tree or a bush or a
creeper shining with flowers which was not seen earlier.

earlier.




31Ayodhya Kanda 55.31
रमणीयान् बहुविधान् पादपान् कुसुमोत्कटान्सीतावचनसम्रब्द अनयामास लक्स्मणः
ramaṇīyān bahuvidhān pādapān kusumotkaṭānsītāvacanasamrabda anayāmāsa laksmaṇaḥ
Duly grasping Seetha's words; Lakshmana brought to her many kinds of beautiful twigs
of trees, full of flowers.


Word by word
31. siitaarachanasamrabdhaH= grasping Seetha's words;lakshmaNaH= Lakshmana;aanayaamaasa= brought;bahuvidhaan= many
kinds;ramaNiiyaan= of beautiful twigs;paadapaan= of tress;kusumotkaTaan= filled with flowers.




32Ayodhya Kanda 55.32
विचित्रवालुकजलाम् हससारसनादिताम्रेमे जनकराजस्य तदा प्रेक्ष्य सुता नदीम्
vicitravālukajalām hasasārasanāditāmreme janakarājasya tadā prekṣya sutā nadīm
Then Seetha the daughter of King Janaka was please to see the River Yamuna with
wonderful sands and waters re-echoing to the cry of swans and cranes.


Word by word
32. tadaa= then;janakaraajasya sutaa= Seetha the daughter
of King Janaka;reme= was please;prekshhya= to see;nadiim= the
River Yamuna;vichitravaalukajalam= with wonderful sands and waters;hamsa saarasa

33Ayodhya Kanda 55.33
क्रोशमात्रम् ततो गत्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मनौबहून्मेध्यान् मृगान् हत्वा चेरतुर्यमुनावने
krośamātram tato gatvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmanaubahūnmedhyān mṛgān hatvā ceraturyamunāvane
Thereafter having travelled only a couple of miles the two brothers Rama and
Lakshmana killed many consecrated deer and ate in the river-forest of Yamuna.


Word by word
33. tataH= thereafter;gatvaa= having travelled;kroshamaatram= only a couple of miles;bhraatarau= the two brothers;raamalakshhmaNau= Rama and Lakshmana;hatvaa= killed;bahuun= many;medhyaan= consecrated;mR^igaan= deer;cheratuH= and ate;yamunaavane= in the river-forest of Yamuna.




34Ayodhya Kanda 55.34
विहृत्य ते बर्हिणपूगनादिते |शुभे वने वानरवारणायुते |समम् नदीवप्रमुपेत्य सम्मतम् |निवासमाजग्मु रदीनदर्शनाः
vihṛtya te barhiṇapūganādite |śubhe vane vānaravāraṇāyute |samam nadīvapramupetya sammatam |nivāsamājagmu radīnadarśanāḥ
Having strolled in the charming forest, mad noisy by a number of peacocks and which
was inhabited by elephants and monkeys and reaching an agreeable level ground at the bank of the
river wearing an undejected look finally sought for an abode for the night.


Word by word
34. te= they;nadiinadarshanaaH= wearing an undejected
look;vihR^itya= having strolled;shubhe vane= in the charming forest;barhiNa puuganaadite= where a number of peacocks called;vaanara vaaraNaayute=
and which was inhabited by elephants and monkeys;upetya= reached;sammatam= an
agreeable;sumam= level ground;nadiipavram= at the bank of the river;aajagmatuH= and sought for;nivaasam= an abode.



    
  
  Sage Bharadwaja informs the route by which Rama and Lakshmana can reach Chitrakuta. They cross the River Yamuna by a raft prepared by themselves. Seetha prays the River Yamuna and a fig tree called Syama. The three of them traveled for a couple of miles along the bank of Yamuna, strolling in the charming forest and reach a leveled ground on the bank to take rest for the night.
