24Yuddha Kanda 29.24
ततस्तम् तु महात्मानम् चारा राक्षससत्तमम्कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम् जग्मुर् यत्र रामः सलक्ष्मणः
tatastam tu mahātmānam cārā rākṣasasattamamkṛtvā pradakṣiṇam jagmur yatra rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ
Having thus made circumambulation to Ravana the excellent and the distinguished

25Yuddha Kanda 29.25
ते सुवेलस्य शैलस्य समीपे राम लक्ष्मणौप्रच्चन्ना ददृशुर् गत्वा ससुग्रीव विभीषणौ
te suvelasya śailasya samīpe rāma lakṣmaṇaupraccannā dadṛśur gatvā sasugrīva vibhīṣaṇau
Having gone in a disguised manner, those spies saw Rama and Lakshman together with
Sugreeva and Vibhishana in the neighbourhood of Mountain Suvela.


Word by word
25. gatvaa= having gone;prachchhannaaH= in a disguised
manner;te= they;dadR^ishuH= saw;raamalakshmaNau= Rama and
Lakshman;sa sugriiva vibhiiSaNau= together with Sugreeva and Vibhishana;saniipe= in the vicinity;suvelasya shailasya= of mountain Suvela.




26Yuddha Kanda 29.26
प्रेक्षमाणाश्चमूम् ताम् च बभूवुर्भयविह्वलाःते तु धर्म आत्मना दृष्टा राक्षस इन्द्रेण राक्षसाः
prekṣamāṇāścamūm tām ca babhūvurbhayavihvalāḥte tu dharma ātmanā dṛṣṭā rākṣasa indreṇa rākṣasāḥ
Seeing that army, those demons became overwhelmed with fear. However, they were
observed by the high-souled Vibhishana the Lord of demons.

overwhelmed with fear;dR^iSTaaH= and were observed;raakshasendreNa= by
Vibhishana the Lord of demons;dharmaatmanaa= the high-souled.




27Yuddha Kanda 29.27
विभीषणेन तत्रस्था निगृहीता यदृच्चयाशार्दूलो ग्राहितस्त्वेकः पापोऽयमिति राक्षसः
vibhīṣaṇena tatrasthā nigṛhītā yadṛccayāśārdūlo grāhitastvekaḥ pāpo.ayamiti rākṣasaḥ
Accidentally, the deomons there were caught by Vibhishana, who said that the demon
Shardula among them was wicked and got him alone seized.


Word by word
27. yard^ichchhayaa= accidentally;tatrasthaaH= the demons
there;nigR^ihiitaaH= were caught;vibhiiSaNena= by Vibhishana;iti=
saying that;ayam= this;raakSasaH= demon;paapaH= was a wicked
person;shaarduulaH tu= Shardula;ekaH= alone;graahitaH= was got
seized.




28Yuddha Kanda 29.28
मोक्षितः सोऽपि रामेण वध्यमानः प्लवङ्गमैःअनृशंसेन रामेण मोक्षिता राक्षसाः सरे
mokṣitaḥ so.api rāmeṇa vadhyamānaḥ plavaṅgamaiḥanṛśaṃsena rāmeṇa mokṣitā rākṣasāḥ sare
That Shardula also, who was going to be killed by the monkeys, was got released by
Rama. The other demons also were got released by Rama, the kind man.


Word by word
28. so.api= that Shardula also;vadhyamaanaH= who was
about to be killed;plavaN^gamaiH= by the monkeys;mochitaH= was got released;raameNa= by Rama;pare= the other;raakSasaaH= demons;mokSitaaH= wee got released;raameNa= by Rama;anR^ishamsena= the
kind man.




29Yuddha Kanda 29.29
वानरैर् अर्दितास् ते तु विक्रान्तैर् लघु विक्रमैःपुनर् लंकाम् अनुप्राप्ताः श्वसन्तो नष्ट चेतसः
vānarair arditās te tu vikrāntair laghu vikramaiḥpunar laṃkām anuprāptāḥ śvasanto naṣṭa cetasaḥ
Those demons, harassed by the courageous and the quick-paced monkeys, became
insensible, heaved a sigh and reached back Lanka.


Word by word
29. te= those demons;arditaaH= harassed;vaanaraiH= by the monkeys;vikraantaiH= the courageous;laghuvikramaiH= and the quick-footed;naSTachetasaH= became insensible;shvasantaH= heaved a
sigh;anupraaptaaH= and reached;laN^kaam= Lanka;punaH= again.




30Yuddha Kanda 29.30
ततो दशग्रीवम् उपस्थितास् ते |चारा बहिर् नित्य चरा निशा चराः |गिरेः सुवेलस्य समीप वासिनम् |न्यवेदयन् भीम बलम् महाबलाः
tato daśagrīvam upasthitās te |cārā bahir nitya carā niśā carāḥ |gireḥ suvelasya samīpa vāsinam |nyavedayan bhīma balam mahābalāḥ
Those spies, who always wander outside and who were valiant rangers of the night,
thereafter approached Ravana and informed him that Rama's army was camping in the vicinity of the
Suvela mountain.


Word by word
30. chaaraaH= (those) spies;nityacharaaH= mahaabalaaH =
valiant;nishaacharaaH= rangers of the night;tataH= thereafter;upasthitaaH= approached;dashagriivam= Ravana;nyavedayan= and
informed him;raama balam= that Rama's army;samiipavaasinam= was camping in
the vicinity;suvelasya= of the Suvela mountain.



    
  
  Ravana reprimands Shuka and Sarana, asking them to leave the assembly. He again sends some spies to the place of Rama and Lakshmana. Those spies were got caught by Vibhishana and the monkeys start harassing them. But the compassionate Rama gets them released and the spies reach back Lanka.

title: Agitated to learn that Rama had arrived to Lanka…
text:
Home/Yuddha Kanda/Sarga 31

  Yuddha Kanda · Sarga 31
  Agitated to learn that Rama had arrived to Lanka…
  Agitated to learn that Rama had arrived to Lanka and is stationed at Suvela mountain along with his army, Ravana confers with his ministers and after dismissing them, approaches Seetha with Vidyujjuha, knower of conjuring tricks.

1Yuddha Kanda 31.1
ततस्तमक्षोभ्यबलम् लङ्कायां नृपतेश्चराः |सुवेले राघवं शैले निविष्टं प्रत्यवेदयन्
tatastamakṣobhyabalam laṅkāyāṃ nṛpateścarāḥ |suvele rāghavaṃ śaile niviṣṭaṃ pratyavedayan
The spies of king Ravana informed him that Rama with his imperturbable army
was encamped at Mount Suvela in Lanka.


Word by word
1. tataH= then;nR^ipateH= the king's;charaaH= spies;pratyavedan= informed (Ravana);tam raaghavam= that Rama;akSobhya balam= with his imperturbable army;niviSTam= was stationed;suvele shaile= at Mount Suvela;laN^kaayaam= in Lanka.




2Yuddha Kanda 31.2
चाराणाम् रावणः श्रुत्वा प्राप्तम् रामम् महाबलम् |जातोद्वेगोऽभवत्किंचित्सचिवानिदमब्रवीत्
cārāṇām rāvaṇaḥ śrutvā prāptam rāmam mahābalam |jātodvego.abhavatkiṃcitsacivānidamabravīt
Hearing through his spies that Rama with his mighty army had arrived to Lanka,
Ravana was a little agitated and spoke to his counsellors as follows:

2. shrutvaa= Hearing;chaaraaNaam= throught;spies;raamam= that Rama;mahaabalam= with his mighty army;praaptam= had arrived;raavaNaH= Ravana;jaatodvegaH= was agitated;kimchit= a little;abraviit= and spoke;idam= thse words;sachivaan= to his counsellors (as follows):




3Yuddha Kanda 31.3
मन्त्रिणः शीघ्रमायान्तु सर्वे वै सु समाहिताः |अयम् नो मन्त्रकालो हि सम्प्रास्त इति राक्षसाः
mantriṇaḥ śīghramāyāntu sarve vai su samāhitāḥ |ayam no mantrakālo hi samprāsta iti rākṣasāḥ
"The time for deliberation has come to us. Let our ministerial colleagues
come quickly with their keenly attentive minds."

तस्य तच्चासनम् श्रुत्वा मन्त्रिणोऽभ्यागमन् द्रुतम् |ततः स मन्त्रयामास राक्षसैः सचिवैः सह
tasya taccāsanam śrutvā mantriṇo.abhyāgaman drutam |tataḥ sa mantrayāmāsa rākṣasaiḥ sacivaiḥ saha
As per his command, the ministers came instantly. Ravana conferred with the
ogres, his ministers.

4. shrutvaa= hearing;tat= that;shaasanam= command;tasya= of his;mantriNaH= the ministers;abhyaagamam= came;drutam= soon;tataH= thereafter;saH= he;mantrayaamaasa= deliberated;sachivaiH saha= with his ministers;raakshhasaiH= the 
 ogres.




5Yuddha Kanda 31.5
मन्त्रयित्वा तु दुर्धर्षः क्षमं यत्तदन्न्तरम् |विसर्जयित्वा सचिवान् प्रविवेश स्वमालयम्
mantrayitvā tu durdharṣaḥ kṣamaṃ yattadanntaram |visarjayitvā sacivān praviveśa svamālayam
The dreadful Ravana discussed about the ensuing things to be done immediately.
He sent away the ministers and entered his palace.

6Yuddha Kanda 31.6
ततो राक्षसमादाय विद्युज्जिह्वम् महाबलम् |मायाविदम् महामायः प्रविशद्यत्र मैथिली

Thereafter, Ravana the practiser of conjuring tricks, took the exceedingly

8Yuddha Kanda 31.8
शिरो मायामयम् गृह्य राघवस्य विशाचर |मां त्वं समुपतिष्ठस्व महच्च सशरम् धनुः
śiro māyāmayam gṛhya rāghavasya viśācara |māṃ tvaṃ samupatiṣṭhasva mahacca saśaram dhanuḥ
"O, demon! Produce a head resembling Rama's along with a great bow and arrows
created deceptively and present yourself before me."

8. nishaachara= O;demon!;tvam= you;samupatisthasva= approached;maam= me;gR^ihya= holding;mayaamayam= a deceptive;raaghavasya= Rama's;shiraa= head sa sharam = along with his arrows;mahat= and the big;dhanuH cha= bow.

  Agitated to learn that Rama had arrived to Lanka and is stationed at Suvela mountain along with his army, Ravana confers with his ministers and after dismissing them, approaches Seetha with Vidyujjuha, knower of conjuring tricks. Informing Seetha that her husband along with his army had been killed in battle, he produces before her an illusive Rama's head along with bow and arrows created with Vidyujjuha's conjuring trick. Thus, Ravana deceives Seetha about the death of Rama.

  An ogre named Sarama reassures Seetha by telling her that Ravana, the conjurer created an illusory appearance of Rama's head and exhibited it before her. She informs Seetha that Rama is still alive and is stationed along with his forces at the southern shore of the ocean. Sarama restores confidence to Seetha, by saying that Rama after killing Ravana in battle will soon win her back.

  Yuddha Kanda · Sarga 35
  With the sound of kettle drums and couches, Rama arrives to Lanka…
  With the sound of kettle drums and couches, Rama arrives to Lanka with his army. Ravana hears those sounds and calls his ministers to chalk out his further course of action.

1Yuddha Kanda 35.1
तेन शन्ख विमिश्रेण भेरी शब्देन राघवः |उपयतो महा बाहू रामह् पर पुरम् जयः
tena śankha vimiśreṇa bherī śabdena rāghavaḥ |upayato mahā bāhū rāmah para puram jayaḥ
The mighty armed Rama, the conqueror of hostile cities sallied forth with the
resonant roll of kettle drums, mingled with the blast of couches.

36Yuddha Kanda 35.36
विष्णुम् मन्यामहे रामम् मानुषम् देहम् आस्थितम् |न हि मानुष मात्रो असौ राघवो दृढ विक्रमः
viṣṇum manyāmahe rāmam mānuṣam deham āsthitam |na hi mānuṣa mātro asau rāghavo dṛḍha vikramaḥ
"I deem Rama of firm fortitude as Vishnu dwelling in human form. This Rama is not a
mere human being, he by whom that most wonderful bridge was built across the sea. O, Ravana!
Conclude peace with Rama, who is the king of men. Having come to know of his acts, let that which
is good for the future be done after a mature understanding."

38Yuddha Kanda 35.38
इदम् वचस् तत्र निगद्य माल्यवन् |परीक्ष्य रक्षो अधिपतेर् मनः पुनः |अनुत्तमेषु उत्तम पौरुषो बली |बभूव तूष्णीम् समवेक्ष्य रावणम्
idam vacas tatra nigadya mālyavan |parīkṣya rakṣo adhipater manaḥ punaḥ |anuttameṣu uttama pauruṣo balī |babhūva tūṣṇīm samavekṣya rāvaṇam
Having spoken thus, the mighty Malyavan, who was foremost in valour among the
bravest warriors, being aware of what was passing in Ravana's mind, eyeing him, became silent.


Word by word

  With the sound of kettle drums and couches, Rama arrives to Lanka with his army. Ravana hears those sounds and calls his ministers to chalk out his further course of action. Malyavan, Ravana's maternal grandfather advises Ravana to conclude peace with Rama and restore Seetha to him as he is perceiving adverse omens.

1Yuddha Kanda 37.1
नर वानर राजौ तौ स च वायु सुतः कपिः |जाम्बवान् ऋक्ष राजसः च राक्षससः च विभीषणः

son of the wind, Jambavan the king of the Bears, Vibhishana the demon, Angada the son of Vali,
Lakshmana, Sushena along with his kinsfolk, Mainda, Dvivida, Gaja, Gavaksha, Kumuda, Nala and
Panasa, all having reached the enemy's territory, assembled to take counsel together.

  Rama, Sugreeva, Hanuman and others assemble to take counsel together, upon reaching the precinets of Lanks. While they were delibrating on the ways and means for the success of their mission, Vibhishana informs that he has sent his counsellors as spies to gather information about the enemy's plans and that they returned after gathering the required news about Ravana's arrangements at the four gates of theity. After hearing Vibhishana's information, Rama orders Nila, Angada Hanuman and others to storm the four gates and decides to stay on Suvela mountain with his army.

20Yuddha Kanda 39.20
निविष्टा तत्र शिखरे लन्का रावण पालितादशयोजनविस्तीर्णा विंशद्योजनमायता
niviṣṭā tatra śikhare lankā rāvaṇa pālitādaśayojanavistīrṇā viṃśadyojanamāyatā

sixty miles, was located on the apex of the mountain there.


Word by word

Commentary & notes
The length and breadth of the city given here varies from that given elsewhere -which is a hundred Yojanas wide and thirty yojanas long. This anomaly is reconciled by commentatorsby explaining the present verse as referring to the length and breadth of Lanka proper, whichcomprised the residence of Ravana.

tām mahāgṛhasambādhāṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ |nagarīṃ tridivaprakhyāṃ vismayaṃ prāpa vīryavān 6-39-28
Beholding that City, which looks like heaven and crammed with huge palaces, the
valiant Rama the elder brother of Lakshmana was seized with astonishment.

ताम् रत्न पूर्णाम् बहु सम्विधानाम् |प्रासाद मालाभिर् अलम्कृताम् च |पुरीम् महा यन्त्र कवाट मुख्याम् |ददर्श रामो महता बलेन

Word by word

  Rama and the monkeys see the charming gardens and groves located in Lanka, viewing them from the top of Suvela mountain. Some of the monkeys, thrilling with rapture, enter the gardens and enjoy their beauty of flowers and birds. Some others went towards Lanka; located on the apex of Trikuta mountain. They see the city with its large mansions and seven storied buildings, including the thousand-pillared mansion of Ravana with a height almost touching the skies.

1Yuddha Kanda 41.1
अथ तस्मिन् निमित्तानि दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मण पूर्वजः |सुग्रीवम् सम्परिष्वज्य रामो वचनमब्रवीत्
atha tasmin nimittāni dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇa pūrvajaḥ |sugrīvam sampariṣvajya rāmo vacanamabravīt

after embracing Sugreeva spoke these words.

असंमन्त्य्र मया सार्थम् तदिदम् साहसं कृतम् |एवम् साहसयुक्तानि न कुर्वन्ति जनेश्वराः
asaṃmantyra mayā sārtham tadidam sāhasaṃ kṛtam |evam sāhasayuktāni na kurvanti janeśvarāḥ

6Yuddha Kanda 41.6
त्वयि चानागते पूर्वमिति मे निश्चिता मतिः |जानतश्चापि ते वीर्यम् महेन्द्रवरुणोपनु
tvayi cānāgate pūrvamiti me niścitā matiḥ |jānataścāpi te vīryam mahendravaruṇopanu
"O, monkey of great strength, equal to Indra the god of celestials and Varuna the king
of universe! If you have not returned, though I am conversant with your valour, this was my pre-determined
resolve that having killed Ravana in fight with his sons forces and chariots, I should have installed
Vibhishana as king of Lanka, placing the kingdom of Ayodhya in the hands of Bharata and renounced my
life."

तमेवम्वादिनं रामं सुग्रीवः प्रत्यभाषत
tamevamvādinaṃ rāmaṃ sugrīvaḥ pratyabhāṣata

  Rama advises Sugreeva not to repeat such reckless acts in future on the ground of he being a king. Then Rama tells Lakshmana about the various evil portents he had seen. Rama commands the monkey-generals to besiege all the four gates of Lanka. He himself along with Lakshmana protects the army, besieging the northern gate being guarded by Ravana. Then, Rama sends Angada to Ravana, to expostulate him and to bring him back to reason. Angada tries his best to convince Ravana, but in vain. Ravana commands his attendants to seize Angada. Angada shakes out those attendants who tried to seize him ascends the roof of Ravana's palace, tramples ad crushes it down by his strength. Angada finally returns to Rama, who was stationed in the midst of the monkey-forces.

1Yuddha Kanda 43.1
युध्यताम् तु ततस् तेषाम् वानराणाम् महात्मनाम् |रक्षसाम् सम्बभूव अथ बल कोपह् सुदारुणः
yudhyatām tu tatas teṣām vānarāṇām mahātmanām |rakṣasām sambabhūva atha bala kopah sudāruṇaḥ
While highly wise monkey-troops and the demons were fighting a terrible military
ferocity arose in them.


Word by word

2Yuddha Kanda 43.2
ते हयैः कान्चन आपीडैर् ध्वजैश च अग्नि शैख उपमैः |रथैश च आदित्य सम्काशाइह् कवचैश च मनो रमैः
te hayaiḥ kāncana āpīḍair dhvajaiśa ca agni śaikha upamaiḥ |rathaiśa ca āditya samkāśāih kavacaiśa ca mano ramaiḥ
Those demons, the best of ogres, doing terrific acts and eager to triumph in
Ravana's name, marched ahead on steeds with golden trappings or elephants resembling pointed
flames, or in chariots flashing like the sun and themselves wearing beautiful armours, creating
reverberant sounds in the ten regions.

3Yuddha Kanda 43.3
निर्ययू राक्षस व्याघ्रा नादयन्तो दिशओ दशा |राक्षसा भीम कर्माणो रावणस्य जय एषिणः

4Yuddha Kanda 43.4
वानराणाम् अपि चमूर् महती जयम् इच्चताम् |अभ्यधावत ताम् सेनाम् रक्षसाम् काम रूपिणाम्
vānarāṇām api camūr mahatī jayam iccatām |abhyadhāvata tām senām rakṣasām kāma rūpiṇām
The great army of monkeys, also eager to triumph, marched opposite to those troops
of demons of terrible acts.

5Yuddha Kanda 43.5
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे तेषाम् अन्योन्यम् अभिधावताम् |रक्षसाम् वानराणाम् च द्वन्द्व युद्धम् अवर्तत
etasminn antare teṣām anyonyam abhidhāvatām |rakṣasām vānarāṇām ca dvandva yuddham avartata

6Yuddha Kanda 43.6
अन्गदेन इन्द्रजित् सार्धम् वालि पुत्रेण राक्षसः |अयुध्यत महा तेजास् त्र्यम्बकेण यथा अन्धकः
angadena indrajit sārdham vāli putreṇa rākṣasaḥ |ayudhyata mahā tejās tryambakeṇa yathā andhakaḥ
The demon Indrajit of immense energy fought with Angada the son of Vali, as the
demon Andhaka fought with Shiva the Lord of destruction.

7Yuddha Kanda 43.7
प्रजन्घेन च सम्पातिर् नित्यम् दुर्मर्षणो रणे |जम्बू मालिनम् आरब्धो हनूमान् अपि वानरः
prajanghena ca sampātir nityam durmarṣaṇo raṇe |jambū mālinam ārabdho hanūmān api vānaraḥ
The ever indomitable Sampati fought with Prajangha and Hanuman the monkey measured

8Yuddha Kanda 43.8
सम्गतः सुमहा क्रोधो राक्षसो रावण अनुजः |समरे तीक्ष्ण वेगेन मित्रघ्नेन विभीषणः
samgataḥ sumahā krodho rākṣaso rāvaṇa anujaḥ |samare tīkṣṇa vegena mitraghnena vibhīṣaṇaḥ
The demon with great fury, Vibhishana the younger brother of Ravana confronted with
Shatrughna possessing fiery velocity in battle.

9Yuddha Kanda 43.9
तपनेन गजह् सार्धम् राक्षसेन महा बलः |निकुम्भेन महा तेजा नीलो अपि समयुध्यत
tapanena gajah sārdham rākṣasena mahā balaḥ |nikumbhena mahā tejā nīlo api samayudhyata

10Yuddha Kanda 43.10
वानर इन्द्रस् तु सुग्रीवह् प्रघसेन समागतः |सम्गतः समरे शरीमान् विरूप अक्षेण लक्ष्मणः
vānara indras tu sugrīvah praghasena samāgataḥ |samgataḥ samare śarīmān virūpa akṣeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ
Sugreeva the king of monkeys confronted well with Praghasa and the glorious

11Yuddha Kanda 43.11
अग्नि केतुश च दुर्धर्षो रशमि केतुश च राक्षसः |सुप्तघ्नो यज्न कोपश च रामेण सह सम्गताः
agni ketuśa ca durdharṣo raśami ketuśa ca rākṣasaḥ |suptaghno yajna kopaśa ca rāmeṇa saha samgatāḥ
The invincible Agniketu, Rashmiketu, Mitraghnu and Yajnakopa confronted with

12Yuddha Kanda 43.12
वज्र मुष्टिश्च मैन्देन द्विविदेन अशानि प्रभः |राक्षसाभ्याम् सुघोराभ्याम् कपि मुख्यौ समागतौ
vajra muṣṭiśca maindena dvividena aśāni prabhaḥ |rākṣasābhyām sughorābhyām kapi mukhyau samāgatau
Vajramushti confronted with Mainda and Ashaniprabha with Dvivida. Those principal

13Yuddha Kanda 43.13
वीरह् प्रतपनो घोरो राक्षसो रण दुर्धरः |समरे तीक्ष्ण वेगेन नलेन समयुध्यत
vīrah pratapano ghoro rākṣaso raṇa durdharaḥ |samare tīkṣṇa vegena nalena samayudhyata

14Yuddha Kanda 43.14
धर्मस्य पुत्रो बलवान् सुषेण;इति विशरुतः |स विद्युन् मालिना सार्धम् अयुध्यत महा कपिः
dharmasya putro balavān suṣeṇa;iti viśarutaḥ |sa vidyun mālinā sārdham ayudhyata mahā kapiḥ
That great monkey called Sushena, the strong son of Yama fought with Vidyunmali.

15Yuddha Kanda 43.15
वानराश च अपरे भीमा राक्षसैर् अपरैह् सह |द्वन्द्वम् समीयुर् बहुधा युद्धाय बहुभिह् सह
vānarāśa ca apare bhīmā rākṣasair aparaih saha |dvandvam samīyur bahudhā yuddhāya bahubhih saha

16Yuddha Kanda 43.16
तत्र आसीत् सुमहद् युद्धम् तुमुलम् लोम हर्षणम् |रक्षसाम् वानराणाम् च वीराणाम् जयम् इच्चताम्
tatra āsīt sumahad yuddham tumulam loma harṣaṇam |rakṣasām vānarāṇām ca vīrāṇām jayam iccatām
A very great tumultuous battle, which caused hair to stand on end, continued there
between heroic demons and monkeys, who were eager to triumph.

tumultuous;aasiit= continued;viiraaNaam= (between) heroic;rakSasaam= demons;vaanaraaNaamcha= and monkeys;ichhataam= who were eager to

17Yuddha Kanda 43.17
हरि राक्षस देहेभ्यह् प्रसृताह् केशा शाअड्वलाः |शारीर सम्घाट वहाह् प्रसुस्रुह् शओणित आपगाः
hari rākṣasa dehebhyah prasṛtāh keśā śāaḍvalāḥ |śārīra samghāṭa vahāh prasusruh śaoṇita āpagāḥ

18Yuddha Kanda 43.18
आजघान इन्द्रजित् क्रुद्धो वज्रेण इव शात क्रतुः |अन्गदम् गदया वीरम् शात्रु सैन्य विदारणम्
ājaghāna indrajit kruddho vajreṇa iva śāta kratuḥ |angadam gadayā vīram śātru sainya vidāraṇam
The enraged Indrajit struck the valiant Angada (who can tear asunder the enemy

19Yuddha Kanda 43.19
तस्य कान्चन चित्र अन्गम् रथम् साशवम् ससारथिम् |जघान समरे शरीमान् अन्गदो वेगवान् कपिः || १९
tasya kāncana citra angam ratham sāśavam sasārathim |jaghāna samare śarīmān angado vegavān kapiḥ || 19
The swift monkey, Angada struck his chariot, having a variegated body of gold, along
with horses and the charioteer in the battle.

20Yuddha Kanda 43.20
सम्पातिस् तु त्रिभिर् बाणैह् प्रजन्घेन समाहतः |निजघान अशव कर्णेन प्रजन्घम् रण मूर्धनि
sampātis tu tribhir bāṇaih prajanghena samāhataḥ |nijaghāna aśava karṇena prajangham raṇa mūrdhani

Ashvakarna tree, at the zenith of the combat.

Ashvakarna tree;raNamuurdhani= at a zenith of the combat.




21Yuddha Kanda 43.21
जम्बू माली रथस्थस् तु रथ शाक्त्या महा बलः |बिभेद समरे क्रुद्धो हनूमन्तम् स्तन अन्तरे
jambū mālī rathasthas tu ratha śāktyā mahā balaḥ |bibheda samare kruddho hanūmantam stana antare

22Yuddha Kanda 43.22
तस्य तम् रथम् आस्थाय हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः |प्रममाथ तलेन आशौ सह तेन एव रक्षसा
tasya tam ratham āsthāya hanūmān māruta ātmajaḥ |pramamātha talena āśau saha tena eva rakṣasā

भिन्न गात्रः शारैस् तीक्ष्णैह् क्षिप्र हस्तेन रक्षसा |प्रजघान अद्रि शऋन्गेण तपनम् मुष्टिना गजः
bhinna gātraḥ śārais tīkṣṇaih kṣipra hastena rakṣasā |prajaghāna adri śaṛngeṇa tapanam muṣṭinā gajaḥ

grasantam iva sainyāni praghasam vānara adhipaḥ |sugrīvaḥ sapta parṇena nirbibheda jaghāna ca
Pierced in the limbs by sharp arrows by Praghasa the swift-handed demon, Sugreeva
the Lord of demons immediately killed Praghasa (who was appearing to swallow the monkey-troops)

25Yuddha Kanda 43.25
प्रपीड्य शार वर्षेण राक्षसम् भीम दर्शानम् |निजघान विरूप अक्षम् शारेण एकेन लक्ष्मणः
prapīḍya śāra varṣeṇa rākṣasam bhīma darśānam |nijaghāna virūpa akṣam śāreṇa ekena lakṣmaṇaḥ

look;nipiiDya= having;tormented;raakSasam= the demon;viruupaakSam= Virupaksha;sharavarSeNa= by a bombardment of arrows;nijaghaana= killed

26Yuddha Kanda 43.26
अग्नि केतुश च दुर्धर्षो रशमि केतुश च राक्षसः |सुप्तिघ्नो यज्न कोपश च रामम् निर्बिभिदुह् शारैः

The invincible Agniketu, Rashmiketu, Mitrughna and Yajnakopa wounded Rama by

27Yuddha Kanda 43.27
तेषाम् चतुर्णाम् रामस् तु शैरांसि समरे शारैः |क्रुद्धश चतुर्भिश चिच्चेद घोरैर् अग्नि शैख उपमैः
teṣām caturṇām rāmas tu śairāṃsi samare śāraiḥ |kruddhaśa caturbhiśa cicceda ghorair agni śaikha upamaiḥ

28Yuddha Kanda 43.28
वज्र मुष्टिस् तु मैन्देन मुष्टिना निहतो रणे |पपात सरथह् साशवह् पुराट्ट इव भू तले
vajra muṣṭis tu maindena muṣṭinā nihato raṇe |papāta sarathah sāśavah purāṭṭa iva bhū tale
Struck with a fist by Mainda in the battle, Vajramushti along with his chariot fell

वज्र अशानि सम स्पर्शओ द्विविदो अप्य् अशानि प्रभम् |जघान गिरि शऋन्गेण मिषताम् सर्व रक्षसाम्
vajra aśāni sama sparśao dvivido apy aśāni prabham |jaghāna giri śaṛngeṇa miṣatām sarva rakṣasām

sharp arrows, like a cloud by the rays of the sun.

द्विविदम् वानर इन्द्रम् तु द्रुम योधिनम् आहवे |शारैर् अशानि सम्काशाइह् स विव्याध अशानि प्रभः
dvividam vānara indram tu druma yodhinam āhave |śārair aśāni samkāśāih sa vivyādha aśāni prabhaḥ

31Yuddha Kanda 43.31
स शारैर् अतिविद्ध अन्गो द्विविदह् क्रोध मूर्चितः |सालेन सरथम् साशवम् निजघान अशानि प्रभम्

निकुम्भस् तु रणे नीलम् नील अन्जन चय प्रभम् |निर्बिभेद शारैस् तीक्ष्णैह् करैर् मेघम् इव अंशौमान्
nikumbhas tu raṇe nīlam nīla anjana caya prabham |nirbibheda śārais tīkṣṇaih karair megham iva aṃśaumān
Even Dvivida, whose impact was like a flash of lightening of a thunder bolt, struck

33Yuddha Kanda 43.33
पुनः शार शातेन अथ क्षिप्र हस्तो निशाअ चरः |बिभेद समरे नीलम् निकुम्भह् प्रजहास च
punaḥ śāra śātena atha kṣipra hasto niśāa caraḥ |bibheda samare nīlam nikumbhah prajahāsa ca

yodhinam= who was fighting with trees;aahave= in the battle.




34Yuddha Kanda 43.34
तस्य एव रथ चक्रेण नीलो विष्णुर् इव आहवे |शैरश चिच्चेद समरे निकुम्भस्य च सारथेः
tasya eva ratha cakreṇa nīlo viṣṇur iva āhave |śairaśa cicceda samare nikumbhasya ca sāratheḥ
With his limbs struck by arrows, that Dvivida agitated as he was by anger, struck

34. abhividdhaaN^gaH= with his limbs struck;sharaiH= by
arrows;saH dvividaH= that Dvivida;krodha muurchhitaH= agitated by anger;nijaghaana= struck;salena= with a Sala tree;ashaniprabha=
Ashaniprabha;saratham= along with the chariot;saashvam= and the horses.




35Yuddha Kanda 43.35
विद्युन् माली रथस्थस् तु शारैह् कान्चन भूषणैः |सुषेणम् ताडयाम् आस ननाद च मुहुर् मुहुः
vidyun mālī rathasthas tu śāraih kāncana bhūṣaṇaiḥ |suṣeṇam tāḍayām āsa nanāda ca muhur muhuḥ
Vidyunmali, seated in a chariot, struck Sushena repeatedly with arrows adorned with
gold and made a roaring sound.

तम् रथस्थम् अथो दृष्ट्वा सुषेणो वानर उत्तमः |गिरि शऋन्गेण महता रथम् आशौ न्यपातयत्

37Yuddha Kanda 43.37
लाघवेन तु सम्युक्तो विद्युन् माली निशाअ चरः |अपक्रम्य रथात् तूर्णम् गदा पाणिह् क्षितौ स्थितः
lāghavena tu samyukto vidyun mālī niśāa caraḥ |apakramya rathāt tūrṇam gadā pāṇih kṣitau sthitaḥ

38Yuddha Kanda 43.38
ततह् क्रोध समाविष्टह् सुषेणो हरि पुम्गवः |शैलाम् सुमहतीम् गृह्य निशाअ चरम् अभिद्रवत्
tatah krodha samāviṣṭah suṣeṇo hari pumgavaḥ |śailām sumahatīm gṛhya niśāa caram abhidravat
Then, the excellent monkey, Sushena engulfed as he was with anger, seizing a very
huge rock in his hands, chased that demon.


Word by word

sizing;sumahatiim= a very huge;shilaam= rock;abhidravat= chased;nishaacharam= that demon.




39Yuddha Kanda 43.39
तम् आपतन्तम् गदया विद्युन् माली निशाअ चरः |वक्षस्य् अभिजग्नान आशौ सुषेणम् हरि सत्तमम्
tam āpatantam gadayā vidyun mālī niśāa caraḥ |vakṣasy abhijagnāna āśau suṣeṇam hari sattamam
Vidyunmali the ranger of the night; struck that approaching Sushena the excellent
monkey, quickly with a mace on his chest.


Word by word
39. vidyunmaalii= Vidyunmali;nishaacharaH= the ranger of
the night;abhijaghaanaha= struck;tam= that;aapatantam= approaching
suSeNam = Sushena;haripuN^gavam= the excellent monkey;aashu= quickly;gadayaa= with a mace;vakSasi= on his chest.




40Yuddha Kanda 43.40
गदा प्रहारम् तम् घोरम् अचिन्त्य प्लवग उत्तमः |ताम् शैलाम् पातयाम् आस तस्य उरसि महा मृधे
gadā prahāram tam ghoram acintya plavaga uttamaḥ |tām śailām pātayām āsa tasya urasi mahā mṛdhe
Not minding that terrific blow with the mace in the great battle, Sushena the
excellent monkey silently threw that huge rock on his chest.


Word by word
40 achintya= not minding;tam= that;ghoram=
terrific;gadaaprahaaram= blow with the mace;mahaamR^idhe= in that great
battle;plavagottamaH= the excellent monkey;Sushena;tuuSNiim= silently;paatayaamaasa= threw;taam= that rock;tasya urasi= on his chest.




41Yuddha Kanda 43.41
शैला प्रहार अभिहतो विद्युन् माली निशाअ चरः |निष्पिष्ट हृदयो भूमौ गत असुर् निपपात ह
śailā prahāra abhihato vidyun mālī niśāa caraḥ |niṣpiṣṭa hṛdayo bhūmau gata asur nipapāta ha
Struck by the thump of that rock, Vidyunmali the demon, his chest crushed, fell

41. nishaacharaH= the demon;vidyunmaalii= Vdyunmali;shilaaprahaaraabhihataH= struck by the thump of that rock;niSpiSTa hR^idayaH=
his chest crushed;nipahaata ha= fell;gataasuH= lifeless;bhuumau=
on the earth.




42Yuddha Kanda 43.42
एवम् तैर् वानरैह् शौउरैह् शौउरास् ते रजनी चराः |द्वन्द्वे विमृदितास् तत्र दैत्या;इव दिव ओकसैः
evam tair vānaraih śauuraih śauurās te rajanī carāḥ |dvandve vimṛditās tatra daityā;iva diva okasaiḥ
Those strong demons were destroyed thus by those valiant monkeys there in a series
of hand to hand encounters, as the demons were destroyed by the blows of the celestials.


Word by word
42. te= those;shuuraaH= strong;rajaniicharaaH=
demons;vimathitaaH= were destroyed;evam= thus;taiH= by those;shuuraiH= strong;vaanaraiH= monkeys;tatra= there;dvandeve= in a series of hand to hand encounters;daityaa iva= as the demons;divaukasaiH= by the celestials.




43Yuddha Kanda 43.43
भल्लैः खड्गैर् गदाभिश च शाक्ति तोमर पट्टसैः |अपविद्धश च भिन्नश च रथैः साम्ग्रामिकैर् हयैः
bhallaiḥ khaḍgair gadābhiśa ca śākti tomara paṭṭasaiḥ |apaviddhaśa ca bhinnaśa ca rathaiḥ sāmgrāmikair hayaiḥ
The battle-field became frightening with extra-ordinary spears, other arrows, maces,
javelins, lances and some other weapons with three points, shattered chariots and military steeds
elephants in rut, monkeys and demons which had been killed, wheels axles and yokes broken and lying
on the ground and frequented as it was by herds of jackals.


Word by word
43;44. aayodhanam= the battle-field;babhuuva= became;ghoram= frightening;bhallaiH= with extra ordinary spears;anyaiH=
other arrows;gadaabhishcha= maces;shaktitomara paTTishaiH= javelins;lances
and some other weapons with three points;apaviddhaiH= shattered;rathaishchaapi= chariots;hayaiH= steeds;kuNjaraiH= elephants;mattaiH= in rut;tathaa= and;vaanara raakSasaiH= monkeys and demons;nihataiH= which
had been killed;chakraakSayugadaN^Daishcha= wheels;axles and yokes;bhagnaiH=
broken;dharaNisamshritaiH= and lying on the ground;gomaayugaNa sevitam= and
frequented as it was by herds of jackals.




44Yuddha Kanda 43.44
निहतैः कुन्जरैर् मत्तैस् तथा वानर राक्षसैः |चक्र अक्ष युग दण्डैश च भग्नैर् धरणि संशरितैःबभूव आयोधनम् घोरम् गोमायु गण सेवितम्
nihataiḥ kunjarair mattais tathā vānara rākṣasaiḥ |cakra akṣa yuga daṇḍaiśa ca bhagnair dharaṇi saṃśaritaiḥbabhūva āyodhanam ghoram gomāyu gaṇa sevitam
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


45Yuddha Kanda 43.45
कबन्धानि समुत्पेतुर् दिक्षु वानर रक्षसाम् |विमर्दे तुमुले तस्मिन् देव असुर रण उपमे
kabandhāni samutpetur dikṣu vānara rakṣasām |vimarde tumule tasmin deva asura raṇa upame
The headless trunks of monkeys and demons sprang up here and there in the midst of
that tumultuous conflict, which resembled the war between celestials and demons.


Word by word
45. kabandhaani= the headless trunks;vaanara rakSasaam=
of monkeys and demons;samutpetuH= sprang up;dikSu= here and there;tasmin= (in the midst) of that;tumule vimarde= tumultuous conflict;devaasura raNopame= which resembled the war between celestials and demons.




46Yuddha Kanda 43.46
निहन्यमाना हरि पुम्गवैस् तदा |निशाअ चराह् शओणित दिग्ध गात्राह् |पुनः सुयुद्धम् तरसा समाशरिता |दिवाकरस्य अस्तमय अभिकान्क्षिणह्
nihanyamānā hari pumgavais tadā |niśāa carāh śaoṇita digdha gātrāh |punaḥ suyuddham tarasā samāśaritā |divākarasya astamaya abhikānkṣiṇah
Then, the rangers of the night, with their limbs anointed with blood after being
attacked by the excellent monkeys, longed for sun-set and again with strength, assembled for a good
combat.


Word by word
46. tadaa= then;nishaacharaaH= the rangers of the night;shoNita digdhagaatraaH= their limbs anointed with blood;nihanyamaanaaH= after
being attacked;haripuNgavaiH= by the excellent monkeys;divaakarasya astamayaabhi
kaaNkSiNaH= longed for sun-set;punaH= and again;samaashritaaH=
assembled;tarasaa= with strength;suyuddham= for a good combat.



    
  
  Extra-ordinary duels arose between the monkeys and demons, who ran up towards each other. Indrajit fought with Angeda, Sampati with Prajangha, Hanuman with Jambumali, Vibhishana with the demon Shatrughna, Gaja with Tapana, Nila with Nikumbha, Sugreeva with Praghasa, Lakshmana with Virupaksha, Agniketu and others with Rama, Vajramsushit with Mainda, Ashaniprabha with Divivda, Pratapana with Nala and Sushena with Vidyunami. Streams of blood flowed from both sides. In a series of hand-to-hand encounters, the valiant monkeys destroyed the strong demons. The remaining demons waited for the sun to se-in and re-assembled with a renewed vigour for the battle.

1Yuddha Kanda 45.1
स तस्य गतिम् अन्विच्चन् राज पुत्रह् प्रतापवान् |दिदेश अतिबलो रामो दश वानर यूथपान्
sa tasya gatim anviccan rāja putrah pratāpavān |dideśa atibalo rāmo daśa vānara yūthapān

2Yuddha Kanda 45.2

dvau suṣeṇasya dāyādau nīlam ca plavaga ṛṣabham |angadam vāli putram ca śarabham ca tarasvinam
Rama the scourger of his enemies ordered both the sons of Sushena, Nila the chief of
monkeys, Angada the son of Vali, the stron Sharabha, Dvivida, Hanuman, the very strong Sanuprastha,
Rishabha and Rishabha skandha.

and Rishabhaskandha.




3Yuddha Kanda 45.3
द्विनतम् जाम्बवन्तम् च सानुप्रस्थम् महा बलम् |ऋषभम् च ऋषभ स्कन्धम् आदिदेश परम् तपः
dvinatam jāmbavantam ca sānuprastham mahā balam |ṛṣabham ca ṛṣabha skandham ādideśa param tapaḥ

  Rama orders ten of the monkey-generals to search for the whereabouts of Indrajit. But Indrajit arrested the approach of those monkeys, by means of his arrows. Both Rama and Lakshmana were transfixed by Indrajit with a net work of serpentine arrows into the vital parts of Rama and Lakshmana and they fall down on the battle-ground in a bath of blood. Seeing those two scions of Raghu in that state, the monkeys give way to utter despondence.

  Yuddha Kanda · Sarga 47
  Ravana summons some female demons including Trijata…
  Ravana summons some female demons including Trijata and instructs them to take Seetha in Pushpaka-plane to the battle-front and show Rama and Lakshmana alleged to have been killed by Indrajit.

leading monkeys surrounded Rama in order to watch over him.

  Ravana summons some female demons including Trijata and instructs them to take Seetha in Pushpaka-plane to the battle-front and show Rama and Lakshmana alleged to have been killed by Indrajit. Accordingly, the female-demons take Seetha in Pushpaka-plane and show her Rama and Lakshmana lying unconscious on a bed of arrows in the battle-field. Imagining Rama and Lakshmana to have been dead, Seetha bursts into sobs.

1Yuddha Kanda 49.1
घोरेण शर बन्धेन बद्धौ दशरथ आत्मजौ |निश्वसन्तौ यथा नागौ शयानौ रुधिर उक्षितौ
ghoreṇa śara bandhena baddhau daśaratha ātmajau |niśvasantau yathā nāgau śayānau rudhira ukṣitau
Bound by that formidable network of arrows, the two high-souled sons of dasaratha
lay bathed in blood, breathing like serpants. All those foremost of monkeys who were exceedingly
strong, including Sugreeva, plunged in grief, were standing around those two illustrious
warriors.


Word by word
1;2. baddhau= bound;ghoreNa= by that formidable;sharabandhena= net work of arrows;mahaatmanau= the high-souled;dasharaatmajau= sons of Dasaratha (Rama and lakshmana);shayaanau= lay;rudhirokSitau= bathed in blood;niHshvasantau= breething;naagau
yathau= like serpants;sarve= all;te vaanarashreSThaH= those foremost of
monkeys;mahaabalaah= who were exceedingly stron;sa sugriivaaH= including
Sugreeva;shokapariplutaaH= plunged in grief;tasthuH= were standing;parivaarya= round;(the two illustrious warriors).




2Yuddha Kanda 49.2
सर्वे ते वानर श्रेष्ठाह् ससुग्रीवा महा बलाः |परिवार्य महात्मानौ तस्थुह् शोक परिप्लुताः
sarve te vānara śreṣṭhāh sasugrīvā mahā balāḥ |parivārya mahātmānau tasthuh śoka pariplutāḥ
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


3Yuddha Kanda 49.3
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तेरे रामह् प्रत्यबुध्यत वीर्यवान् |स्थिरत्वात् सत्त्व योगाच् च शरैह् संदानितो अपि सन्
etasminn antere rāmah pratyabudhyata vīryavān |sthiratvāt sattva yogāc ca śaraih saṃdānito api san
In the meanwhile, the mighty Rama by virtue of his hardihood and native strength,
awoke from his swwon, despite the shafts that held him captive.


Word by word
3. etasmin antare= in the meanwhile;viiryavaan= the
mighty;raamaH= Rama;sthiratvaat sattvayogaat cha= by virtue of his hardihood
and native strength;pratyabuddhata= awoke from his sworn;samdaanito.api shaaiH= despite the shifts that held him captive.




4Yuddha Kanda 49.4
ततो दृष्ट्वा सरुधिरम् विषण्णम् गाढम् अर्पितम् |भ्रातरम् दीन वदनम् पर्यदेवयद् आतुरः
tato dṛṣṭvā sarudhiram viṣaṇṇam gāḍham arpitam |bhrātaram dīna vadanam paryadevayad āturaḥ
Then, beholding his brother, bleeding unconscious, firmly thrown on teh floor, and
his features changed, Rama full of grief lamented thus:


Word by word
4. tataH= then;dR^iSTvaa= beholding;bhraataram= his brother;sarudhiram= discharging blood;niSaNNam= unconcious;gaaDham= firmly;arpitam= thrown on the floor;diinavadanam= and with
a melancholic face;paryadevayat= (Rama) lamented;aaturaH= full of grief
(thus):




5Yuddha Kanda 49.5
किम् नु मे सीतया कार्यम् किम् कार्यम् जीवितेन वा |शयानम् यो अद्य पश्यामि भ्रातरम् युधि निर्जितम्
kim nu me sītayā kāryam kim kāryam jīvitena vā |śayānam yo adya paśyāmi bhrātaram yudhi nirjitam
"Of what use to me is the recovery of Seetha or even life itself, since my brother
now lying, before my eyes, has been struck down in teh fight?"


Word by word

of Seetha;kim kaaryam vaa= or of what use;jiivitena= is even life itself;me= to me;yaH= since;pashyaami= I am seeing;bhraataram=
my brother;adya= now;shayaanam= lying;nirjitam= subdued;yudhi= in the fihgt.




6Yuddha Kanda 49.6
शक्या सीता समा नारी प्राप्तुम् लोके विचिन्वता |न लक्ष्मण समो भ्राता सचिवह् साम्परायिकः
śakyā sītā samā nārī prāptum loke vicinvatā |na lakṣmaṇa samo bhrātā sacivah sāmparāyikaḥ
"It can be possible, if I were to look for her, to find a consort equal to Seetha in
this world of mortals but not a brother, a friend and a comrade in a hostile war, such as
Lakshmana!"


Word by word
6. shakyaa= It can be possible;vichinvataa= if I were to
look for her;(to find);naarii= a consort;siitaasamaa= equal to Seetha;martyaloke= in the world of mortals;na= but not;bhraataa= a
brother;sachivaH= a friend;saamparaayikaH= and a comrade in a hostile war;lakSmaNaH samaH= such as Lakshmana.




7Yuddha Kanda 49.7
परित्यक्ष्याम्य् अहम् प्राणान् वानराणाम् तु पश्यताम् |यदि पन्चत्वम् आपन्नह् सुमित्र आनन्द वर्धनः
parityakṣyāmy aham prāṇān vānarāṇām tu paśyatām |yadi pancatvam āpannah sumitra ānanda vardhanaḥ
"If Lakshmana returned to the five elements, he the increaser of Sumitra's joy, I
will yield up my life-breaths while the monkeys stand looking on."


Word by word
7. aapannaH yadi= If he has returned;paNchatvam= to the
five elements;sumitraananda vardhanaH= he;the increaser of Sumitra's joy;aham= I;parityakSyaami= will yield up;praaNaan= my life-breaths;vaanaraNaam= (while) the monkeys;pashyataam= stand looking on.




8Yuddha Kanda 49.8
किम् नु वक्ष्यामि कौसल्याम् मातरम् किम् नु कैकयीम् |कथम् अम्बाम् सुमित्रांच पुत्र दर्शन लालसाम्
kim nu vakṣyāmi kausalyām mātaram kim nu kaikayīm |katham ambām sumitrāṃca putra darśana lālasām
"What shall I say to my mother, Kausalya or to Kaikeyi? How can I talk to my mother
Sumitra, sighing for the sight of her son?"


Word by word
8. kim nu vakSyaami= what shall I say;maataram= to my
mother;kausalyaam= Kausalya?;kim nu= what shall I tell;kaikeyiim=
to Kaikeyi?' katham = and how can I talk;ambaam= to my mother;sumitraam=
Sumitra;putra darshanalaalasaam= who is keenly sighing for the sight of her son.




9Yuddha Kanda 49.9
विवत्साम् वेपमानाम् च क्रोशन्तीम् कुररीम् इव |कथम् आश्वासयिष्यामि यदि यास्यामि तम् विना
vivatsām vepamānām ca krośantīm kurarīm iva |katham āśvāsayiṣyāmi yadi yāsyāmi tam vinā
"How shall I console Sumitra, trembling and crying out like an osprey, bereft of her
son, if I return to Ayodhya without lakshmana?"


Word by word
9. katham= How;aashvaasayiSyaami= shall I console;
(Sumitra);vepamaanaam cha= trembling;kroshantiim= and crying out;kurariimiva= like an osprey;vivatsaam= bereft of her son;Lakshmana;yaasyaami yadi= if I return (to Ayodhya);tam vinaa= without Lakshmana.




10Yuddha Kanda 49.10
कथम् वक्ष्यामि शत्रुघ्नम् भरतम् च यशस्विनम् |मया सह वनम् यातो विना तेन आगतह् पुनः
katham vakṣyāmi śatrughnam bharatam ca yaśasvinam |mayā saha vanam yāto vinā tena āgatah punaḥ
"How shall I tell Shatrughna and the illustrious Bharata when I return without
Lakshmana, who followed to the forest along with me?"

10. katham= how;vakSyaami= shall I tell shatrughnam =
Shatrughna;yashashvinam= and the illustrious;bharatam= Bharata;aham= (when) I;aagataH= return;tena vinaa= without Lakshmana;yaataH=
who followed;vanam= to the forest;mayasaha= along with me?




11Yuddha Kanda 49.11
उपालम्भम् न शक्ष्यामि सोढुम् बत सुमित्रया |इह एव देहम् त्यक्ष्यामि न हि जीवितुम् उत्सहे
upālambham na śakṣyāmi soḍhum bata sumitrayā |iha eva deham tyakṣyāmi na hi jīvitum utsahe
"Alas! I should not be able to endure Sumitra's reproaches. I will leave my body
here itself. I do not wish to continue living."


Word by word
11. bata= Alas!;na shakSyaami= I should not be able;soDhum= to endure;upaalambham= the reproaches;sumitrayaa= of
Sumitra;tyakSyaami= I will leave;deham= my body;ihaiva= here
itself;na utsahe= I do not wish;jiivitum= to live.




12Yuddha Kanda 49.12
धिग् माम् दुष्कृत कर्माणम् अनार्यम् यत् कृते ह्य् असौ |लक्ष्मणह् पतितह् शेते शर तल्पे गत असुवत्
dhig mām duṣkṛta karmāṇam anāryam yat kṛte hy asau |lakṣmaṇah patitah śete śara talpe gata asuvat
"Woe unto me to my wicked deed and to my lack of nobility. Through my fault,
Lakshmana has fallen and lies indeed on a bed of arrows as on who has yielded up his life!"


Word by word
12. dhik= woe;maam= unto me;duSkR^ita karmaaNam= to my wicked deed anaaryam = and to my lack of nobility;matkR^ite= through my fault;asau= this;lakSmaNaH= Lakshmana;paatitaH= was befallen;shete
hi= and lies indeed;sharatalpe= on a bed of arrows;gataasuvat= as me
who has yielded up his life!




13Yuddha Kanda 49.13
त्वम् नित्यम् सुविषण्णम् माम् आश्वासयसि लक्ष्मण |गत असुर् न अद्य शक्नोषि माम् आर्तम् अभिभाषितुम्
tvam nityam suviṣaṇṇam mām āśvāsayasi lakṣmaṇa |gata asur na adya śaknoṣi mām ārtam abhibhāṣitum
"O, Lakshmana! You always used to consoe me whenever I was in a great sorrow. You,
having lost your life now are not able to allay my sufferings with your words."


Word by word
13. lakSmaNa= O;Lakshmana!;tvam= you aashvaasayasi =
used to console;maam= me;nityam= always;suviSaNNam= whenever I was
in a great sorrow;gataasuH= you;having lost your life;naasi= are not;shaktaH= able;abhibhaaSitum= to talk;maam= to me;aartam=
afflicted with grief.




14Yuddha Kanda 49.14
येन अद्य बहवो युद्धे राक्षसा निहताह् क्षितौ |तस्याम् एव क्षितौ वीरह् स शेते निहतह् परैः
yena adya bahavo yuddhe rākṣasā nihatāh kṣitau |tasyām eva kṣitau vīrah sa śete nihatah paraiḥ
"You, who in this battle today, struck down inummerable demons to the earth, are
fallen, pierced by darts, like a hero on the self same field."


Word by word
14. tvam yena= You;who;yuddhe= in this battle;adya= today;nihataaH= struck down;bahavaH= innumerable;raakSasaaaH= demons;kSitau= to the earth;sheSe= are fallen;nihataH= pierced;sharaiH= by darts;shuuraH= like a hero;tasyaameva= on the self same field.




15Yuddha Kanda 49.15
शयानह् शर तल्पे अस्मिन् स्व शोणित परिप्लुतः |शर जालैश् चितो भाति भास्करो अस्तम् इव व्रजन्
śayānah śara talpe asmin sva śoṇita pariplutaḥ |śara jālaiś cito bhāti bhāskaro astam iva vrajan
"Lying on this bed of arrows, bathed in blood, you are piled up; sharajaalaiH= in a
heap of arrows; saH= you, as such; bhaasi= look; bhaaskaraH= iva= like the sun; vrajan= setting
behind; astam= the horizon.


Word by word
15. shayaanaH= lying;asmin sharatalpe= on this bed of
arrows;shoNitapariplutaH= bathed in blood;chitaH= you are piled up;sharajaalaiH= in a heap of arrows;saH= you;as such;bhaasi= look;bhaaskaraH iva= like the sun;vrajan= setting behind;astam= the
horizon.




16Yuddha Kanda 49.16
बाण अभिहत मर्मत्वान् न शक्नोत्य् अभिवीक्षितुम् |रुजा च अब्रुवतो ह्य् अस्य दृष्टि रागेण सूच्यते
bāṇa abhihata marmatvān na śaknoty abhivīkṣitum |rujā ca abruvato hy asya dṛṣṭi rāgeṇa sūcyate
"Your vital parts having been pierced with arrows, you are not able even to speak
now. Eventhough you not speaking, your agony is disclosed by the redness of your eyes."


Word by word
16. baaNaabhihata marmatvaat= your vital parts having been pierced
with arrows;na shaknoti= you are not able even;abhibhaaSitum= to speak (now);abruvato.api= eventhough you are not speaking;asya rujaa= your agony;suuchyate= is disclosed;dR^iSTiraageNa= by the redness of your eyes.




17Yuddha Kanda 49.17
यथा एव माम् वनम् यान्तम् अनुयातो महा द्युतिः |अहम् अप्य् अनुयास्यामि तथैव एनम् यम क्षयम्
yathā eva mām vanam yāntam anuyāto mahā dyutiḥ |aham apy anuyāsyāmi tathaiva enam yama kṣayam
"I shall follow him to the region of Yama, as that illustrious warrior accompanied
me when I retired to the forest."


Word by word
17. anuyaasyaami= I shall follow;enam= him;yamakSayam= to the region of Yama;yathaiva= as;mahadyutuH= that
illustrious warrior anuyaataH = accompanied;maam= me;ahamapi= when I;yaantam= retired;vanam= to the forest.




18Yuddha Kanda 49.18
इष्ट बन्धु जनो नित्यम् माम् च नित्यम् अनुव्रतः |इमाम् अद्य गतो अवस्थाम् मम अनार्यस्य दुर्नयैः
iṣṭa bandhu jano nityam mām ca nityam anuvrataḥ |imām adya gato avasthām mama anāryasya durnayaiḥ
"He who loved his own kinsfolk and was filled iwth devotion for me, got this state
to which my misdeeds have brought him, wretched that I am!"


Word by word
18. nityam= He who ever;iSTa bandhu janaH= loved his own
kinsfolk;anuvrataH= and was filled with devotion;maam= for me;gataH= got;imaam= this;avasthaam= state;durnayaiH= to which the
misdeeds;mama= of me;(have brought him);wretched that I am !




19Yuddha Kanda 49.19
सुरुष्टेन अपि वीरेण लक्ष्मणेना न संस्मरे |परुषम् विप्रियम् वा अपि श्रावितम् न कदाचन
suruṣṭena api vīreṇa lakṣmaṇenā na saṃsmare |paruṣam vipriyam vā api śrāvitam na kadācana
"I do not remember to have heard any harsh or hateful words from that valiant
Lakshmana, even if he is deeply provoked."


Word by word
19. na samsmare= I do not remember;shraavitam= to have
heard;kadaachana= at any time;paruSam= harsh;vipriyam= and hateful
words;lakSmaNena= by lakshmana;viireNa= the valiant man;suruSTenaapi= even if he is deeply provoked.




20Yuddha Kanda 49.20
विससर्ज एक वेगेन पन्च बाण शतानि यः |इष्व् अस्त्रेष्व् अधिकस् तस्मात् कार्तवीर्याच् च लक्ष्मणः
visasarja eka vegena panca bāṇa śatāni yaḥ |iṣv astreṣv adhikas tasmāt kārtavīryāc ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
"Lakshmana, who was able to loose five hundred arrows in one shot, was surpassing
kartavirya himself in the science of archery."


Word by word
20. yaH= he who;visasarja= was able to loose;paNcha
baaNa shataani= five hundred arrows;eka vegena= in one shot;tasmaat=
such;lakSmaNaH= Lakshmana;adhikaH= was surpassing;kaartaviiryaat
cha= Kartavirya himself;iSvastreSu= in the science of archery.




21Yuddha Kanda 49.21
अस्त्रैर् अस्त्राणि यो हन्यात् शक्रस्य अपि महात्मनः |सो अयम् उर्व्याम्हतह् शेते महा अर्ह शयन उचितः
astrair astrāṇi yo hanyāt śakrasya api mahātmanaḥ |so ayam urvyāmhatah śete mahā arha śayana ucitaḥ
"This Lakshmana, who was accustomed to a rich couch and who by his arrows severe the
weapons the mighty Indra the Lord of celestials, is lying slain on the ground."


Word by word
21. saH ayam= this Lakshmana;yaH= who;mahaarha
shayanochitaH= was accustomed to a rich couch;astraiH= and who by his arrows;hanyaat= severe;astraanapi= the weapons even;shakrasya= of Indra;mahaatmanaH= the mighty one;shete= is lying;hataH= slain;urvyaam= on the earth.




22Yuddha Kanda 49.22
तच् च मिथ्या प्रलप्तम् माम् प्रधक्ष्यति न संशयः |यन् मया न कृतो राजा राक्षसानाम् विभीषणः
tac ca mithyā pralaptam mām pradhakṣyati na saṃśayaḥ |yan mayā na kṛto rājā rākṣasānām vibhīṣaṇaḥ
"Those vain words uttered by me, will ndoubtedly consume me since I have not made
Vibhishana the king of demons."


Word by word
22. mithyaa pralaptam= (Those) vain words;na samshayaH=
without doubt;pradhakSyati= will consume;maam= me;yat tat= since;vibhiiSaNaH= Vibhishana;na kR^itaH= was not made;rajaa= the king;raakSasaanaam= of demons;mayaa= by me.




23Yuddha Kanda 49.23
अस्मिन् मुहूर्ते सुग्रीव प्रतियातुम् इतो अर्हसि |मत्वा हीनम् मया राजन् रावणो अभिद्रवेद् बली
asmin muhūrte sugrīva pratiyātum ito arhasi |matvā hīnam mayā rājan rāvaṇo abhidraved balī
"O, Sugreeva! You ought to return at once from here since knowing that you are
bereft of my support, Ravana will overcome you, O king!"


Word by word
23. sugriiva= O;Sugreeva!;arhasi= you ought;pratiyaatum= to return;asmin= this;muhuurte= moment;itaH= from here;(since);matvaa= knowing (you are);hiinam= without;mayaa= me;raavanaH= Ravana;abhibhaviSyat= will overcome (you);raajan= O;king!.




24Yuddha Kanda 49.24
अन्गदम् तु पुरस् कृत्य ससैन्यह् ससुहृज् जनः |सागरम् तर सुग्रीव पुनस् तेन एव सेतुना
angadam tu puras kṛtya sasainyah sasuhṛj janaḥ |sāgaram tara sugrīva punas tena eva setunā
"O, Sugreeva! Recross the sea with your army, keeping Angada in front and with your
followers, Nila and Nala."


Word by word
24. sugriiva= O;Sugreeva!;tara= re-cross;samudram= the sea;sasainyam= with you army;puraskR^itya= keeping
Angada in front;aNgadam puraskR^itya= keeping Angada in front;parichchhadam=
with your followers;niilena cha= Nila;nalenacha= and Nala.




25Yuddha Kanda 49.25
कृतम् हनुमता कार्यम् यद् अन्यैर् दुष्करम् रणे |ऋक्ष राजेन तुष्यामि गो लान्गूल अधिपेन च
kṛtam hanumatā kāryam yad anyair duṣkaram raṇe |ṛkṣa rājena tuṣyāmi go lāngūla adhipena ca
"I am fully satisfied by the great military exploit, done by Jambavan the king of
Bears and the General of the Monkeys, which was impossible to any other in battle."


Word by word
25. tuSyaami= I am fully satisfied;sumahat= by the great;karma= military exploit;kR^itam hi= acccomplished indeed;R^ikSarajena= by Jambavan;the king of Bears;golaaNguuladhipena= and the

to any other;raNe= in battle.




26Yuddha Kanda 49.26
अन्गदेन कृतम् कर्म मैन्देन द्विविदेन च |युद्धम् केसरिणा सम्ख्ये घोरम् सम्पातिना कृतम्
angadena kṛtam karma maindena dvividena ca |yuddham kesariṇā samkhye ghoram sampātinā kṛtam
"A great act was done by Angada, Mainda and Dvivida. A terrible combat was done by
Kesari and Sampati in the battle-field."


Word by word
26. karma= A (great) act;kR^itam= was done;aN^gadena= by Angada;maindena= Mainda;dvividena= and Dvivida;ghoram= A terrible;yuddham= combat;kR^itam= was done;kesariNaa= by Kesari;sampaatinaa= and Sampati;samkhye= in the
battle-field.




27Yuddha Kanda 49.27
गवयेन गव अक्षेण शरभेण गजेन च |अन्यैश् च हरिभिर् युद्धम् मद् आर्थे त्यक्त जीवितैः
gavayena gava akṣeṇa śarabheṇa gajena ca |anyaiś ca haribhir yuddham mad ārthe tyakta jīvitaiḥ
"By Gavaya, Gavaksha, Sharabha, Gaja and other monkeys, who are willing to sacrifice
their lives for me, the battle was carried on."


Word by word
27. gavayena= by Gavaya;gavaakSeNa= Gavaksha;sharabheNa= Sharabha;gajena= Gaja;anyaiH= and other;haribhishcha= mokeys;tyakta jiivitaiH= who are willing to sacrifice their
lives;madarthe= for me;yuddham= the battle was carried on.




28Yuddha Kanda 49.28
न च अतिक्रमितुम् शक्यम् दैवम् सुग्रीव मानुषैः |यत् तु शक्यम् वयस्येन सुहृदा वा परम् तपकृतम् सुग्रीव तत् सर्वम् भवता अधर्म भीरुणा
na ca atikramitum śakyam daivam sugrīva mānuṣaiḥ |yat tu śakyam vayasyena suhṛdā vā param tapakṛtam sugrīva tat sarvam bhavatā adharma bhīruṇā
"O, Sugreeva! It is not possible for mortals to avoid their destiny. O, Sugreeva the
tormentat of enemies! Fearing to fail in your duty, you have done all that which a friend and a
comrade could do."


Word by word
28. sugriiva= O;Sugreeva!;na cha shakyam= It is not
possible;maanushaiH= for mortals;atikramitum= to avoid;daivam=
their destiny;sugriiva= O;Sugreeva;paramtapa= the tormentator of enemies!;dharma bhiiruNaa= fearing to fail in your duty;kR^itam= it was done;tvayaa= by you;sarvam= all;tat= that;yatha= which
suhR^idaa = a friend;vayasyena= and a comrade;shakyam= could do.




29Yuddha Kanda 49.29
मित्र कार्यम् कृतम् इदम् भवद्भिर् वानर ऋषभाःअनुज्नाता मया सर्वे यथा इष्टम् गन्तुम् अर्हथ
mitra kāryam kṛtam idam bhavadbhir vānara ṛṣabhāḥanujnātā mayā sarve yathā iṣṭam gantum arhatha
"O. foremost of Monkyes! You have accomplished all this due to your friendship. I
take leave of you all; go where it seems best to you!"


Word by word
29. vaanararSabhaaH= O;foremost of monkeys!;idam= this;mitra kaaryam= friendly act;kR^itam= has been done;bharadbhiH= by
you;sarve= all of you;anujJNaataaH= are being permitted mayaa = by me;arhatha= you ought;gantum= to go;yatheSTam= where it seems best to
you!.




30Yuddha Kanda 49.30
शुश्रुवुस् तस्य ते सर्वे वानराह् परिदेवितम्वर्तयाम् चक्रुर् अश्रूणि नेत्रैह् कृष्ण इतर ईक्षणाः
śuśruvus tasya te sarve vānarāh paridevitamvartayām cakrur aśrūṇi netraih kṛṣṇa itara īkṣaṇāḥ
All the tawny eyed monkeys, who heard Rama's lament thus, allowed tears to fall from
their eyes.


Word by word
30. sarve= all;vaanaraaH= the monkeys;kR^iSNatarekSaNaaH= the tawny eyed one;ye= who;shushruvaH= heard;tasya= that Rama's;paridevitam= lamentation;ashruuNi vartayaam
chakrire= allowed tears to fall netraiH = from their eyes.




31Yuddha Kanda 49.31
ततः सर्वाण्य् अनीकानि स्थापयित्वा विभीषणःआजगाम गदा पाणिस् त्वरितो यत्र राघवः
tataḥ sarvāṇy anīkāni sthāpayitvā vibhīṣaṇaḥājagāma gadā pāṇis tvarito yatra rāghavaḥ
Meanwhile, Vibhishana having established order in all the ranks, with mace in his
hand, came quickly to Rama.


Word by word
31. tataH= thereafter;vibhiiSaNaH= Vibhishana;sthaapayitvaa= having establied order;sarvaaNi= in all;a niikaani=
the ranks;gadaa paaNih= mace in his land;aajagaama= come;tvaritam=
quickly;yatra= where;raaghava= Rama (was then).




32Yuddha Kanda 49.32
तम् दृष्ट्वा त्वरितम् यान्तम् नील अन्जन चय उपमम्वानरा दुद्रुवुह् सर्वे मन्यमानास् तु रावणिम्
tam dṛṣṭvā tvaritam yāntam nīla anjana caya upamamvānarā dudruvuh sarve manyamānās tu rāvaṇim
Seeing him, who resembled a mass of collyrium, hastening towards them thus, all the
monkeys thinking him to be Indrajit the son of Ravana, fled away.


Word by word
32. dR^iSTvaa= seeing;tam= him;niilaaNjana
chayopamam= who resembled a mass of collyrium;tvaritam yaantam= hastening;
(towards them thus);sarve= all;vaanaraaH= the monkeys;manyamaanaaH= thinking;(him) raavaNim= to be Indrajit;the son of Ravana;dudruvuH= fled
away.



    
  
  Returning to consciousness, Rama laments over the plight of Lakshmana, who was lying unconscious. The foremost of monkeys too were plunged in grief and despondency on seeing Rama lamenting as aforesaid. In the meantime, Vibhishana approaches Rama and the monkeys flee away, mistaking him as Indrajit.

1Yuddha Kanda 51.1
तेषाम् सुतुमुलम् शब्दम् वानराणाम् तरस्विनाम् |नर्दताम् राक्षसैह् सार्धम् तदा शुश्राव रावणः
teṣām sutumulam śabdam vānarāṇām tarasvinām |nardatām rākṣasaih sārdham tadā śuśrāva rāvaṇaḥ
That tumultuous sound, set up by the monkeys who were full of martial ardour,
arrested the attention of Ravana and his demons.


Word by word
1. tadaa= then;raavaNaH= Ravana;raakSasaiH
saardham= along with (other) demons;shushraava= heard;tumulam= the
tumultuous;shabdam= sound;teSaam vaanaraaNaam= of those monkes;mahaujasaam= who were full of martial ardour;nardataam= and who were making a
roaring sound.




2Yuddha Kanda 51.2
स्निग्ध गम्भीर निर्घोषम् श्रुत्वा स निनदम् भृशम् |सचिवानाम् ततस् तेषाम् मध्ये वचनम् अब्रवीत्
snigdha gambhīra nirghoṣam śrutvā sa ninadam bhṛśam |sacivānām tatas teṣām madhye vacanam abravīt
Hearing that mighty clamour, sounding smooth and deep, Ravana spoke to his ministers
who surrounded him.


Word by word
2. shrutvaa= hearing;bhR^isham= the mighty;ninadam= clamour;snighdha gambhiira nirghoSam= in a smooth and deep sound;saH= that Ravana;tataH= then;abraviit= spoke;vachanam=
(the following) words;madhye= in the midst;teshaam sachivaanaam= of those
ministers.




3Yuddha Kanda 51.3
यथा असौ सम्प्रहृष्टानाम् वानराणाम् समुत्थितः |बहूनाम् सुमहान् नादो मेघानाम् इव गर्जताम्
yathā asau samprahṛṣṭānām vānarāṇām samutthitaḥ |bahūnām sumahān nādo meghānām iva garjatām
"A great uproar, resembling the rumbling of clouds, has arisen from that horde of
rejoiced monkeys. Undoubtedly their joy is great, their mighty roars are agitating the briny ocean
itself.


Word by word

clouds;eteSaam= (that) their;priitiH= happiness;mahatii= is
immense;na samshayaH= there is no doubt;atra= in this matter;tathaahi= for instance;lavaNaarNavaH= the briney ocean;chukSubhe=
is agitated;vipulaiH naadaiH= by the loud noises.




4Yuddha Kanda 51.4
व्यक्तम् सुमहती प्रीतिर् एतेषाम् न अत्र संशयः |तथा हि विपुलैर् नादैश् चुक्षुभे वरुण आलयः
vyaktam sumahatī prītir eteṣām na atra saṃśayaḥ |tathā hi vipulair nādaiś cukṣubhe varuṇa ālayaḥ
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


5Yuddha Kanda 51.5
तौ तु बद्धौ शरैस् तीष्क्णैर् भ्रातरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ |अयम् च सुमहान् नादह् शन्काम् जनयति इव मे
tau tu baddhau śarais tīṣkṇair bhrātarau rāma lakṣmaṇau |ayam ca sumahān nādah śankām janayati iva me
"Those two brothers Rama and Lakshmana were tied by sharp arrows. This sound of a
great magnitude being heard by me, is begetting an apprehension in me."


Word by word

6Yuddha Kanda 51.6
एवम् च वचनम् च उक्त्वा मन्त्रिणो राक्षस ईश्वरः |उवाच नैरृतांस् तत्र समीप परिवर्तिनः
evam ca vacanam ca uktvā mantriṇo rākṣasa īśvaraḥ |uvāca nairṛtāṃs tatra samīpa parivartinaḥ
Having spoken thus to his ministers, Ravana the Lord of Demons said to his demons
who stood round him there (as follows)

7Yuddha Kanda 51.7
ज्नायताम् तूर्णम् एतषाम् सर्वेषाम् वन चारिणाम् |शोक काले समुत्पन्ने हर्ष कारणम् उत्थितम्
jnāyatām tūrṇam etaṣām sarveṣām vana cāriṇām |śoka kāle samutpanne harṣa kāraṇam utthitam
"You immediately discover from what cause this general rejoicing among all these
monkeys coming for the their present grievous situation!'

7. jJNaayataam= It is to be known;tuurNam= immediately;harSa kaaraNam= the cause of joy;utthitam= coming forth;sarveSaam=

8Yuddha Kanda 51.8
तथा उक्तास् तेन सम्भ्रान्ताह् प्राकारम् अधिरुह्य ते |ददृशुह् पालिताम् सेनाम् सुग्रीवेण महात्मना
tathā uktās tena sambhrāntāh prākāram adhiruhya te |dadṛśuh pālitām senām sugrīveṇa mahātmanā
Thus commanded by Ravana, they mounted the rampart very briskly and saw the army
lead by the high-souled Sugreeva and also the highly fortunate Rama and Lakshmana who were relieved
of the terrific shackle of arrow a and risen up together. All the demons felt desponded on seeing
it.

तौ च मुक्तौ सुघोरेण शर बन्धेन राघवौ |समुत्थितौ महा भागौ विषेदुह् प्रेक्ष्य राक्षसाः

10Yuddha Kanda 51.10
सम्त्रस्त हृदया सर्वे प्राकाराद् अवरुह्य ते |विवर्ण रक्षनाः घोरा राक्षस इन्द्रम् उपस्थिताः
samtrasta hṛdayā sarve prākārād avaruhya te |vivarṇa rakṣanāḥ ghorā rākṣasa indram upasthitāḥ
With their hearts trembling with fear and faces turning pale, all those terrific

तद् अप्रियम् दीन मुखा रावणस्य निशा चराः |कृत्स्नम् निवेदयाम् आसुर् यथावद् वाक्य कोविदाः

यौ ताव् इन्द्रजिता युद्धे भ्रातरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ |निबद्धौ शर बन्धेन निष्प्रकम्प भुजौ कृतौ

vimuktau śara bandhena tau dṛśyete raṇa ajire |pāśān iva gajāu cittvā gaja indra sama vikramau
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


14Yuddha Kanda 51.14
तत् श्रुत्वा वचनम् तेषाम् राक्षस इन्द्रो महा बलः |चिन्ता शोक समाक्रान्तो विषण्ण वदनो अब्रवीत्
tat śrutvā vacanam teṣām rākṣasa indro mahā balaḥ |cintā śoka samākrānto viṣaṇṇa vadano abravīt
Hearing their words, the might Ravana was filled with anxiety and fury. His face
became pale (and he spoke as follows):

घोरैर् दत्त वरैर् बद्धौ शरैर् आशी विष उमपैः |अमोघैह् सूर्य सम्काशैह् प्रमथ्य इन्द्रजिता युधि
ghorair datta varair baddhau śarair āśī viṣa umapaiḥ |amoghaih sūrya samkāśaih pramathya indrajitā yudhi
"If my adversaries, having thus been bound by Indrajit are freed, despite their

तम् अस्त्र बन्धम् आसाद्य यदि मुक्तौ रिपू मम |संशयस्थम् इदम् सर्वम् अनुपश्याम्य् अहम् बलम्

The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


17Yuddha Kanda 51.17
निष्फलाह् खलु सम्वृत्ताह् शरा वासुकि तेजसः |आदत्तम् यैस् तु सम्ग्रामे रिपूणाम् मम जीवितम्
niṣphalāh khalu samvṛttāh śarā vāsuki tejasaḥ |ādattam yais tu samgrāme ripūṇām mama jīvitam
"Those very arrows, bright as fire, which in battle have taken the life of my

fire;yaiH= which;samgraame= in battle;aadattam= have taken;jiivitam= the life;ripuuNaam= of my enemies;samvR^ittaaH khalm=
have indeed been rendered;niSphalaaH= void.




18Yuddha Kanda 51.18
एवम् उक्त्वा तु सम्क्रुद्धो निश्वसन्न् उरगो यथा |अब्रवीद् रक्षसाम् मध्ये धूम्र अक्षम् नाम राकसम्
evam uktvā tu samkruddho niśvasann urago yathā |abravīd rakṣasām madhye dhūmra akṣam nāma rākasam

resembling a flood, protected by the arms of Rama.

  Hearing the rejoicing cries of the monkeys, Ravana asks some demons to discover the cause of that rejoicing. The demons mount the rampart and discover that Rama and Lakshmana have been relieved of the shackle of arrows. They come to Ravana and inform that the two brothers Rama and Lakshmana are alive and appear like two strong elephants in the battle-field. Ravana then calls Dhumraksha, a demon and asks him to go with an army and kill Rama, Lakshmana and the monkeys Dhumraksha along with his army enters the western gate of Lanks where the army-chief Hanuman is stationed. While Dhumraksha advances in the battle-field, he observes several bad omens and feels disturbed.

  Ravana sends Vajradamstra, another demon to kill Rama, Sugreeva and his monkeys. Vajradamstra and his army emerge from the southern gate where Angada, the General of the Monkeys is stationed. The monkeys had a tough fight with the demons. Angada, the leader of the monkeys strikes the terrible strong demons, chopping off their heads.

1Yuddha Kanda 55.1
वज्रदम्र अक्षम् निहतम् श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षस ईश्वरः |बल अध्यक्षम् उवाच इदम् कृत अन्जलिम् उपस्थितम्
vajradamra akṣam nihatam śrutvā rāvaṇo rākṣasa īśvaraḥ |bala adhyakṣam uvāca idam kṛta anjalim upasthitam
Hearing that Vajradamshtra was killed by Angada, Ravana spoke the following words to
the General of his forces who, with joined palms, stood near him.


Word by word
1. shrutvaa= hearing;vajradamSTram= (that) Vajradamshtra;hatam= was killed;vaaliputreNa= by Angada;raavaNaH= Ravana;uvaacha= spoke;idam= these words;upasthitam= to the nearby;balaadhyakSam= army general;kR^itaaN^jalim= who joined his palms in
reverence.




2Yuddha Kanda 55.2
शीघ्रम् निर्यान्तु दुर्धर्षा राक्षसा भीम विक्रमाः |अकम्पनम् पुरस् कृत्य सर्व शस्त्र प्रकोविदम्
śīghram niryāntu durdharṣā rākṣasā bhīma vikramāḥ |akampanam puras kṛtya sarva śastra prakovidam
"Let the invincible demons of irresistible courage go forth soon, with Akampana as
their head, who is skilled in the use of every weapon and missile."


Word by word
2. bhiimavikramaaH= (Let) the invincible;raakSasaaH=
demons;durdharSaaH= of irresistible courage;niryaantu= go forth;shiighram= soon;akampanam= with Akampana;puraskR^itya= in front;sarva shastraastra kovidam= who is skilled in use of every weapon and missile.




3Yuddha Kanda 55.3
एष शास्ता च गोप्ता च नेता च युधि सत्तमः |भूतिकामश्च मे नित्यं नित्यम् च समरप्रियः
eṣa śāstā ca goptā ca netā ca yudhi sattamaḥ |bhūtikāmaśca me nityaṃ nityam ca samarapriyaḥ
"This excellent demon is a chastiser, a protector and a leader in battle. He ever
desired my welfare and always loved war."


Word by word

leader;yudhi= in batle;nityam= ever;me bhuutikaamashcha= desiring
my welfare;samarapriyaH= and loved war;nityam= forever.




4Yuddha Kanda 55.4
एष जेष्यति काकत्थ्सौ सुग्रीवं च महाबलम् |वानरांश्चापरान् घोरान् हनिष्यति न संशयः
eṣa jeṣyati kākatthsau sugrīvaṃ ca mahābalam |vānarāṃścāparān ghorān haniṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
"There is no doubt that he will prove victorious and Rama, Lakshmana, the mighty
Sugreeva and the other terrible monkeys."


Word by word
4. eSaH= He;jeSyati= will prove victorious;haniSyati= and can kill;kaakutsthau= Rama;Lakshmana;mahaabalam=
the mighty;sugriivam= Sugreeva;aparaan= and the other;ghoraan=
terrific;vaanaraan= monkeys;na= there is no;samshayaH= doubt.




5Yuddha Kanda 55.5
परिगृह्य स तामाज्ञाम् रावणस्य महाबलः |बलं सम्प्रेरयामास तदा लघुपराक्रमः
parigṛhya sa tāmājñām rāvaṇasya mahābalaḥ |balaṃ samprerayāmāsa tadā laghuparākramaḥ
Taking that command of Ravana, the mighty Akampana of quick resolution then
mobilized the army.


Word by word
5. parigR^ihya= taking;taam= that;aajJNaam=
command;raavaNasya= of Ravana;mahaabalaH= the mighty;saH=
Akampana;laghuparaakramaH= of quick resolution;tadaa= then;samprerayaamaasa= mobilized;balam= the army.




6Yuddha Kanda 55.6
ततो नानाप्रहरणा भीमाक्षा भीमदर्शनाः |निष्पेतू राक्षसा मुख्या बलाध्यक्षप्रचोदिताः
tato nānāpraharaṇā bhīmākṣā bhīmadarśanāḥ |niṣpetū rākṣasā mukhyā balādhyakṣapracoditāḥ
Those foremost of demons of terrifying appearance, furnished with every kind of
weapon and fearful to look upon, rushed into the fray where their general had dispatched them.


Word by word

had dispatched them.




7Yuddha Kanda 55.7
रथमास्थाय विपुलं तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणम् |मेघाभो मेघवर्णश्च मेघस्वनमहास्वनः
rathamāsthāya vipulaṃ taptakāñcanabhūṣaṇam |meghābho meghavarṇaśca meghasvanamahāsvanaḥ
Then, Akampana of the stature and colour of a cloud, whose voice resembled a
thunder, ascended his great chariot, decorated with fine gold and set out, surrounded by dreadful
demons.


Word by word
7. tadaa= then;akampanaH= Akampana;meghaabhaH=
of the stature of a cloud;meghavarNashcha= of the colour of a cloud;meghasvana

gold;niryaati= and set out;samvR^itaH= surrounded;ghoraiH= by

8Yuddha Kanda 55.8
न हि कम्पयितुम् शक्यह् सुरैऋअपि महा मृधेअकम्पनस् ततस् तेषाम् आदित्य;इव तेजसा
na hi kampayitum śakyah suraiṛapi mahā mṛdheakampanas tatas teṣām āditya;iva tejasā
Even celestials were indeed unable to upset Akampana in a great battle. Hence, among
the demons, he was shining like the sun, by his splendour.


Word by word
8. surairapi= even celestials too;nashakyaH hi= were
indeed unable;kampayitum= to upset;akampanaH= Akampana;mahaamR^idhe= in a great battle;tataH= hence;(he) tejasaa= by his splendour;aadityaH
iva= was resembling the sun;teSaam= among the demons.




9Yuddha Kanda 55.9
तस्य निधावमानस्य सम्रब्धस्य युयुत्सयाअकस्माद् दैन्यम् आगच्चद्द् हयानाम् रथ वाहिनाम्
tasya nidhāvamānasya samrabdhasya yuyutsayāakasmād dainyam āgaccadd hayānām ratha vāhinām
As he sped on his way, hastened and eager to enter the battle, the horses drawing
his chariot were suddenly deprived of their energy.

9. tasya= (As) he;nirdhaava maanasya= sped on his way;samrabdhasya= hastening;yuyutsayaa= and eager to enter the battle;hayaanaam= the horses;rathavaahinaam= drawing his chariot;aagachchhat
dainyam= were deprived of their energy;akasmaat= suddenly.




10Yuddha Kanda 55.10
व्यस्फुरन् नयनम् च अस्य सव्यम् युद्ध अभिनन्दिनःविवर्णो मुख वर्णश् च गद्गदश् च अभवत् स्वरः
vyasphuran nayanam ca asya savyam yuddha abhinandinaḥvivarṇo mukha varṇaś ca gadgadaś ca abhavat svaraḥ
The left eye of Akampana, who delighted in warfare, began to twitch. His countenance
grew pale and his voice trembled.

10. savyam= the left;nayanam= eye;asya= of
Akampana;yudhaabhinandinaH= who delighted in warfare;visphurat= began to

and his voice;abhavat= became;gadgadaH= trembled.




11Yuddha Kanda 55.11
अभवत् सुदिने च अपि दुर्दिने रूक्ष मारुतम्ऊचुह् खगा मृगाह् सर्वे वाचह् क्रूरा भय आवहाः
abhavat sudine ca api durdine rūkṣa mārutamūcuh khagā mṛgāh sarve vācah krūrā bhaya āvahāḥ
At a time of a good day, marked by fine weather, it turned into a day of bad weather
with a bitter wind beginning to blow. Birds and beasts uttered cruel and fearful cries.

12Yuddha Kanda 55.12
स सिम्ह उपचित स्कन्धह् शार्दूल सम विक्रमःतान् उत्पातान् अचिन्त्य एव निर्जगाम रण आजिरम्
sa simha upacita skandhah śārdūla sama vikramaḥtān utpātān acintya eva nirjagāma raṇa ājiram
That demon, who had the shoulders of a lion and the agility of a tiger, disregarding
those portents, rushed towards the battle-field.

13Yuddha Kanda 55.13
तदा निर्गच्चतस् तस्य रक्षसह् सह राक्षसैःबभूव सुमहान् नादह् क्षोभयन्न् इव सागरम्
tadā nirgaccatas tasya rakṣasah saha rākṣasaiḥbabhūva sumahān nādah kṣobhayann iva sāgaram
While Akampana advanced thus with his troops, an immense tumult arose that seemed to
convulse the ocean.


Word by word

along with other demons;nirgachchhataH= went forward;tathaa= thus;sumahaan naadaH= an immense tumult;babhuuva= arose;khhobhayanmivaa=
that seemed to convulse;saagaram= the ocean.




14Yuddha Kanda 55.14
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्ता वानराणाम् महा चमूःद्रुम शैल प्रहरणा योद्धुम् समवतिष्ठत
tena śabdena vitrastā vānarāṇām mahā camūḥdruma śaila praharaṇā yoddhum samavatiṣṭhata
By hearing that clamour of the demons coming for the battle, the huge army of the
monkeys, brandishing trees and rocks, was frightened.

15Yuddha Kanda 55.15
तेषाम् युद्धम् महा रौद्रम् सम्जज्ने कपि रक्षसाम्राम रावणयोऋअर्थे समभित्यक्त जीविनाम्
teṣām yuddham mahā raudram samjajne kapi rakṣasāmrāma rāvaṇayoṛarthe samabhityakta jīvinām
A highly fierce battle ensued between those monkeys and demons, who were ready to
lose their lives for the sake of Rama and Ravana.

and demons;samabhityakta jiivinaam= who were ready to lose their lives;raama

16Yuddha Kanda 55.16
सर्वे ह्य् अतिबलाह् शूराह् सर्वे पर्वत सम्निभाःहरयो राक्षसाश् चैव परस्पर जिघंसवः
sarve hy atibalāh śūrāh sarve parvata samnibhāḥharayo rākṣasāś caiva paraspara jighaṃsavaḥ
All the monkeys and demons, who were willing to kill each other, were very strong
and valiant. All were resembling mountains.

each other;atibalaaH= were very strong;shuuraaH= valiant;sarve=
and all;parvata samnibhaaH= were resembling mountains.




17Yuddha Kanda 55.17
तेषाम् विनर्दाताम् शब्दह् सम्युगे अतितरस्विनाम्शुश्रुवे सुमहान् क्रोधाद् अन्योन्यम् अभिगर्जताम्
teṣām vinardātām śabdah samyuge atitarasvināmśuśruve sumahān krodhād anyonyam abhigarjatām
The tremendous clamour of the aforesaid warriors, yelling in their rage and
strength, making savage cries, were distinctly heard on the battle-field.

were heard;pamyuge= in that combat.




18Yuddha Kanda 55.18
रजसः च अरुण वर्ण आभम् सुभीमम् अभवद् भृशम्उद्धूतम् हरि रक्षोभिः सम्रुरोध दिशो दश
rajasḥ ca aruṇa varṇa ābham subhīmam abhavad bhṛśamuddhūtam hari rakṣobhiḥ samrurodha diśo daśa
A highly terrific dust, in a thick coppery colour, raised by the monkeys and demons
enveloped all the ten quarters.

19Yuddha Kanda 55.19
अन्योन्यम् रजसा तेन कौशेय उद्धूत पाण्डुनासम्वृतानि च भूतानि ददृशुऋन रण अजिरे
anyonyam rajasā tena kauśeya uddhūta pāṇḍunāsamvṛtāni ca bhūtāni dadṛśuṛna raṇa ajire
The combatants, enveloped by that dust, which was whitish like a piece of silk
shaken by the wind, could no longer distinguish each other on the battle-field.

20Yuddha Kanda 55.20
न ध्वजो न पताका वा वर्म वा तुरगो अपि वाआयुधम् स्यन्दनम् वा अपि ददृशे तेन रेणुना
na dhvajo na patākā vā varma vā turago api vāāyudham syandanam vā api dadṛśe tena reṇunā
Neither standard, banner and shield, nor horse, weapon and chariot could be
discerned in that pall of dust.

20. na= neither;dhvajaH= standard;pataakaa vaa= banner;na= nor;charma vaa= shield;turago.api vaa= horse;aayudham= weapon;syandanova api= even chariot;(could be seen);tena= in that;reNunaa= dust.




21Yuddha Kanda 55.21
शब्दसः च सुमहांस् तेषाम् नर्दताम् अभिधावताम्श्रूयते तुमुले युद्धे न रूपाणि चकाशिरे
śabdasḥ ca sumahāṃs teṣām nardatām abhidhāvatāmśrūyate tumule yuddhe na rūpāṇi cakāśire
A great tumultuous clamour, of warriors, making challenging cries and rushing upon
each other, was heard on the battle-field, yet in that confusion, no form was visible.


Word by word
21. sumahaan= a great;tumulaH= tumultuous;shabdashcha= clamour;teSaaM= of warriors;nardataam= making

22Yuddha Kanda 55.22
हरीन् एव सुसम्क्रुद्धा हरयो जघ्नुऋआहवेराक्षसाश् च अपि रक्षांसि निजघ्नुस् तिमिरे तदा
harīn eva susamkruddhā harayo jaghnuṛāhaverākṣasāś ca api rakṣāṃsi nijaghnus timire tadā
In the darkness, the greatly enraged monkeys killed the monkeys themselves and the
demons killed the demons themselves in battle.

23Yuddha Kanda 55.23
ते परांश्च विनिघ्नन्तः स्वांश्च वानरराक्षसाःरुधिरार्द्राम् तदा चक्रुर्म हीं पङ्कानुलेपनाम्

Those monkeys and demons killing other and their own people then made the earth
dampened with blood, anointing its body with mud.


Word by word
23. te= those;vaanara raakSasaaH= monkeys and demons;nighnantaH= killing;paraamshcha= others;svaamshcha= and their own
people;tadaa= then;chakruH= make;mahiim= the earth;rudhiraardraam= dampened with blood;paNkaanulepanaam= anointing its body with
mud.




24Yuddha Kanda 55.24
ततस् तु रुधिर ओघेण सिक्तम् व्यपगतम् रजःशरीर शव सम्कीर्णा बभूव च वसुम् धरा

Under the stream of blood being sprinkled, the dust was laid, revealing the earth
covered with bodies and corpses.

25Yuddha Kanda 55.25
द्रुम शक्ति शिला प्रासैऋगदा परिघ तोमरैःहरयो राक्षसास् तूर्णम् जघ्नुऋअन्योन्यम् ओजसा
druma śakti śilā prāsaiṛgadā parigha tomaraiḥharayo rākṣasās tūrṇam jaghnuṛanyonyam ojasā
The demons and the monkeys vigorously struck each other swiftly with blows from
trees, spears, maces, javelins, stones, bars and picks.

26Yuddha Kanda 55.26
बाहुभिः परिघा आकारैऋयुध्यन्तह् पर्वत उपमाःहरयो भीम कर्माणो राक्षसान् जघ्नुऋआहवे

The monkeys of dreadful deeds, resembling mountains, fighting with their arms

अकम्पनः सुसंक्रुद्धो राक्षसानां चमूपतिःसंहर्षयति तान्सर्वान्राक्षसान् भीमविक्रमान्

हरयस् त्व् अपि रक्षांसि महा द्रुम महा अश्मभिःविदारयन्त्य् अभिक्रम्य शस्त्राण्य् आच्चिद्य वीर्यतः

एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे वीरा हरयह् कुमुदो नलःमैन्दसः च परम क्रुद्धश् चक्रुऋवेगम् अनुत्तमम्
etasminn antare vīrā harayah kumudo nalaḥmaindasḥ ca parama kruddhaś cakruṛvegam anuttamam
Meanwhile Kumuda, Nala and Mainda the courageous monkeys in an outburst of anger,

कदनम् सुमह चक्रुर् लीलया हरि यूथपाः |ममन्थू राक्षसान् सर्वे नानाप्रहरणैर्भृशम्

  Ravana next sends Akampana for the battle. As Akampana along with his army sets out for the war, he visualized various bad portents. A deadly conflict ensued between monkeys and demons. Kumuda, Nala and Mainda the chiefs of monkeys creates a great carnage among demons.

1Yuddha Kanda 57.1
अकम्पन वधम् श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धो वै राक्षस ईश्वरः |किंचिद् दीन मुखश् च अपि सचिवांस् तान् उदैक्षत
akampana vadham śrutvā kruddho vai rākṣasa īśvaraḥ |kiṃcid dīna mukhaś ca api sacivāṃs tān udaikṣata
Hearing of Akampana's killing, Ravana the Lord of demons, with a little depressed
face, was enraged and looked towards his ministers.


Word by word
1. shrutvaa= hearing;akampana vadham= about the killing
of Akampana;raakSaseshvaraH= Ravana the Lord of demons;kruddhaH= was enraged;kimchit diinamukhaH cha api= had a little depressed face;udaikSata= and
looked;taan sachivaan= towards those ministers.




2Yuddha Kanda 57.2
स तु ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तम् तु मन्त्रिभिह् सम्विचार्य च |ततस्तु रावणः पूर्वदिवसे राक्षसाधिपःपुरीम् परिययौ लन्काम् सर्वान् गुल्मान् अवेक्षितुम्
sa tu dhyātvā muhūrtam tu mantribhih samvicārya ca |tatastu rāvaṇaḥ pūrvadivase rākṣasādhipaḥpurīm pariyayau lankām sarvān gulmān avekṣitum
Having reflected awhile and deliberated with his ministers, Ravana the king of
Demons then passed that forenoon in inspecting his defenses in the City of Lanka.


Word by word
2. dhyaatvaa= having reflected;muhuurtam= a while;samvichaarya= and deliberated;mantribhiH= with his ministers;saH
raavaNaH= that Ravana;raakSasaadhipaH= the king of Demons;tataH= then;yayau= went;laN^kaam puriim= to the City of Lanka;avekSitum= to
inspect;sarvagulmaan= all his defenses;puurvadivasa= in the forenoon.




3Yuddha Kanda 57.3
ताम् राक्षस गणैर् गुप्ताम् गुल्मैर् बहुभिर् आवृताम्ददर्श नगरीम् लन्काम् पताका ध्वज मालिनीम्
tām rākṣasa gaṇair guptām gulmair bahubhir āvṛtāmdadarśa nagarīm lankām patākā dhvaja mālinīm
The king Ravana saw that City, guarded by groups of demons, filled with innumerable
troops and decorated with banners and flags.


Word by word

nagariim= that city;guptaam= protected;taam raakSasagaNaiH= by those
groups of demons;aavR^itaam= and surrounded;bahubhiH= by many;gulmaiH= bodies of troops;pataaka dhvajamaaliniim= decorated with banners and
flags.




4Yuddha Kanda 57.4
रुद्धाम् तु नगरीम् दृष्ट्वा रावणो राक्षस ईश्वरःउवाच अमर्षितह् काले प्रहस्तम् युद्ध कोविदम्
ruddhām tu nagarīm dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇo rākṣasa īśvaraḥuvāca amarṣitah kāle prahastam yuddha kovidam
Seeing Lanka besieged, Ravana the Lord of Demons spoke as follows to Prahasta who
was skilled in war-fare and who wished well of him even at a critical time.


Word by word

kovidam= who was skilled in war-fare;aatmahitam= and who wished well of him;kaale= even at a critical time.




5Yuddha Kanda 57.5
पुरस्य उपनिविष्टस्य सहसा पीडितस्य हन अन्यम् युद्धात् प्रपश्यामि मोक्षम् युद्ध विशारद
purasya upaniviṣṭasya sahasā pīḍitasya hana anyam yuddhāt prapaśyāmi mokṣam yuddha viśārada
"O, Prahasta the proficient in war-free! I do not see any other deliverance than a

Word by word
5. yuddha vishaarada= O;the proficient one in war-free!;na
prapashyaami= I do not see;anyam= any other;mokSam= deliverance;yuddhaat= than a battle;purasya= for this City;upaniviSTasya= which
is beseiged;sahasaa= suddenly;piiDitasya= and being devastated.




6Yuddha Kanda 57.6
अहम् वा कुम्भ कर्णो वा त्वम् वा सेना पतिर् ममइन्द्रजिद् वा निकुम्भो वा वहेयुर् भारम् ईदृशम्
aham vā kumbha karṇo vā tvam vā senā patir mamaindrajid vā nikumbho vā vaheyur bhāram īdṛśam
"Either myself or Kumbhakarna or yourself my army-chief or Indrajit or Nikumbha and

vaa= or Indrajit;nikumbho vaa= or Nikumbha;vaheyuH= can bear;iidR^isham= such;bhaaram= a burden.




7Yuddha Kanda 57.7
स त्वम् बलम् इतह् शीघ्रम् आदाय परिगृह्य चविजयाय अभिनिर्याहि यत्र सर्वे वन ओकसः
sa tvam balam itah śīghram ādāya parigṛhya cavijayāya abhiniryāhi yatra sarve vana okasaḥ
"For that reason, taking a company of warriors, you quickly place yourself in their
midst and set forth in order to triumph over all those monkeys."

8Yuddha Kanda 57.8
निर्याणाद् एव ते नूनम् चपला हरि वाहिनीनर्दताम् राक्षस इन्द्राणाम् श्रुत्वा नादम् द्रविष्यति
niryāṇād eva te nūnam capalā hari vāhinīnardatām rākṣasa indrāṇām śrutvā nādam draviṣyati
"Unsettled in no time on knowing your decision to enter the battle-field, the army
of monkeys will run away on hearing the raring sound of the leaders of demons."

9Yuddha Kanda 57.9
चपला ह्य् अविनीताश् च चल चित्ताश् च वानराःन सहिष्यन्ति ते नादम् सिम्ह नादम् इव द्विपाः
capalā hy avinītāś ca cala cittāś ca vānarāḥna sahiṣyanti te nādam simha nādam iva dvipāḥ
"The monkeys are unsteady, mis-behaved and fickle-minded. They do not tolerate your

10Yuddha Kanda 57.10
विद्रुते च बले तस्मिन् रामह् सौमित्रिणा सहअवशस्ते निरालम्बह् प्रहस्त वशम् एष्यति
vidrute ca bale tasmin rāmah saumitriṇā sahaavaśaste nirālambah prahasta vaśam eṣyati
"O, Prahasta! As that army takes to its heels, Rama along with Lakshmana being
supportless, will fall into your power though unwillingly."

11Yuddha Kanda 57.11
आपत् संशयिता श्रेयो न अत्र निह्संशयी कृताप्रतिलोम अनुलोमम् वा यद् वा नो मन्यसे हितम्
āpat saṃśayitā śreyo na atra nihsaṃśayī kṛtāpratiloma anulomam vā yad vā no manyase hitam
"A skeptical misfortune is preferable to one that is certain! Whether it is
unpleasing to hear or not, say what you consider as an advantage to us."

12Yuddha Kanda 57.12
रावणेन एवम् उक्तस् तु प्रहस्तो वाहिनी पतिःराक्षस इन्द्रम् उवाच इदम् असुर इन्द्रम् इव उशना
rāvaṇena evam uktas tu prahasto vāhinī patiḥrākṣasa indram uvāca idam asura indram iva uśanā
Hearing the words of Ravana, Prahasta the Army-General spoke the following words to
Ravana, like Ushana the preceptor of demons would speak to Bali, the king of demons.

13Yuddha Kanda 57.13
राजन् मन्त्रित पूर्वम् नह् कुशलैह् सह मन्त्रिभिःविवादसः च अपि नो वृत्तह् समवेक्ष्य परस्परम्
rājan mantrita pūrvam nah kuśalaih saha mantribhiḥvivādasḥ ca api no vṛttah samavekṣya parasparam
O, king! Formerly, we deliberated this matter with our wise ministers and, after
having a good dialogue with each other, a disagreement arose between us."

deliberated;naH= by us;mantribhiH saha= along with ministers;kushalaiH= who were skilful;samavekSya= having observed attentively;parasparam= with one another;vivaadashcha= a disagreement;vR^ittaH=

14Yuddha Kanda 57.14
प्रदानेन तु सीतायाह् श्रेयो व्यवसितम् मयाअप्रदाने पुनर् युद्धम् दृष्टम् एतत् तथैव नः
pradānena tu sītāyāh śreyo vyavasitam mayāapradāne punar yuddham dṛṣṭam etat tathaiva naḥ
"To return Seetha was what I considered preferable. Not to do so meant war; we

15Yuddha Kanda 57.15
सो अहम् दानैश् च मानैश् च सततम् पूजितस् त्वयासान्त्वैसः च विविधैह् काले किम् न कुर्याम् प्रियम् तव

"I have ever been honoured by you at appropriate times by gifts, felicitations and

16Yuddha Kanda 57.16
न हि मे जीवितम् रक्ष्यम् पुत्र दार धनानि वात्वम् पश्य माम् जुहूषन्तम् त्वद् अर्थे जीवितम् युधि

"Neither wives nor sons nor riches are going to be spared by me. See you me,

17Yuddha Kanda 57.17
एवम् उक्त्वा तु भर्तारम् रावणम् वाहिनी पतिःउवाचेदम् बलाध्यक्षान् प्रहस्तह् पुरतः स्थितान्
evam uktvā tu bhartāram rāvaṇam vāhinī patiḥuvācedam balādhyakṣān prahastah purataḥ sthitān
Having spoken thus to Lord Ravana, the General Prahasta said to his leading officers
