1Yuddha Kanda 93.1
स प्रविश्य सभान् राजा दीनः परमदुःखितः |निषसादासने मुख्ये सिन्हः क्रुद्ध इव श्वसन्
sa praviśya sabhān rājā dīnaḥ paramaduḥkhitaḥ |niṣasādāsane mukhye sinhaḥ kruddha iva śvasan
That king, who was dejected and very much distressed, having entered the
ssembly-hall, sat on his pre-eminent seat, snorting like a lion.


Word by word
1. saH raajaa= that king;diinaH= who was dejected;parama duHkhitaH= and very much distressed;sabhaam pravishya= having entered
the assembly-hall;niShasaada= sat;mukhya aasane= on his pre-eminent seat;shvasan= snorting;simhaH iva= like a lion.




2Yuddha Kanda 93.2
अब्रवीच्च तदा सर्वान्बलमुख्यान्महाबलः |रावणः प्रांजलीन्वाक्यं पुत्रव्यसनकर्शितः
abravīcca tadā sarvānbalamukhyānmahābalaḥ |rāvaṇaḥ prāṃjalīnvākyaṃ putravyasanakarśitaḥ
That mighty Ravana, who was emaciated for his son's death, having joined both his
palms in salutation, spoke the following words all those chiefs of army:


Word by word
2. saH mahaabalaH raavaNaH= that mighty Ravana;putra vyasana
karshitaH= who was emaciated with is son's death;praajJNaliH= having joined both
his palms in salutation;abraviichcha= spoke;vaakyam= the following words;taan sarvaan= to all those;balamukhyaan= chiefs of his army.




3Yuddha Kanda 93.3
सर्वे भवन्तः सर्वेण हस्त्यश्वेन समावृताः |निर्यान्तु रथसंघैश्च पादातैश्चोपशोभिताः
sarve bhavantaḥ sarveṇa hastyaśvena samāvṛtāḥ |niryāntu rathasaṃghaiśca pādātaiścopaśobhitāḥ
"Surrounded by the entire elephants and horses, as also graced with columns of
chariots and foot-soldiers, all of you march forward."


Word by word
3. samaavR^itaaH= surrounded by;sarvaNa= all;hastyashvena= the elephants and horses;upashobhitaaH= as also graced with;ratha samghaishcha= columns of chariots;paadataishcha= and foot-soldiers;sarve bhavantaH= all of you;niryaantu= march forward.




4Yuddha Kanda 93.4
एकन् रामं परिक्षिप्य समरे हन्तुमर्हथ |प्रहृष्टा शरवर्षेण प्रावृट्काल इवाम्बुदाः
ekan rāmaṃ parikṣipya samare hantumarhatha |prahṛṣṭā śaravarṣeṇa prāvṛṭkāla ivāmbudāḥ
"Encircling Rama alone, you have to kill him, by showering streams of arrows upon
him, even as clouds pour showers during the rainy season."


Word by word
4. pariShipya= encircling;raamam= Rama;ekam=
alone;arhatha= you ought;hantum= to kill (him);varShantaH= by
showering;shara varShaaNi= streams of arrows;ambudaaH iva= even as clouds;(pour showers) praavR^iTkaale= during the rainy season.




5Yuddha Kanda 93.5
अथ वाहन् शरैर्तीष्क्णैर्भिन्नगात्रं महारणे |भवद्भिः श्वो निहन्तास्मि रामन् लोकस्य पश्यतः
atha vāhan śarairtīṣkṇairbhinnagātraṃ mahāraṇe |bhavadbhiḥ śvo nihantāsmi rāman lokasya paśyataḥ
"Or I shall kill Rama, while the world is witnessing it tomorrow, once his limbs are
torn by you with your sharp arrows in the great battle."


Word by word
5. bhinna gaatram= once his limbs are torn;bharadbhiH= by
you;tiiikShNaiH sharaiH= with your sharp arrows;mahaahave= in the great
battle;aham= I;nihantaasmi= shall kill;raamam= Rama;lokasya= while the world;pashyaataH= is witnessing it;shvaH=
tomorrow.




6Yuddha Kanda 93.6
इत्येवन् राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वाक्यमादाय राक्षसाः |निर्ययुस्ते रथैः शीघ्रं नागानीकैश्च सन्वृताः
ityevan rākṣasendrasya vākyamādāya rākṣasāḥ |niryayuste rathaiḥ śīghraṃ nāgānīkaiśca sanvṛtāḥ
Having heard those words of Ravana, those demons sallied forth for the battle, along
with various kinds of armies and speedy chariots.


Word by word
6. aadaaya= having grasped;etat= these;vaakyam= words;raakShasendrasya= of Ravana;te raakShasaaH= those demons;niryayuH= sallied forth;samyutaaH= along with;naanaaniikaishcha=
the various kinds of armies;shiighraiH rathaiH= and speedy chariots.




7Yuddha Kanda 93.7
परिघान् पट्टिशांश्चैव शरखड्गपरश्वधान् |शरीरान्तकरान् सर्वे चिक्षिपुर्वानरान् प्रतिवानराश्च द्रुमान् शैलान् राक्षसान् प्रति चिक्षिपुः
parighān paṭṭiśāṃścaiva śarakhaḍgaparaśvadhān |śarīrāntakarān sarve cikṣipurvānarān prativānarāśca drumān śailān rākṣasān prati cikṣipuḥ
All those demons hurled iron clubs, sharp-edged spikes, arrows, swords and axes
capable of destroying the life. The monkeys too hurled trees and mountains towards the demons.


Word by word
7. sarve= all those demons;chikShipuH= hurled;parighaan= iron clubs;paTTishaamshchaiva= sharp-edged pikes;sharakhaDga
parashvadhaan= arrows;swords and axes;shariiraantakaan= capable of destroying the
life;vaanaraashcha= the monkeys too;chikShipaH= hurled;drumaan=
trees;shailaan= and mountains;raakShasaan prati= towards the demons.




8Yuddha Kanda 93.8
स संग्रामो महाभीमः सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रतिरक्षसान् वानराणान् च तुमुलः समपद्यत
sa saṃgrāmo mahābhīmaḥ sūryasyodayanaṃ pratirakṣasān vānarāṇān ca tumulaḥ samapadyata
Towards sun-rise, that very terrific battle became tumultuous between demons and
monkeys.


Word by word
8. suuryasya udayanam prati= towards sun-rise;saH
mahaabhiimaH= that very terrific;samgraamaH= battle;samapadyata=
became;tumulaH= tumultuous;rakShasaam vaanaraaNaam cha= between demons and
monkeys.




9Yuddha Kanda 93.9
ते गदाभिर्विचित्राभिः प्रासैः खड्गैः परश्वधैःअन्योन्यन् समरे जघ्नुस्तदा वानरराक्षसाः
te gadābhirvicitrābhiḥ prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥanyonyan samare jaghnustadā vānararākṣasāḥ
Those monkeys and demons then began to strike each other with multi-coloured maces,
darts, swords and axes in the battle.


Word by word
9. te= those;vaanara raakShasaaH= monkeys and demons;tadaa= then;jaghnuH= struck;anyonyam= each other;chitraabhiH= with multi-coloured;gadaabhiH= maces;praasaiH= darts;khaDgaiH= swords;parashvadhaiH= and axes;samare= in the battle.




10Yuddha Kanda 93.10
एवं प्रवृते संग्रामे ह्यदुभुतं सुमहद्रजःरक्षसां वानराणां च शान्तं शोणितविस्रवैः
evaṃ pravṛte saṃgrāme hyadubhutaṃ sumahadrajaḥrakṣasāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca śāntaṃ śoṇitavisravaiḥ
While the battle was thus in progress, the surprisingly enormous dust was actually
settled down by the streams of blood, proceeding from the demons and mokeys.


Word by word
10. samgraame evam pravR^itte= while the battle was thus in
progress;adbhutam= surprisingly;sumahat= enormous;rajaH= dust;shaantam= was actually settled down;shoNita visravaiH= by the streams of
blood;rakShasaam vaanaraamcha= proceeding from the demons and monkeys.




11Yuddha Kanda 93.11
मातंगरथकूलस्य वाजिमत्स्या ध्वजद्रुमाःशरीरसंघाटवहाः प्रसस्रुः शोणितापगाः
mātaṃgarathakūlasya vājimatsyā dhvajadrumāḥśarīrasaṃghāṭavahāḥ prasasruḥ śoṇitāpagāḥ
With elephants and chariots as their river-banks, with horses as their fish and with
flag-staffs as trees, rivers of blood gushed forth, carrying dead


Word by word
11. shoNitaapagaaH= rivers of blood;maataN^garatha kuulaaH= with elephants and chariots as their river-banks;vaajimatsyaaH= with horses as their
fish;dhvajadrumaaH= with flag-staffs as trees;prasasruH= gushed forth;shariira samghaaTavahaaH= carrying dead bodies as logs of wood.




12Yuddha Kanda 93.12
ततस्ते वानराः सर्वे शोणितौघपरिप्लुताः
tataste vānarāḥ sarve śoṇitaughapariplutāḥ
Then, all those monkeys were drenched in streams of blood. Leaping and bouncing on
the battle-field, the monkey-chiefs broke off flag-staffs, armours, chariots, horses and various
kinds of weapons.


Word by word
12;13. tataH= then;sarve= all;te= those;vaanaraaH= monkeys;shoNitangha pariplutaaH= were drenched with streams of
blood;aaplutya aaplutya= leaping and bouncing;samare= on the battle-field;vaanarendraaH= the monkey-chiefs;babhaN^jare= broke off;dhvaja varma
rathaan= flag = staff;srmours;chariots;ashvaan= horses;naanaapraharaaNicha= and various kinds of weapons.




13Yuddha Kanda 93.13
ध्वजवर्मरथानश्वान्नानाप्रहरणानि च |आप्लुत्याप्लुत्य समरे वानरेन्द्रा बभंजिरे
dhvajavarmarathānaśvānnānāpraharaṇāni ca |āplutyāplutya samare vānarendrā babhaṃjire
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


14Yuddha Kanda 93.14
केशान्कर्णललाटांश्च नासिकाश्च प्लवंगमाः |रक्षसान् दशनैस्तीक्ष्णैर्नखैश्चापि व्यकर्तयन्
keśānkarṇalalāṭāṃśca nāsikāśca plavaṃgamāḥ |rakṣasān daśanaistīkṣṇairnakhaiścāpi vyakartayan
With their sharp teeth and nails, the monkeys tore off the hair, ears, eye-brows and
noses of the demons.


Word by word
14. plavangamaaH= the monkeys;tiikShaNaiH dashanaiH= with
their sharp teeth;nakhaishchaapi= and even nails;vyakartayan= tore off;keshaan= the hair;karNa lalaaTaamshcha= ears eye-brows;naasikaashchaapi= and noses;rakShasaan= of demons.




15Yuddha Kanda 93.15
एकैकन् राक्षसं संख्ये शतं वानरपुंगवाः |अभ्यधावन्त फलिनन् वृक्षं शकुनयो यथा
ekaikan rākṣasaṃ saṃkhye śataṃ vānarapuṃgavāḥ |abhyadhāvanta phalinan vṛkṣaṃ śakunayo yathā
A hundred monkey-chiefs rushed towards each single demon in the battle, even as
birds would rush towards a tree laden with fruits.


Word by word
15. shatam= A hundred;vaanara pungavaaH= monkey-chiefs;abhyadhaavanta= rushed towards;ekaikam= each single;raakShasam=
demon;samkhye= in battle;shakunayo yathaa= even as birds;(would rush
towards);vR^ikSham= a tree;phalinam= laden with fruits.




16Yuddha Kanda 93.16
तथा गदाभिर्गुर्वीभिः प्रासैः खड्गैः परश्वधैः |निर्जघ्नुर्वानरान्घोरान्राक्षसाः पर्वतोपमाः
tathā gadābhirgurvībhiḥ prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ |nirjaghnurvānarānghorānrākṣasāḥ parvatopamāḥ
Then, the demons resembling mountain in size, struck down the terrific monkeys with
large maces, darts, swords and axes.


Word by word
16. tadaa= then;raakShasaaH= the demons;parvatopamaaH= resembling mountains in size;nirjaghnuH= struck down;ghoraan= the terrific;vaanaraan= monkeys;gurviibhiH gadaabhiH= with
large maces;praasaiH= darts;khaDgaiH= swords;parashvadhaiH= and
axes.




17Yuddha Kanda 93.17
राक्षसैर्वध्यमानानान् वानराणां महाचमूः |शरण्यन् शरणं याता रामन् दशरथात्मजम्
rākṣasairvadhyamānānān vānarāṇāṃ mahācamūḥ |śaraṇyan śaraṇaṃ yātā rāman daśarathātmajam
The huge army of monkeys, being struck down by the demons, sought refuge in Rama,
the son of Dasaratha, who affords protection.


Word by word
17. mahaachamuuH= the huge army of monkeys;vadhyamaanaanaam= being struck down;raakShasaiH= by the demons;yaataa= sought;sharaNam= refuge;raamam= in Rama;dasharathaatmajam= the son of Dasaratha;sharaNyam= who affords protection.




18Yuddha Kanda 93.18
ततो रामो महातेजा धनुरादाय वीर्यवान् |प्रविश्य राक्षसन् सैन्यं शरवर्षं ववर्ष ह
tato rāmo mahātejā dhanurādāya vīryavān |praviśya rākṣasan sainyaṃ śaravarṣaṃ vavarṣa ha
Thereupon, Rama of great splendour and prowess, taking up his bow and entering the
army of demons, streamed forth showers of arrows.


Word by word
18. tataH= thereupon;raamaH= Rama;mahaatejaaH=
of great splendour;viiryavaan= and prowess;aadaaya= taking up;dhanuH= his bow;pravishya= and entering;sainyam= the army;raakShasam= of demons;vavarShaha= streamed forth;shara varSham=
showers of arrows.




19Yuddha Kanda 93.19
प्रविष्टन् तु तदा रामं मेघाः सूर्यमिवाम्बरे |नाभिजग्मुर्महाघोरं निर्दहन्तन् शराग्निना
praviṣṭan tu tadā rāmaṃ meghāḥ sūryamivāmbare |nābhijagmurmahāghoraṃ nirdahantan śarāgninā
Those highly terrific demons dared not approach Rama, having entered their ranks,
was scorching them with the flame of his arrows, even as clouds would not approach the scorching
sun in the sky.


Word by word

20Yuddha Kanda 93.20

  As per Ravana's command, his army marches forward to the battle-field, so as to fight fiercely with Rama and his army with their weapon. When the demons attack the monkeys with their various weapons fiercely, they seek refuge in Rama. Rama destroys the troops of demons in the battle-field swiftly.

  Yuddha Kanda · Sarga 95
  On beholding the sight of female-demons, afflicted with grief in the houses…
  On beholding the sight of female-demons, afflicted with grief in the houses of Lanka, Ravana is very much enraged and orders his generals to tell their armies to set out for the battle immediately.

arrows.

  On beholding the sight of female-demons, afflicted with grief in the houses of Lanka, Ravana is very much enraged and orders his generals to tell their armies to set out for the battle immediately. Ravana promises them to take revenge by killing Rama and Lakshmana as also monkey-chiefs in the battle. Accompanied by several demon-warriors, Ravana marched to the battle-field, where Rama and Lakshmana are while Ravana is sallying forth for the battle, he sees several bad omens presaging his death. On hearing the noise of the demons entering the battle-field, the army of monkeys return to the battle. A tumultuous fight ensues, between the monkeys and the demons. Ravana fights fiercely with monkeys.

hatvā tan vānaraiḥ sārdhaṃ nanāda mudito hariḥcukrodha ca daśagrīvo babhau hṛṣṭaśca rāghavaḥ
Having killed Mahodara, Sugreeva made a rejoicing roar with his monkeys. Ravana was
enraged. Rama looked rejoicing.


Word by word
35. hatvaa= having killed;tam= Mahodara;hariH=
Sugreeva;nanaada muditaH= made a rejoicing roar;vaanaraiH saardham= with his
monkeys;dashagriivaH= Ravana;chukrodha cha= was enraged;raaghavashcha= Rama;babhau hR^iShTaH= looked rejoicing.




36Yuddha Kanda 97.36
विषण्णवदनाः सर्वे राक्षसा दीनचेतसःविद्रवन्ति ततः सर्वे भयवित्रस्तचेतसः
viṣaṇṇavadanāḥ sarve rākṣasā dīnacetasaḥvidravanti tataḥ sarve bhayavitrastacetasaḥ
With their faces looking low-spirited all the demons felt dejected. With their minds
stricken with fear, all of them ran away from the battle-field.


Word by word
36. viShaNNa vadanaah= with their faces looking low-spirited;sarve raakShasaaH= all the demons;diinachetasaH= felt dejected;bhayavitrasta chetasaH= with their minds stricken with fear;sarve= all of
them;vidravanti= ran away;tataH= from the battle-field.




37Yuddha Kanda 97.37
महोदरं तं विनिपात्य भूमौ |महागिरेः कीर्णमिवैकदेशम् |सूर्यात्मजस्तत्र रराज लक्ष्म्या |सूर्यः स्वतेजोभिरिवाप्रधृष्यः
mahodaraṃ taṃ vinipātya bhūmau |mahāgireḥ kīrṇamivaikadeśam |sūryātmajastatra rarāja lakṣmyā |sūryaḥ svatejobhirivāpradhṛṣyaḥ
Having thrown down to the ground that Mahodara, looking like a part of a huge
mountain lying shattered the invincible Sugreeva shone in glory in the battle-field like the sun
shines with its rays.


Word by word
37. vinipaatya= having thrown down;bhuumau= to the
ground;tam mahodaram= that Mahodara;ekadesham iva= looking like a part;mahaagireH= of a huge mountain;kiirNam lying shattered;apradhR^iShyaH= the
invincible;suuryaatmajaH= Sugreeva;raraaja= shone;lakShmyaa= in
glory;tatra= there;suuryaH iva= like the sun;svatejobhiH= shines
with its rays.




38Yuddha Kanda 97.38
अथ विजयमवाप्य वानरेन्द्रः |समरमुखे सुरसिद्धयक्षसंघैः |अवनितलगतैश्च भूतसंघै |र्हरुषसमाकुलितैर्निरीक्ष्यमाणः
atha vijayamavāpya vānarendraḥ |samaramukhe surasiddhayakṣasaṃghaiḥ |avanitalagataiśca bhūtasaṃghai |rharuṣasamākulitairnirīkṣyamāṇaḥ
Having attained victory in the battle-front, Sugreeva then continued to be looked at
by the multitude of gods, Siddhas (a class of demigods who are endowed with mystic powers) and
Yakshas (another class of demigods attending on Kubera, the god of riches) as also a host of beings
standing on the earth's surface who were all overwhelmed with joy.


Word by word
38. aavaapya= having attained;vijayam= victory;samaramukhe= in the battle-front;vaanarendraH= Sugreeva;atha= then;niriikShyamaaNah= continued to be looked at;surasiddhe yakShasamghaiH= by the
multitude of gods;Siddhas (a class of demi-gods who are endowed with mystic powers) and Yakshas
(another class of demi-gods attending upon Kubera;the god of riches) bhuutasamghaiH cha=
as also a multitude of beings;avanitalagaiH= standing on the earth's surface;haruShasamaakulitaiH= who were all overwhelmed with joy.



    
  
  Ravana sends Mahodara to the battle-field. Mahodara creates havoc, by cutting off the hands, feet and thighs of monkeys. Some monkeys seek refuge with Sugreeva and some ran away for life. Sugreeva attacks Mahodara and initially kills the horses of the latter. Both of them fight till the weapons in their hands get broken. Then, they start wrestling with each other, till they get exhausted. Finally, Sugreeva cuts off Mahodara's head with a huge sword.

1Yuddha Kanda 99.1
महोदरमहापार्श्वौ हतौ दृष्ट्वा तु राक्षसौ |तस्मिंश्च निहते वीरे विरूपाक्षे महाबले
mahodaramahāpārśvau hatau dṛṣṭvā tu rākṣasau |tasmiṃśca nihate vīre virūpākṣe mahābale
Seeing Mahodara and Mahaparshva the demons having been killed, and that valiant and
mighty Virupaksha struck down in that great battle, a tremendous anger took possession of Ravana.
He urged on his charioteer and addressed to him the following words:

आविवेश महान्क्रोधो रावणन् तु महामृधे |सूतन् सञ्चोदयामास वाक्यन् चेदमुवाच ह
āviveśa mahānkrodho rāvaṇan tu mahāmṛdhe |sūtan sañcodayāmāsa vākyan cedamuvāca ha

3Yuddha Kanda 99.3
निहतानाममात्यानान् रुद्धस्य नगरस्य च |दुःखमेषोअपनेष्यामि हत्वा तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
nihatānāmamātyānān ruddhasya nagarasya ca |duḥkhameṣoapaneṣyāmi hatvā tau rāmalakṣmaṇau
"Killing those two princes, Rama and Lakshmana, I will remove surely the sorrow
caused to me on account of the ministers who have been killed and the city which has been laid
siege to (by the monkeys)."

4Yuddha Kanda 99.4
रामवृक्षन् रणे हन्मि सीतापुष्पफलप्रदम् |प्रशाखा यस्य सुग्रीवो जाम्बवान्कुमुदो नलः
rāmavṛkṣan raṇe hanmi sītāpuṣpaphalapradam |praśākhā yasya sugrīvo jāmbavānkumudo nalaḥ
"In the battle, I will cut down the tree in the shape of Rama, which is going to
yield fruit through its flower in the form of Seetha, whose principal branches are Sugreeva,
Jambavan, Kumuda, Nala, Dvivida, Mainda, Angada, Gandhamadana, Hanuma, Sushena and all the chiefs
of monkey-warriors."

स दिशो दश घोषेण रथस्यातिरथो महान् |नादयन्प्रययौ तूर्णन् राघवन् चाभ्यवर्तत
sa diśo daśa ghoṣeṇa rathasyātiratho mahān |nādayanprayayau tūrṇan rāghavan cābhyavartata
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


6Yuddha Kanda 99.6
पूरिता तेन शब्देन सनदीगिरिकानना |सञ्चचाल मही सर्वा सवराहमृगद्विपा
pūritā tena śabdena sanadīgirikānanā |sañcacāla mahī sarvā savarāhamṛgadvipā
Ravana, the mighty and the surpassing Chariot-Warrior, went quickly, making a noise
in all the ten directions, with the sound of the chariot, rushing towards Rama.

7Yuddha Kanda 99.7
तामसन् सुमहाघोरन् चकारास्त्रं सुदारुणम् |निर्ददाह कपीन्सर्वान्स्ते प्रपेतुः समन्ततः
tāmasan sumahāghoran cakārāstraṃ sudāruṇam |nirdadāha kapīnsarvānste prapetuḥ samantataḥ
Filled with that sound, the entire earth, with its rivers, mountains and forests,
trembled, throwing lions, antelopes and birds, into fright.

8Yuddha Kanda 99.8
तान्यनीकान्यनेकानि रावणस्य शरोत्तमैः |दृष्ट्वा भग्नानि शतशो राघवः पर्यवस्थितः
tānyanīkānyanekāni rāvaṇasya śarottamaiḥ |dṛṣṭvā bhagnāni śataśo rāghavaḥ paryavasthitaḥ
He employed very highly terrific and exceedingly frightful mystic missile called
Tamasa, which began to consume all the monkeys, who started falling down on all sides.

9Yuddha Kanda 99.9
उत्पपात रजो भूमौ तैर्भग्नै संप्रधावितैः |न हि तत्सहितुं शेकुर्ब्रह्मणा निर्मितं स्वयम्
utpapāta rajo bhūmau tairbhagnai saṃpradhāvitaiḥ |na hi tatsahituṃ śekurbrahmaṇā nirmitaṃ svayam
Dust began to fly up from the earth, while those frustrated monkeys were fleeing
away for they could no longer bear that missile built by Brahma himself.

10Yuddha Kanda 99.10
तान्यनीकान्यनेकानि रावणस्य शरोत्तमैः |दृषःट्वा भग्नानि शतशो राघवः पर्यवस्थितः
tānyanīkānyanekāni rāvaṇasya śarottamaiḥ |dṛṣḥṭvā bhagnāni śataśo rāghavaḥ paryavasthitaḥ
Seeing those hundreds of many of his armies shattered by excellent arrows of Ravana,
Rama took his stand, ready for the battle.

11Yuddha Kanda 99.11
ततो राक्षसशार्दूलो विद्राव्य हरिवाहिनीम् |स ददर्श ततो रामन् तिष्ठन्तमपराजितम्
tato rākṣasaśārdūlo vidrāvya harivāhinīm |sa dadarśa tato rāman tiṣṭhantamaparājitam
Having driven away the army of monkeys, Ravana the foremost among the demons then
saw Rama, the annihilator of his enemies, who was endowed with long arms and eyes as wide as lotus
petals standing unconquered with his brother Lakshmana-like Indra the lord of celestials is seen
with Vishnu, the supreme lord of preservation-holding up his great bow as though scraping the
sky.

लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा विष्णुना वासवन् यथा |आलिखन्तमिवाकाशमवष्टभ्य महद्धनुःपद्मपत्रविशालाक्षन् दीर्घबाहुमरिन्दमम्

13Yuddha Kanda 99.13
ततो रामो महातेजाः सौमित्रिसहितो बली
tato rāmo mahātejāḥ saumitrisahito balī
Seeing the disappointed monkeys and Ravana advancing, the mighty Rama who was
endowed with a great splendour and accompanied by Lakshmana who were born in Raghu dynasty, then
pleasingly seized his bow at the middle.

Rama;mahaatejaaH= of great splendour;raaghavaH= who was born in Raghu

वानरांश्च रणे भग्नानापतन्तन् च रावणम् |समीक्ष्य राघवो हृष्टो मध्ये जग्राह कार्मुकम्
vānarāṃśca raṇe bhagnānāpatantan ca rāvaṇam |samīkṣya rāghavo hṛṣṭo madhye jagrāha kārmukam
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


15Yuddha Kanda 99.15
विस्फारयितुमारेभे ततः स धनुरुत्तमम् |महावेगं महानादं निर्भिन्दन्निव मेदिनीम्

force and sonorous, as though he was breaking the earth asunder.

16Yuddha Kanda 99.16
रावणस्य च बाणौघै रामविस्फारितेन च |शब्देन राक्षसास्तेन पेतुश्च शतशस्तदा
rāvaṇasya ca bāṇaughai rāmavisphāritena ca |śabdena rākṣasāstena petuśca śataśastadā
Then, due to that buzzing sound produced by the streams of Ravana's arrows as also
by the twang of Rama's bow, those demons fell down in their hundreds.

17Yuddha Kanda 99.17
तयोः शरपथं प्राप्य रावणो राजपुत्रयोः |स बभूव यथा राहुः समीपे शशिसूर्ययोः
tayoḥ śarapathaṃ prāpya rāvaṇo rājaputrayoḥ |sa babhūva yathā rāhuḥ samīpe śaśisūryayoḥ
That Ravana, coming within the range of arrow-shots of Rama and Lakshmana, resembled
Rahu (the demon who is supposed to seize the sun and the moon), standing in the vicinity of the
moon and the sun.

18Yuddha Kanda 99.18
तमिच्छन्प्रथमन् योद्धुं लक्ष्मणो निशितैः शरैः |मुमोच धनुरायम्य शरानग्निशिखोपमान्
tamicchanprathaman yoddhuṃ lakṣmaṇo niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ |mumoca dhanurāyamya śarānagniśikhopamān
Wishing to fight him with his sharp arrows at the earliest, Lakshmana stretching his

तान्मुक्तमात्रानाकाशे लक्ष्मणेन धनुष्मता |बाणान्बाणैर्महातेजा रावणः प्रत्यवारयत्
tānmuktamātrānākāśe lakṣmaṇena dhanuṣmatā |bāṇānbāṇairmahātejā rāvaṇaḥ pratyavārayat
Ravana of extra ordinary energy prevented those arrows, the moment they were
released by Lakshmana, with his arrows, in the sky itself.

20Yuddha Kanda 99.20
एकमेकेन बाणेन त्रिभिस्त्रीन्दशभिर्दश |लक्ष्मणस्य प्रचिच्छेद दर्शयन्पाणिलाघवम्
ekamekena bāṇena tribhistrīndaśabhirdaśa |lakṣmaṇasya praciccheda darśayanpāṇilāghavam
Showing the dexterity of his hand, Ravana split the arrows of Lakshmana one with
one, three with three and ten with ten arrows.


Word by word
20. darshayan= showing;paaNilaaghavam= the dexterity of
his hand;(Ravana) prachichchheda= split;baaNena= the arrows;lakShmaNasya= of Lakshmana;ekam ekena= one with one;tribhiH triin=

21Yuddha Kanda 99.21
अभ्यतिक्रम्य सौमित्रिन् रावणः समितिञ्जयः |आससाद ततो रामन् स्थितं शैलमिवाचलम्
abhyatikramya saumitrin rāvaṇaḥ samitiñjayaḥ |āsasāda tato rāman sthitaṃ śailamivācalam
Overpassing Lakshmana, Ravana the victorious in battle, approached Rama, who stood

Struck by Rama's missile, the terrific arrows of Ravana got destroyed in the sky and
fell down in thousands of pieces.


Word by word
48. raaghavaastra samaahataaH= struck by the missile of Rama;te= those;ghoraaH= terrific;raavaNasharaaH= arrows of Ravana;jagmuH= got;vilayam= destroyed;aakaashe= in the sky;jagmuH= and fell;sahasrashaH= in thousands of pieces.




49Yuddha Kanda 99.49
तदस्त्रं निहतन् दृष्ट्वा रामेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा
tadastraṃ nihatan dṛṣṭvā rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
Rejoiced to see that missile struck down by Rama, who was unweary in action, all the
valiant monkeys, who were capable of changing their form at will, then encompassing Rama, raised a
clamour, facing Sugreeva.


Word by word
49;50. hR^iShTaaH dR^iShTvaa= rejoiced to see;tat astram= that missile;nihatam= struck down;raameNa= by Rama;akliShTakarmaNaa= who was unweary in action;sarve viiraaH kapayaH= all the
valiant monkeys;kaama ruupiNaH= who were capable of changing their form at will;tataH= then;neduH= raised a clamour;samparikShipya= encompassing;raamam= Rama;sugriivaabhi mukhaaH= facing Sugreeva.




50Yuddha Kanda 99.50
हृष्टा नेदुस्ततः सर्वे कपयः कामरूपिणः |सुग्रीवाभिमुखा वीराः संपरिक्षिप्य रागवम्
hṛṣṭā nedustataḥ sarve kapayaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ |sugrīvābhimukhā vīrāḥ saṃparikṣipya rāgavam
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


51Yuddha Kanda 99.51
ततस्तदस्त्रं विनिहत्य राघवः |प्रसह्य तद्रावणबाहुनिःसृतम् |मुदान्वितो दाशरथिर्महात्मा |विनेदुरुच्चैर्मुदिताः कपीश्वरा
tatastadastraṃ vinihatya rāghavaḥ |prasahya tadrāvaṇabāhuniḥsṛtam |mudānvito dāśarathirmahātmā |vineduruccairmuditāḥ kapīśvarā
Striking down with force that missile which came forth from Ravana's arms, the
great-souled Rama, then was filled with rejoice while the chiefs of monkeys, full f joy, shouted
loudly.


Word by word
51. vinihatya= striking down;prasahya= with force;tat= that;astram= missile;tadraavaNabaahuniHsR^itam= which came
forth from the hands of that Ravana;mahaatmaa= the great souled;daasharathiH=
Rama;tataH= then;mudaa anvitaH= was filled with joy;muditaiH= full
of joy;vineduH uchchaiH= shouted loudly.



    
  
  Ravana enters the battle-field and with his mystic missile, frightens several monkeys and destroys them. Rama and Lakshmana come and attack Ravana. Then, Rama and Ravana fight each other with various kinds of arrows. When the missile employed by Ravana is struck down by Rama, all the monkeys shout loudly with a rejoice.

title: Rama laments over the uncertain condition of Lakshmana
text:
Home/Yuddha Kanda/Sarga 101

  Yuddha Kanda · Sarga 101
  Rama laments over the uncertain condition of Lakshmana
  Rama laments over the uncertain condition of Lakshmana. He calls Sushena, the monkey-physician.
  57 shlokas≈ 31 minDevanagari completeEnglish 93%


  
    Shlokas (57)
  
  Sarga summary
  
    Reading notes
  


  
    
      Jump to a shloka123456789101112131415161718192021222324252627282930313233343536373839404142434445464748495051525354555657
      
1Yuddha Kanda 101.1
शक्त्या निपातितं दृष्ट्वा रावणेन बलीयसा |लक्ष्मणं समर् शूरं शोणितौघपरिप्लुतम्
śaktyā nipātitaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇena balīyasā |lakṣmaṇaṃ samar śūraṃ śoṇitaughapariplutam
Seeing the valiant Lakshmana bathed in a stream of blood, when struck down in battle
with a spear by the mighty Ravana and having given a tumultuous fight, to the evil-minded Ravana,
Rama spoke as follows to Sushena, even while releasing a multitude of arrows (at Ravana).


Word by word
1;2. dR^iShTyaa= seeing;shuuram= the valiant;lakShmaNam= Lakshmana;shoNitau ghapariphitam= who was bathed in a stream of
blood;samare= in battle;nipaatitam= when overthrown;shaktyaa= with
a spear;baliiyasaa raavaNena= by the mighty Ravana;saH= Rama;dattvaa= giving;tumulam= a tumultuous;yuddham= fight;duraatmanaH raavaNaH= with the evil-minded Ravana;visR^ijanneva= and even
while releasing;baaNaughaan= a multitude of arrows;abraviit= spoke;suSheNam= to Sushena;idam= the following words:




2Yuddha Kanda 101.2
स दत्त्वा तुमुलन् युद्धं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः |विसृजनेव बाणौघान्सुषेणन् वाक्यमब्रवीत्
sa dattvā tumulan yuddhaṃ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ |visṛjaneva bāṇaughānsuṣeṇan vākyamabravīt
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


3Yuddha Kanda 101.3
एष रावणवेगेन लक्ष्मणः पतितः क्षितौ |सर्पवद्वेष्टते वीरो मम शोकमुदीरयन्
eṣa rāvaṇavegena lakṣmaṇaḥ patitaḥ kṣitau |sarpavadveṣṭate vīro mama śokamudīrayan
"This heroic Lakshmana, falling down on earth yielding to Ravana's prowess, is
wiggling like a serpent, causing an increase in grief to me."


Word by word
3. eShaH= this;viiraH= heroic;lakShmaNaH=
Lakshmana;patitaH= who fell down;bhuvi= on earth;raavaNa viiryeNa=
on account of Ravana's prowess;udiirayan= increasing;shokam= my sorrow;cheShTate= is wiggling;bhuumau= on the ground;sarpavat= like a
serpent.




4Yuddha Kanda 101.4
शोणितार्द्रमिमन् वीरं प्राणैरिष्टतरं मम |पश्यतो मम का शक्तिर्योद्धुं पर्याकुलात्मनः
śoṇitārdramiman vīraṃ prāṇairiṣṭataraṃ mama |paśyato mama kā śaktiryoddhuṃ paryākulātmanaḥ
"My energy to fight is failing, even as I see this valiant Lakshmana, who is dearer
to me than life, bathed in blood, my mind being greatly disturbed."


Word by word
4. kaa= what;shaktiH= energy (is there);mama=
for me;paryaakulaatmanaH= disturbed in mind;yauddhum= to fight;pashyataH= while seeing;imam= this;viiram= valiant Lakshmana;mama priyataram praaNaiH= the most beloved to me as dear as life;shoNitaardram= bathed in blood?




5Yuddha Kanda 101.5
अयन् स समरश्लाघी भ्राता मे शुभलक्षणः |यदि पञ्चत्वमापन्नः प्राणैर्मे किन् सुखेन वा
ayan sa samaraślāghī bhrātā me śubhalakṣaṇaḥ |yadi pañcatvamāpannaḥ prāṇairme kin sukhena vā
"Of what use is life or happiness to me, if this illustrious brother of mine, who is
endowed with auspicious bodily marks and who always speaks highly of war, meets with his
death?"


Word by word
5. kim= of what use;praaNaiH= is life;sukhena
vaa= or happiness;me= to me;yadi saH ayam me bhraataa= if this famous
brother of mine;shubha lakShaNaH= who is endowed with auspicious bodily marks;samarashlaaghii= and always speaks highly of war;aapannaH= obtain;paN^chatvam= his death?




6Yuddha Kanda 101.6
लज्जतीव हि मे वीर्यं भ्रश्यतीव कराद्धनुः |सायका व्यवसीदन्ति दृष्टिर्बाष्पवशन् गता
lajjatīva hi me vīryaṃ bhraśyatīva karāddhanuḥ |sāyakā vyavasīdanti dṛṣṭirbāṣpavaśan gatā
"My valour is feeling shy, as it were. My bow seems to fall down from any hand. My
arrows are dropping down. My vision has been overcome with tears."


Word by word
6. me= my;viiryam= valour;lajjatiiva= is
feeling shy;as it were;dhanuH= my bow;bhrashyatiiva= is falling down;karaat= from my hand;saayakaaH= my arrows;vyavasiidanti= are
dropping down;dR^iShTiH= my vision;gataa= got;baaShpavasham=
overcome with tears.




7Yuddha Kanda 101.7
अवसीदन्ति गात्राणि स्वप्नयाने नृणामिव |चिन्ता मे वर्धते तीव्रा मुमूर्षापि च जायते
avasīdanti gātrāṇi svapnayāne nṛṇāmiva |cintā me vardhate tīvrā mumūrṣāpi ca jāyate
"My limbs seem to sink down, like those of men in sleep. I have a serious tension,
growing in me. I even wish to die."


Word by word
7. gaatraaNi= my limbs;avasiidanti= seem to sink down;nR^iNaam iva= like those of men;svapnayaane= in sleep;chintaa=
tension;vartate= is;tiivraa= growing;me= in me;jaayate
mumuurShaapi= I even wish to die.




8Yuddha Kanda 101.8
भ्रातरं निहतन् दृष्ट्वा रावणेन दुरात्मना |विष्टन्न्तं तु दुःखार्तं मर्मण्यभिहतं भृशम्
bhrātaraṃ nihatan dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇena durātmanā |viṣṭanntaṃ tu duḥkhārtaṃ marmaṇyabhihataṃ bhṛśam
"My brother has been struck down by the evil-minded Ravana, seriously wounded in his
vital parts, afflicted with agony and groaming."


Word by word
8. bhraataram= my brother;abhihatam= has been struck
down;duraatmanaa= by the evil-minded;raavaNena= Ravana;abhihatam
bhR^isham= seriously wounded;marmaNi= in his vital parts;duHkhaartam=
afflicted with agony;viShTanantam= and grooming.




9Yuddha Kanda 101.9
राघवो भ्रातरं दृष्ट्य प्रियं प्राणं बहिश्चरम् |दुःखेन महताविष्टो ध्यानशोकपरायणः
rāghavo bhrātaraṃ dṛṣṭya priyaṃ prāṇaṃ bahiścaram |duḥkhena mahatāviṣṭo dhyānaśokaparāyaṇaḥ
Seeing his beloved brother, who was his very life-breath moving outside, Rama was
afflicted with excessive agony and gave himself up to anxiety and grief.


Word by word
9. dR^iShTvaa= seeing;priyam= his beloved;bhraataram= brother;praaNam= who was his very life-breath;bahishcharam= moving outside;raaghavaH= Rama;aaviShTaH= was
stricken;mahataa duHkhena= with excessive agony;dhayaana shoka paraayaNaH=
gave himself up to anxiety and grief.




10Yuddha Kanda 101.10
परन् विषादमापन्नो विललापाकुलेन्द्रियः |न हि युद्धेन मे कार्यं नैव प्राणैर्न सीतया
paran viṣādamāpanno vilalāpākulendriyaḥ |na hi yuddhena me kāryaṃ naiva prāṇairna sītayā
Seeing Lakshmana his brother lying wounded in the dust of the battle-field, he got
into extreme despondency and lamented (as follows), confused in mind, as he was:


Word by word
10. dR^iShTvaa= seeing;lakShmaNam= Lakshmana;bhraataram= his brother;nihatam raNapaamsuShu= lying wounded in the dust of
the battle-field;aapannaH= he got into;param= extreme;viShaadam=
despondency;vilalaapa= and lamented (as follows);aakulendriyaH= confused in
mind;as he was.




11Yuddha Kanda 101.11
विजयोऽपि हि मे शूर न प्रियायोपकल्पते |अचक्षुर्विषयश्चन्द्रः कां प्रीतिं जनयिष्यति
vijayo.api hi me śūra na priyāyopakalpate |acakṣurviṣayaścandraḥ kāṃ prītiṃ janayiṣyati
"O the valiant Lakshmana! Even victory cannot create a pleasure for me. What
pleasure can the moon create for a man who has lost his vision?"


Word by word
11. shuura= O the valiant Lakshmana!;vijayaH.api= even
victory;na priyaaya upakalpate= is not making a pleasure;me= for me;kaam= what;priitim= pleasure;(can) chandraH= the moon;janayiShyati= create;achakShurviShayaH= for a man who has lost his vision?




12Yuddha Kanda 101.12
किं मे युद्धेन किं प्राणैर्युद्धकार्यं न विद्यते |यत्रायं निहतः शेते रणमूर्धनि लक्ष्मणः
kiṃ me yuddhena kiṃ prāṇairyuddhakāryaṃ na vidyate |yatrāyaṃ nihataḥ śete raṇamūrdhani lakṣmaṇaḥ
"What purpose of mine will be served by fighting or eve by life? When this Lakshmana
lies killed in the forefront of battle here, I have no use for the war."


Word by word
12. kim me= what purpose of mine will be served by fighting;kim
praaNaiH= or even by life?;ayam lakShmaNaH= this Lakshmana;shete= lies;nihataH= killed;yatra raNamuurdhani= in forefront of battle here;na
vidyate= I have no;yuddhakaaryam= use for the war.




13Yuddha Kanda 101.13
यथैव मां वनं यान्तमनुयाति महाद्युतिः |अहमप्युपयास्यामि तथैवैनं यमक्षयम्
yathaiva māṃ vanaṃ yāntamanuyāti mahādyutiḥ |ahamapyupayāsyāmi tathaivainaṃ yamakṣayam
"In the same way as the very glorious Lakshmana followed me When I was going to the
forest, I too will in the same way follow him to the abode of Yama the lord of Death."


Word by word
13. yathaiva= in the same way as;mahaadyutiH= the very
glorious Lakshmana;amyaati= followed;maam= me;yaantam= when I was
going;vanam= to the forest;ahamapi= I too;tathaiva= will in the
same way;upayaasyaami= follow;enam= him;yamakShayam= to the abode
of Yama the Lord of Death.




14Yuddha Kanda 101.14
इष्टबन्दुजनो नित्यं मां स नित्यमनुव्रतः |इमामवस्थां गमितो राक्षसैः कूटयोधिभिः
iṣṭabandujano nityaṃ māṃ sa nityamanuvrataḥ |imāmavasthāṃ gamito rākṣasaiḥ kūṭayodhibhiḥ
"The demons, who fight treacherously, created this condition to Lakshmana, who loved
his relatives and who was ardently devoted forever to me."


Word by word
14. saH= Lakshmana;iShTa bandhujanaH= who is having his
beloved relatives;anuvrataH= and who is ardently devoted;maam= to me;nityam= forever;gamitaH= is obtained;imaam= this;avasthaam= condition;raakShasaiH= by the demons;kuuTayodhibhiH= who
fight treacherously.




15Yuddha Kanda 101.15
देशे देशे कलत्राणि देशे देशे च बान्धवाः |तं तु देशं न पश्यामि यत्र भ्राता सहोदरः
deśe deśe kalatrāṇi deśe deśe ca bāndhavāḥ |taṃ tu deśaṃ na paśyāmi yatra bhrātā sahodaraḥ
"Wives may be obtained ever where. Relatives can be had every where. However, I do
not find a brother, born of the same womb, at such a place whatesoever."


Word by word
15. kalatraaNi= wives may be obtained;deshe deshe=
everywhere;baandhavaaH= relatives (can be had) deshe deshe cha = everywhere;na
pashyaami= I do not find;bhraataa= brother;sahodaraH= born of the same
womb;yatra tam desham tu= as such a place;wherever.




16Yuddha Kanda 101.16
इत्येवं विलपन्तं तं शोकविह्वलितेन्द्रियम् |विवेष्टमानं करुणमुच्छ्वसन्तं पुनः पुनः
ityevaṃ vilapantaṃ taṃ śokavihvalitendriyam |viveṣṭamānaṃ karuṇamucchvasantaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
The monkeys saw that Rama, thus lamenting with his mind reeling and distressed in
grief and pitiably sighing his breath repeatedly.


Word by word
16. (The monkeys saw) tam= that Rama;vilapantam ityevam=
thus lamenting;shoka vihvalitendriyam viveShTamaanam= with his mind reeling and
distressed in grief;karuNam= pitiably;uchchhvasantam= sighing his breath;punaH punaH= repeatedly.




17Yuddha Kanda 101.17
किं नु राज्ये दुर्धर्षलक्ष्मणेन विना मम |कथं वक्ष्याम्यहं त्वम्बां सुमित्रां पुत्रवत्सलाम्
kiṃ nu rājye durdharṣalakṣmaṇena vinā mama |kathaṃ vakṣyāmyahaṃ tvambāṃ sumitrāṃ putravatsalām
"Of what use is the kingdom for me, without Lakshmana, who was difficult to over
power? What can I tell to Sumitra, the mother who was so fond of her son?"


Word by word
17. kim nu= of what use;raajyena= is the kingdom;mama= for me;durdharSha lakSmaNena vinaa= without Lakshmana;who was difficult
to over power?;aham katham akShyaami= what can I tell;sumitraam= to Sumitra;putravatsalaamambaam= the mother;who was fond of her son.




18Yuddha Kanda 101.18
उपालम्भं न शक्ष्यामि सोढुं दत्तं सुमित्रया |किं नु वक्ष्यामि कौसल्यां मातरं किं नु कैकयीम्
upālambhaṃ na śakṣyāmi soḍhuṃ dattaṃ sumitrayā |kiṃ nu vakṣyāmi kausalyāṃ mātaraṃ kiṃ nu kaikayīm
"I shall not be able to bear the reproach, which will be levelled by Sumitra. What
shall I pay to kausalya the mother or what shall I say to Kaikeya?"


Word by word
18. na shakShyaami= I shall not be able;soDhum= to bear;upaalambham= the reproach;dattam= which will be given;sumitrayaa=
by sumitra;kim nu vakShyaami= what shall I say;kausalyaam= to Kausalya;maataram= the mother;kimnu= and what shall I say;kaikeyiim= to
Kaikeyi?




19Yuddha Kanda 101.19
भरतं किं नु वक्ष्यामि शत्रुघ्नं च महाबलम् |सह तेन वनं यातो विना तेनागतः कथम्
bharataṃ kiṃ nu vakṣyāmi śatrughnaṃ ca mahābalam |saha tena vanaṃ yāto vinā tenāgataḥ katham
"What shall I say to Bharata or to the mighty Shatrughna, when they ask me, how I
came back without Lakshmana even though I went to the forest along with him?"


Word by word
19. kim nu vakShyaami= what shall I say;bharatam= to
Bhrata;mahaabalam shatrughnam= or to the mighty Shatrughna;(when they ask me);katham= how;aagataH= I can back;tena vinaa= without Lakshmana;yaataH= eventhogh I went;vanam= to the forest;tena saha= along with
him?




20Yuddha Kanda 101.20
इहैव मरणं श्रेयो न तु बन्धुविगर्हणम् |किं मया दुष्कृतं कर्म कृतमन्यत्र जन्मनियेन मे धार्मिको भ्राता निहतश्चाग्रतः स्थितः
ihaiva maraṇaṃ śreyo na tu bandhuvigarhaṇam |kiṃ mayā duṣkṛtaṃ karma kṛtamanyatra janmaniyena me dhārmiko bhrātā nihataścāgrataḥ sthitaḥ
"It is better to die at this place only, rather than hear the reproaches of one's
own people. What sinful act was done by me in a previous birth due to which my righteous brother
lies killed before me?


Word by word
20. maraNam= death;shreyaH= is better;ihaiva=
here only;tu= but;na= not;bandhuvigarhaNam= a reproaches by one's
own people;kim= what;duSkR^itam karma= sinful act;kR^itam= was
done;mayaa= by me;anyatra janmani= in another life;yena= due to
which;dhaarmikaH me bhraataa= my righteous brother;nihataH= having been
killed;sthitaH= lies;agrataH= before me.




21Yuddha Kanda 101.21
हा भ्रातर्मनुजश्रेष्ठ शूराणाम् प्रवर प्रभोएकाकी किं नु मां त्यक्त्वा परलोकाय गच्छसि
hā bhrātarmanujaśreṣṭha śūrāṇām pravara prabhoekākī kiṃ nu māṃ tyaktvā paralokāya gacchasi
"Alas! O the powerful brother, the best of men! O the foremost among the valiant

48. raamaH= Rama;paraviirahaa= the destroyer of enemies;abraviit= said;lakShmaNam= to Lakshmana;iti= saying;ehi
ehi= "come;come!" sasvaje= and embraced him;snehagaaDham cha= firmly
with affection;baaShpaparyaakulekShaNaH= with his eyes clouded with tears.




49Yuddha Kanda 101.49
अब्रवीच्च परिष्वज्य सौमित्रिन् राघवस्तदादिष्ट्या त्वान् वीर पश्यामि मरणात्पुनरागतम्
abravīcca pariṣvajya saumitrin rāghavastadādiṣṭyā tvān vīra paśyāmi maraṇātpunarāgatam
After embracing Lakshmana, Rama then said to him: "Luckily, O valiant one, I see you
here, returned from death."


Word by word
49. pariShvajya= after embracing;saumitrim= Lakshmana;raaghavaH= Rama;tadaa= then;abraviichcha= said to him;diShTyaa= luckily;viira= O valiant one;pashyaami= I see;tvaam= you;punaH aagatam= returned;maraNaat= from death.




50Yuddha Kanda 101.50
न हि मे जीवितेनार्थः सीतया च जयेन वाको हि मे जीवितेनार्थस्त्वयि पञ्चत्वमागते
na hi me jīvitenārthaḥ sītayā ca jayena vāko hi me jīvitenārthastvayi pañcatvamāgate
"There is no purpose of mine, by me own life nor of Seetha nor of victory. If you
have attained demise, tell me what significnace is there for it to me?"


Word by word
50. na hi arthaH= there is indeed no purpose;me= of mine;jiivitena= by me my own life;siitayaa= nor of Seetha;vijayenavaa=
nor of victory;tvaye= If you;aagate= have attained;paN^chatvam=
demise;vada= tell me;kaH= what;arthaH= significane;(is there);tena= by it;me= to me?




51Yuddha Kanda 101.51
इत्येवन् वदतस्तस्य राघवस्य महात्मनःखिन्नः शिथिलया वाचा लक्ष्मणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
ityevan vadatastasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥkhinnaḥ śithilayā vācā lakṣmaṇo vākyamabravīt
While the great souled Rama was speaking thus, the exhausted Lakshmana, in a feeble
tone, spoke the following words:


Word by word
51. mahaatmanaH raaghavah= (while) the great souled Rama;vaataH= was speaking ityevam = thus;khinnaH= the exhausted;lakShmaNaH= Lakshmana;abraviit= spoke;vaakyam= the following words;shithilayaa vaachaa= in a feeble tone.




52Yuddha Kanda 101.52
तां प्रतिज्ञां प्रतिज्ञाय पुरा सत्यपराक्रमलघुः कश्चिदिवासत्त्वो नैवन् वक्तुमिहार्हसि
tāṃ pratijñāṃ pratijñāya purā satyaparākramalaghuḥ kaścidivāsattvo naivan vaktumihārhasi
"Having solemnly taken that pledge (of killing Ravana) before, O brother true to
your promise, you ought not to speak as you have done like a weak and courageless man."


Word by word
52. satya paraakramaa= O brother;true to your promise!;na
arhasi= you ought not;vaktum= to speak;evam= like this;iha=
now;kashchidiva= like somebody;asattvah= who has no courage;laghuH= and who is weak;pratijJNaaya= having taken;taam pratijJNaam= that vow (of
killing Ravana);puraa= before.




53Yuddha Kanda 101.53
न प्रतिज्ञान् हि कुर्वन्ति वितथां साधवोअनघलक्ष्मणन् हि महत्त्वस्य प्रतिज्ञापरिपालनम्
na pratijñān hi kurvanti vitathāṃ sādhavoanaghalakṣmaṇan hi mahattvasya pratijñāparipālanam
"There is no purpose of mine, by me own life nor of Seetha nor of victory. If you
have attained demise, tell me what significance is there for it to me?"


Word by word
53. satyavaadinaH= those who speak the truth;na kurvanti
hi= do not make;pratijJNaam= their promise;vitathaam= futile;pratijJNapaalanam= fulfilling their pledge;lakShaNam hi= is indeed the
attribute;mahattvasya= of the moral amplitude.




54Yuddha Kanda 101.54
नैराश्यमुपगन्तुन् ते तदलं मत्कृतेअनघवधेन रावणस्याद्य प्रतिज्ञामनुपालय
nairāśyamupagantun te tadalaṃ matkṛteanaghavadhena rāvaṇasyādya pratijñāmanupālaya
"O the faultless one! Getting into homelessness for my sake is not befitting of you.
Fulfill your promise now, by killing Ravana."


Word by word
54. anagha= O the faultless one!;te= to you;upagantum cha nairaashyam= getting into hopelessness too;matkR^ite= for my
sake;naalam= is not befitting;anupaalaya= fulfill;pratijJNaam=
your promise;vadhena= by killing;raavaNasya= of Ravana;adya=
now.




55Yuddha Kanda 101.55
न जीवन्यास्यते शत्रुस्तव बाणपथन् गतःनर्दतस्तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रस्य सिन्हस्येव महागजः
na jīvanyāsyate śatrustava bāṇapathan gataḥnardatastīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrasya sinhasyeva mahāgajaḥ
"An enemy who falls victim to your arrows, cannot turn out alive, as a huge elephant
which gets into the path of a roaring lion possessing terrible tusks."


Word by word
55. shatruH= An enemy;gataH= who stands;tava baaNa
patham= within the path of your arrows;na yaasyate= cannot turn out;jiivan= alive;mahaagajaH iva= as a huge elephant;nardataH simhasya=
(which gets into the path) of a roaring lion;tiikShNa damShTrsya= having terrible
tusks.




56Yuddha Kanda 101.56
अहन् तु वधमिच्छामि शीघ्रमस्य दुरात्मनःयावदस्तं न यात्येष कृतकर्मा दिवाकरः
ahan tu vadhamicchāmi śīghramasya durātmanaḥyāvadastaṃ na yātyeṣa kṛtakarmā divākaraḥ
"I, for my part, wish to see the death of this evil-minded fellow instantly, even
before this sun, having finished his task, does not sink below the horizon."


Word by word
56. aham= I;ichchhaami= wish for;vadham= the
death;asya duraatmanaH= of this evil-minded fellow;shiighram= instantly;yaavat= even before;eShaH= this;divaakaraH= sun;kR^ita
karmaa= having finished his task;na yaati= does not sink;astam= below
the horizon.




57Yuddha Kanda 101.57
यदि वधमिच्छसि रावणस्य संख्ये |यदि च कृतां हि तवेच्छसि प्रतिज्ञाम् |यदि तव राजसुताभिलाष आर्य |कुरु च वचो मम शीग्रमद्य वीर
yadi vadhamicchasi rāvaṇasya saṃkhye |yadi ca kṛtāṃ hi tavecchasi pratijñām |yadi tava rājasutābhilāṣa ārya |kuru ca vaco mama śīgramadya vīra
"O venerable hero! If you wish to kill Ravana in battle, if you wish to fulfill your
promise and if you feel affectionate towards Seetha, do as I tell you soon and now."


Word by word
57. aarya= O venerable;viira= hero!;ichchhasiyadi= If you wish;vadham= the killing;raavaNasya= of
Ravana;samkhye= in battle;kR^itaam ichchhasiyadi tava pratijJNaam= if you
want to fulfil your promise;tava raaajasutaabhilaaShaH yadi= and if you feel
affectionate towards Seetha;kurucha= you do;mama vachaH= as I tell you;shiighram= soon;adya= now.



    
  
  Rama laments over the uncertain condition of Lakshmana. He calls Sushena, the monkey-physician. Sushena tests Lakshmana and says he is still alive. Sushena then requests Hanuma to go all the way to Himalayas and bring the required herbs to treat Lakshmana. Hanuma proceeds to Mount Mahodara and failing to identify the herbs there, carries the mountain-peak itself and brings it to Sushena. Lakshmana regains consciousness, after getting treated with that herb by Sushena.

1Yuddha Kanda 103.1
स तु तेन तदा क्रोधात्काकुत्स्थेनार्दितो रणे |रावणः समरश्लाघी महाक्रोधमुपागमत्
sa tu tena tadā krodhātkākutsthenārdito raṇe |rāvaṇaḥ samaraślāghī mahākrodhamupāgamat
Tormented by Rama in fury, that Ravana then for his part, who was boasting of his
fight, flew into a great rage.


Word by word
1. saH raavaNaH= that Ravana;samara shlaaghii= boasting
of his fight;arditaH= who was tormented;bhR^isham= much;kaakutsthena= by Rama;krodhaat= in fury;tadaa= then;upaagamat= flew into;mahaakrodhaat= a highly enraged state.




2Yuddha Kanda 103.2
स दीप्तनयनो रोषाच्चापमायम्य वीर्यवान् |अभ्यर्दयत्सुसङ्क्रुद्धो राघवं परमाहवे
sa dīptanayano roṣāccāpamāyamya vīryavān |abhyardayatsusaṅkruddho rāghavaṃ paramāhave
Raising his bow, his eyes blazing with anger, extremely enraged as he was with Rama
in that great battle, the valiant Ravana of prowess continued to oppress, by covering Rama with
thousands of streams of arrows, as a rainy cloud would fill a pond with thousands of arrow-like
torrents from the sky.


Word by word
2;3. Udyamya= raising;chaapam= his bow;diiptanayanaH= his eyes blazing;amarShaat= with rage;raaghavam
samkruddhaH= extremely enraged with Rama as he was;paramaahave= in that great
battle;viiraH= the valiant Ravana;viiryavaan= of prowess;abhyardayat= continued to oppress;puurayan= by covering;raaghavam=
Rama;baaNadhaavaasahasraiH= with thousands of streams of arrows;saH toyadaH
iva= as a rainy cloud;(would fill) taTaakam= a pond;(with thousands of arrow-like
torrents;ambaraat= from the sky.




3Yuddha Kanda 103.3
बाणधारा सहस्रैस्तु स तोयद इवाम्बरात् |राघवन् रावणो बाणैस्तटाकमिव पूरयत्
bāṇadhārā sahasraistu sa toyada ivāmbarāt |rāghavan rāvaṇo bāṇaistaṭākamiva pūrayat
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


4Yuddha Kanda 103.4
पूरितः शरजालेन धनुर्मुक्तेन सन्युगे |महागिरिरिवाकम्प्यः काकुस्थो न प्रकम्पते
pūritaḥ śarajālena dhanurmuktena sanyuge |mahāgiririvākampyaḥ kākustho na prakampate
Covered by a multitude of arrows discharged from Ravana's bow in battle, Rama did
not wince, like a large mountain which was unshakable.


Word by word
4. puuritaH= covered;sharajaalena= by a multitude = of
arrows;dhanurmuktena= discharged from the bow;samyuge= in battle;kaakutsthaH= Rama;na kampate= did not wince;mahaagiririva= like a
large mountain;akampyaH= which was unshakable.




5Yuddha Kanda 103.5
स शरैः शरजालानि वारयन्समरे स्थितः |गभस्तीनिव सूर्यस्य प्रतिजग्राह वीर्यवान्
sa śaraiḥ śarajālāni vārayansamare sthitaḥ |gabhastīniva sūryasya pratijagrāha vīryavān
The valiant Rama stood interrupting the torrents of arrows with his own arrows in
the battle-field and endured them as rays of the sun.


Word by word
5. viiryavaan= The valiant;saH= Rama;sthitaH=
stood;vaarayan= interrupting;sharajaalaani= the torrents of arrows;sharaiH= with his own arrows;samyuge= in the battle-field;pratjagraaha= and accepted them;gabhastiiniva= as rays;suurya= of
the sun.




6Yuddha Kanda 103.6
ततः शरसहस्राणि क्षिप्रहस्तो निशाचरः |निजघानोरसि क्रुद्धो राघवस्य महात्मनः
tataḥ śarasahasrāṇi kṣiprahasto niśācaraḥ |nijaghānorasi kruddho rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
Then, the enraged Ravana of brisk hand, struck thousands of arrows into the breast
of the great-souled Rama.


Word by word
6. tataH= then;kruddhaH= the enraged;nishaachaiaH= Ravana;kShipra hastaH= of brisk hand;nijaghaana=
struck;shara sahasraaNi= thousands of arrows;urasi= into the breast;mahaatmanaH= of the great souled Rama.




7Yuddha Kanda 103.7
स शोणित समादिग्धः समरे लक्ष्मणाग्रजः |दृष्टः फुल्ल इवारण्ये सुमहान्किंशुकद्रुमः
sa śoṇita samādigdhaḥ samare lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ |dṛṣṭaḥ phulla ivāraṇye sumahānkiṃśukadrumaḥ
Rama, bathed in blood in the battle-field, appeared like a very big Kimshuka tree
with bloom in a forest.


Word by word
7. lakShmaNaagrajaH= Rama;shoNita samaadigdhaH= bathed in
blood;samare= in the battle-field;dR^iShTaH= appeared;sumahaan kimshuka
drumaH= like a very big Kimshuka tree;phullaH= with bloom;araNye= in a
forest.




8Yuddha Kanda 103.8
शराभिघातसन्रब्धः सोअपि जग्राह सायकान् |काकुत्स्थः सुमहातेजा युगान्तादित्यवर्चसः
śarābhighātasanrabdhaḥ soapi jagrāha sāyakān |kākutsthaḥ sumahātejā yugāntādityavarcasaḥ
Enraged at the impact of the arrows, that Rama of very great splendour , took hold
of arrows which shone like the sun at the time of dissolution of the world.


Word by word
8. sharaabhighaata samrabdhaH= enraged at the impact of the arrows;saH kaakutsthaH= that Rama;sumahaatejaH= of very great splendour;abhijagraaha= took hold of;saayakaan= arrows;yugaantaaditya tejasaH= which shone like the sun at the time of the dissolution of the world.




9Yuddha Kanda 103.9
ततोअन्योन्यन् सुसन्रब्धावुभौ तौ रामरावणौ |शरान्धकारे समरे नोपालक्षयतान् तदा
tatoanyonyan susanrabdhāvubhau tau rāmarāvaṇau |śarāndhakāre samare nopālakṣayatān tadā
Both Rama and Ravana who were see each other at that time in the battle-field, which
was shrouded in darkness by the arrows.


Word by word
9. tau ubhau raama raavaNau= Rama and Ravana;susamrabdhau= who were quite enraged;tataH anyonyam nopalakShayataam= could not thereupon see each
other;tadaa= at that time;samara= in the battle-field;sharaandhakaare= which was shrouded in darkness by the arrows.




10Yuddha Kanda 103.10
ततः क्रोधसमाविष्टो रामो दशरथात्मजः |उवाच रावणन् वीरः प्रहस्य परुषं वचः
tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭo rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ |uvāca rāvaṇan vīraḥ prahasya paruṣaṃ vacaḥ
Bursting into laughter, though filled with anger, the valiant Rama, the son of
Dasaratha spoke the following harsh words to Ravana.


Word by word
10. prahasya= bursting into laughter;krodhasamaariShTaH=
though filled with anger;viiraH= the valiant;raamaH= Rama;dasharathaatmajaH= the son of Dasaratha;uvaacha= spoke;paruSham
vachaH= the following harsh words;raavaNam= to Ravana.




11Yuddha Kanda 103.11
मम भार्या जनस्थानादज्ञानाद्राक्षसाधम |हृता ते विवशा यस्मात्तस्मात्त्वं नासि वीर्यवान्
mama bhāryā janasthānādajñānādrākṣasādhama |hṛtā te vivaśā yasmāttasmāttvaṃ nāsi vīryavān
"O the worst of demons! Since you took away my helpless wife without my notice from
Janasthana, hence you are not a person of prowess."


Word by word
11. raakShasaadhama= O the worst of demons!;yasmaat=
since;mama bhaaryaa= my wife;hR^itaa= was taken away;te= by you;janasthaanaat= from Janasthana;vivashaa= helpless as she was;ajNaanaat= when I was unaware;tasmaat= hence;tvam= you;naasi= are not;viiryavaan= a person of prowess.




12Yuddha Kanda 103.12
मया विरहितान् दीनान् वर्तमानां महावने |वैदेहीं प्रसभन् हृत्वा शूरोअहमिति मन्यसे
mayā virahitān dīnān vartamānāṃ mahāvane |vaidehīṃ prasabhan hṛtvā śūroahamiti manyase
"Having taken away by force the miserable Seetha while she was staying in the forest
away from me, you think: �I am a champion'."


Word by word
12. hR^itvaa= having taken away;prasabham= by force;diinaam= the miserable;vaidehiim= Seetha;vartamaanaam= while she
was staying;mahaavane= in the great forest;virahitaam= away from me;manyase= am a champion."




13Yuddha Kanda 103.13
स्त्रीषु शूर विनाथासु परदाराभिमर्शके |कृत्वा कापुरुषन् कर्म शूरोअहमिति मन्यसे
strīṣu śūra vināthāsu paradārābhimarśake |kṛtvā kāpuruṣan karma śūroahamiti manyase
"Having done an act of cowardly persons of laying your hands on another's wife,
posing as a hero in relation to women without a protector, you think: "I am a champion'."


Word by word
13. kR^itvaa= having done;karma= an act;kaapuruSham= of cowardly persons;paradaaraabhimarshaka= of laying your hands
on another's wife;shuura= posing as a hero;striiShu= in relation to women;vinaathaasu= without a protector;manyase= you think;iti= that;aham= I;shuuraH= am a champion.




14Yuddha Kanda 103.14
भिन्नमर्याद निर्लज्ज चारित्रेष्वनवस्थित |दर्पान्मृत्युमुपादाय शूरोअहमिति मन्यसे
bhinnamaryāda nirlajja cāritreṣvanavasthita |darpānmṛtyumupādāya śūroahamiti manyase
"O shameless person, who have broken the bounds of morality and are unstable of
customs, having laid hold through vanity of death (in the form of Seetha) you think �I am a
champion'."


Word by word
14. nirlajja= O shameless person;bhinna maryaada= who
have broken the bounds of morality;anavasthita= and are unstable;chaaritreShu= of customs;upaadaaya= having laid hold;darpaat mR^ityum= through vanity of
death (in the form of Seetha);manasye= you think;iti= that;aham
shuuraH= �I am a champion'.




15Yuddha Kanda 103.15
शूरेण धनदभ्रात्रा बलैः समुदितेन च |श्लाघनीयन् यशस्यन् च कृतं कर्म महत्त्वया
śūreṇa dhanadabhrātrā balaiḥ samuditena ca |ślāghanīyan yaśasyan ca kṛtaṃ karma mahattvayā
"Indeed a praiseworthy, great and glorious act has been performed by you, a valiant
brother of Kubera, the god of wealth, rich in strength!"


Word by word
15. shlaaghaniiyam= indeed a praise worthy;mahat= great;yashasyam cha= and glorious;karma= act;kR^itam= has been performed;tvayaa= by you shuureNa dhanada bhraatraa = a valiant brother of Kubera;the god of
wealth;balaiH samuditena= rich in strength!.




16Yuddha Kanda 103.16
उत्सेकेनाभिपन्नस्य गर्हितस्याहितस्य च |कर्मणः प्राप्नुहीदानीन् तस्याद्य सुमहत्फलम्
utsekenābhipannasya garhitasyāhitasya ca |karmaṇaḥ prāpnuhīdānīn tasyādya sumahatphalam
"Reap now and today the stupendous fruit of that noxious and contemptible act,
perpetrated through sheer vanity."


Word by word
16. praapnuhi= reap;sumahat= a stupendous;phalam= fruit;idaaniim= now;adya= today;tasya karmaNaH=
for that act;abhipannasya= done;utsekena= with vanity;garhitasya=
which is contemptible;ahitasya= and noxious.




17Yuddha Kanda 103.17
शूरोऽहमिति चात्मानमवगच्छसि दुर्मते |नैव लज्जास्ति ते सीतान् चोरवद्व्यपकर्षतः
śūro.ahamiti cātmānamavagacchasi durmate |naiva lajjāsti te sītān coravadvyapakarṣataḥ
"O evil-minded one! You think: �I am a champion' yourself! Shame did not stand in

  A ferocious battle ensues between Rama and Ravana, hurling thousands of arrows on each other. Each one intercepts the other's arrows. Rama speaks harsh words to Ravana for having carried away Seetha from Janasthana-forest to Lanka and vows that he will soon dispatch him surely to the world of Death. Rama then pours down streams of arrows on Ravana. Rama more vehemently torments Ravana with his sharp arrows and mystic missiles, till Ravana becomes helplessly weak and confused. Ravana's charioteer carries away Ravana in the chariot, camly and slowly away from the battle-front.

ādityaḥ savitā sūryaḥ khagaḥ pūṣā gabhastimān |suvarṇasadṛśo bhānurhiraṇyaretā divākaraḥ
"An off-spring of Aditi, the progenitor of all, Surya the sun-god and the provocator
of acts in people, the courser in the sky, the nourisher of all iwth rain, the possessor of rays
the golden, the brilliant, having golden seed whose energy constitutes the seed of the universe and
the maker of the day."


Word by word
10. aadityaH= an off-spring of Aditi;savitaa= the
progenitor of all;suuryaH= Surya;the sun-god and the provocator of acts in people;khagaH= the courser in the sky;puuShaa= the nourisher of all with rain;gabhastimaan= the possessor of rays;suvarNa sadR^ishaH= the golden;bhaanuH= the brilliant;hiraNya retaaH= having golden seed;divaakraH= and the maker of the day.




11Yuddha Kanda 105.11
हरिदश्वः सहस्रार्चिः सप्तसप्तिर्मरीचिमान् |तिमिरोन्मधनः शम्भुस्त्वष्टा मार्तण्डकोऽंशुमान्
haridaśvaḥ sahasrārciḥ saptasaptirmarīcimān |timironmadhanaḥ śambhustvaṣṭā mārtaṇḍako.aṃśumān
"He has seven green horses, is thousand-rayed, full of rays, the destroyer of
darkness, the source of happiness, maker of thinness, the infuser of life in the lifeless cosmic
egg and radiant."


Word by word
11. haridashvaH sapta saptiH= he has seven green horses;mariichimaan= full of rays;timironmathanaH= the destroyer of darkness;shambhuH= the source of happiness;tvaShTaa= maker of thinness;maartaN^DakaH= the infuser of life in the lifeless cosmic egg;amshumaan= and
radiant.




12Yuddha Kanda 105.12
हिरण्यगर्भः शिशिरस्तपनोऽहस्करो रविः |अग्निगर्भोऽदितेः पुत्रः शङ्खः शिशिरनाशनः
hiraṇyagarbhaḥ śiśirastapano.ahaskaro raviḥ |agnigarbho.aditeḥ putraḥ śaṅkhaḥ śiśiranāśanaḥ
"He is a golden foetus, maker of coolness, creator of heat, the bringer of a day,
the one who is eulogized by all, pregnant with fire, the son of Aditi, the one who pacifies himself
in the evening and the destroyer of frost."


Word by word
12. hiraNyagarbhaH= (He is) a golden foetus;shishiraH=
maker of coolness;tapanaH= creator of heat;ahaskaaH= the bringer of a day;raviH= the one who is eulogized by all;agnigarbhaH= pregnant with fire;aditoH putraH= the son of Aditi;shaN^khaH= the one who pacifies himself in the
evening;shishiranaashanaH= and the destroyer of frost.




13Yuddha Kanda 105.13
व्योमनाथस्तमोभेदी बुग्यजुः सामपारगः |घनवृष्टिरपां मित्रो विन्ध्यवीथीप्लवंगमः
vyomanāthastamobhedī bugyajuḥ sāmapāragaḥ |ghanavṛṣṭirapāṃ mitro vindhyavīthīplavaṃgamaḥ
"He is the lord of the sky, the disperser of darkness, the master of the three Vedas
(Viz. Rik, Sama and Yajur), the sender of thick rain, the friend of water and the on who courses
swiftly in the path of the sky."


Word by word
13. vyomanaathaHi= (He is) the lord of the sky;tamobhedii= disperser of darkness;R^igyajuH saamapaaragaH= the master of the three Vedas (Rik;
Sama and Yajur);ghana vR^iShTiH= the sender of thick rain;mitraH= the friend;apaam= of water;vindhyaviithiiplavangamaH= and the one who courses swiftly in
the path of the sky.




14Yuddha Kanda 105.14
आतपी मण्डली मृत्युः पिङ्गलः सर्वतापनः |कविर्विश्वो महातेजा रक्तः सर्वभवोद्भवः
ātapī maṇḍalī mṛtyuḥ piṅgalaḥ sarvatāpanaḥ |kavirviśvo mahātejā raktaḥ sarvabhavodbhavaḥ
"He is the radiator of heat and adrned with a circle of rays. He is death himself,
tawny of hue, a giver of warmth to all, omniscent, all-formed, endowed with extra-ordinary
splendour, the one who has an affection in all and the source of all evolutes."


Word by word
14. aatapii= (He is) the radiator of heat;maN^Dalii= and
adorned with a circle of rays;mR^ityuH= He is death (himself);piN^galaH=
tawny of hue;sarva taapanaH= giver of warmth to all;kaviH= (He is) omniscent;vishvaH= all-formed;mahaatejaaH= endowed with extra-ordinary splendour;raktaH= the one who has an affection in all;sarvabhavodbhavaH= and the source
of all evolutes.




15Yuddha Kanda 105.15
नक्षत्रग्रहताराणामधिपो विश्वभावनः |तेजसामपि तेजस्वी द्वादशात्मन्नमो.स्तु ते
nakṣatragrahatārāṇāmadhipo viśvabhāvanaḥ |tejasāmapi tejasvī dvādaśātmannamo.stu te
"He is the controller of all lunar mansions, planets and stars, the creator of all
and the resplendent among the splendid. O god, appearing in twelve forms (in the shape of twelve
months in a year), hail to you."


Word by word
15. nakShatra grahataaraaNaam adhipaH= the controller of all lunar
mansions;planets and stars;vishvabhaavanaH= the creator of all;tejasaamapi
tejasvii= the resplendent among the splendid;dvaadashaatman= O god;appearing in
twelve forms (in the shape of twelve months in a year);te namaH astu= hail to you!.




16Yuddha Kanda 105.16
नमः पूर्वाय गिरये पश्चिमायाद्रये नमः |ज्योतिर्गणानां पतये दिनाधिपतये नमः
namaḥ pūrvāya giraye paścimāyādraye namaḥ |jyotirgaṇānāṃ pataye dinādhipataye namaḥ
"Hail to you in the form of eastern mountain and hail to the western mountain. Hail
to the lord of host of luminaries and hail to the lord of the day."


Word by word
16. namaH= Hail to you;puurvaaya giraye= in the form of
eastern mountain namaH = and hail;pashchimaaya adraye= to the western mountain;namaH= Hail;yotirgaNaanaam pataye= to the lord of hosts of luminaries;namaH= hail;dinaadhipataye= to the lord of the day.




17Yuddha Kanda 105.17
जयाय जयभद्राय हर्याश्वाय नमो नमः |नमो नमः सहस्रांशो आदित्याय नमो नमः
jayāya jayabhadrāya haryāśvāya namo namaḥ |namo namaḥ sahasrāṃśo ādityāya namo namaḥ
"Hail to you, the giver of victory, hail to you, the joy born of victory! Hail to
you, the god with green horses, hail to you, having thousands of rays! Hail, hail to you the son of
Aditi!


Word by word
17. namaH jayaaya= hail to you;the giver of victory;namaH
jayabhadraaya= hail to you;the joy born of victory!;namaH harvashvaaya= hail to
you;the god having green horses;namaH sahasraamshaH= hail to you;having thousands of
rays!;namaH namaH aadityaaya= hail;hail to you the son of Aditi!




18Yuddha Kanda 105.18
नम उग्राय वीराय सारङ्गाय नमो नमः |नमः पद्मप्रबोधाय प्रचण्डाय नमोऽस्तु ते
nama ugrāya vīrāya sāraṅgāya namo namaḥ |namaḥ padmaprabodhāya pracaṇḍāya namo.astu te
"Hail to you, the fierce one, hail to you the valiant one! Hail to you, the one with
variegated colours! Hail to you, the awakener of the louts, hail to you, the furious one!"


Word by word
18. namaH ugraaya= hail to you;the fierce one! namaH
viiraaya= hail to you;the valiant one!;namaH saaraN^gaaya= hail to you;the one
with variegated colours!;namaH padma prabodhaaya= hail to you;the awakener of the
lotus!;te namaH tu prachaN^Daaya= hail to you the furious one!




19Yuddha Kanda 105.19
ब्रह्मेशानाच्युतेशाय सूर्यायादित्यवर्चसे |भास्वते सर्वभक्षाय रौद्राय वपुषे नमः
brahmeśānācyuteśāya sūryāyādityavarcase |bhāsvate sarvabhakṣāya raudrāya vapuṣe namaḥ
"Hail to you, the ruler of Brahma, Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu the infallible, the
sun-god, the light indwelling the solar orb, the resplendent one, the devourer of all, appearing in
form of Rudra."


Word by word
19. namaH= hail to you;brahmeshaanaachyuteshaaya= the
ruler of Brahma;Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu;the infallible;suuryaaya= the sun-god;aaditya varchase= the light indwelling the solar orb;bhaasvate= the
resplendent one;sarva bhakShaaya= the devourer of all;raudraaya vapuShe=
appearing in teh form of Rudra.




20Yuddha Kanda 105.20
तमोघ्नाय हिमग्नाय शत्रुघ्नायामितात्मने |कृतघ्नघ्नाय देवाय ज्योतिषां पतये नमः
tamoghnāya himagnāya śatrughnāyāmitātmane |kṛtaghnaghnāya devāya jyotiṣāṃ pataye namaḥ
"Hail to you, the dispeller of darkness, the destroyer of cold, the exterminator of
foes, the one whose extent in immeasurable, the destroyer of the ungrateful, the god, who is the
ruler of all lights."


Word by word
20. namaH= Hail to you;tamoghnaaya= the dispeller of
darkness;himaghnaaya= the destroyer of cold;shatrughnaaya= teh exterminator
of foes;amitaatmane= the one whose extent is immeasurable;kR^itaghnaghnaaya=

21Yuddha Kanda 105.21
तप्तचामीकराभाय हरये विश्वकर्मणे |नमस्तमोभिनिघ्नाय रुचये लोकसाक्षिणे
taptacāmīkarābhāya haraye viśvakarmaṇe |namastamobhinighnāya rucaye lokasākṣiṇe
"Hail to you, possessing the lustre of refined gold, the dispeller of ignorance, the
architect of the universe, the uprooter of darkness, the splendour incarnate, the onlooker of the
world!'"


Word by word
21. namaH= Hail to you;tapta chaamiikaraabhaaya=
possessing the lustre of refined gold;haraye= the dispeller of ignorance;vishvakarmaya= the architect of the universe;tamobhinighnaaya= the uprooter of
darkness;ruchaye= the splendour incarnate;lokasaakShiNe= the onlooker of the
world!




22Yuddha Kanda 105.22
नाशयत्येष वै भूतं तदेव सृजति प्रभुः |पायत्येष तपत्येष वर्षत्येष गभस्तिभिः
nāśayatyeṣa vai bhūtaṃ tadeva sṛjati prabhuḥ |pāyatyeṣa tapatyeṣa varṣatyeṣa gabhastibhiḥ
"This sun, the lord alone destroys and brings into existence all the brings. He
radiates heat by his rays. He sends the rain."


Word by word
22. eShaH vai prabhuH= this sun;the lord alone;naashayati= destroys;tadeva sR^ijati= and brings into existence;bhuutam= all the
beings;eShaH= he;tapati paayati= radiates heat;gabhastiH= by his
rays;eShaH= He;varShati= sends the rain.




23Yuddha Kanda 105.23
एष सुप्तेषु जागर्ति भूतेषु परिनिष्ठितः |एष चैवाग्निहोत्रं च फलं चैवाग्निहोत्रिणाम्
eṣa supteṣu jāgarti bhūteṣu pariniṣṭhitaḥ |eṣa caivāgnihotraṃ ca phalaṃ caivāgnihotriṇām
"Planted in all created beings, he remains awake, when they have fallen asleep. He
alone is the oblation to the fire-god and the fruit attained by those who pour such oblations."


Word by word
23. pariniShThitaH= planted in all created beings;eShaH=
he;jaagarti= remains awake;supteShu= when they have fallen asleep;eShaH
chaiva= he alone;agnihotram cha= is the oblation to the fire-god;phalam
cha= and the fruit;agnihotriNaam= attained by those who pour such oblations.




24Yuddha Kanda 105.24
देवाश्च क्रतवश्चैव क्रतूनां फलमेव च |यानि कृत्यानि लोकेषु सर्वेषु परमप्रभुः
devāśca kratavaścaiva kratūnāṃ phalameva ca |yāni kṛtyāni lokeṣu sarveṣu paramaprabhuḥ
"He comprises all the gods, as well as the sacrifies as also the fruit of all
sacrifices. He is a supremely competent one of all activities, which are found in all the
worlds."


Word by word
24. devaaH= (He comprises) all the gods;kratavashchaiva=
as well as the sacrifices;kratavashchaiva= as well as the sacrifices;kratuunaam
phalamevacha= as also the fruit of sacrifices;parama prabhuH= he is the supremely
competent one;kR^ityaami= of all activities;yaani= which are found;sarveShu lokeShu= in all the worlds.




25Yuddha Kanda 105.25
एनमापत्सु कृच्छ्रेषु कान्तारेषु भयेषु च |कीर्तयन् पुरुषः कश्चिन्नावसीदति राघव
enamāpatsu kṛcchreṣu kāntāreṣu bhayeṣu ca |kīrtayan puruṣaḥ kaścinnāvasīdati rāghava
"O Rama! No individual glorifying this sun-god, in distresses in difficulties; in
the woods or in times of peril, comes to grief."


Word by word
25. raaghava= O Rama!;na kashchit puruShaH= no
individual;kiirtayan= glorifying;enam= this sun-god;aapatsu= in
distresses;kR^ichchheShu= in difficulties;kaantaareShu= in the wood;bhayeShu= in times of peril;avasiidati= comes to grief.




26Yuddha Kanda 105.26
पूजयस्वैनमेकाग्रो देवदेवं जगत्पतिम् |एतत्त्रिगुणितं जप्त्वा युद्धेषु विजयिष्यसि
pūjayasvainamekāgro devadevaṃ jagatpatim |etattriguṇitaṃ japtvā yuddheṣu vijayiṣyasi
"Worship this sun-god, the lord of the universe and the god of all gods with
undivided attention. Muttering this praise three times, you will come out victorious in
battles."


Word by word
26. puujayasva= worship;enam= this sun-god;jagatpatim= the lord of the universe;devadevam= and the god of all gods;ekaagraH= with undivided attention;japtyaa= muttering;etat= this
praise;triguNetam= three times;vijayiShyasi= you will come out victorious;yuddheShu= in battles.




27Yuddha Kanda 105.27
अस्मिन् क्षणे महाबाहो रावणं त्वं वधिष्यसि |एवमुक्त्वा ततोऽगस्त्यो जगाम स यथागतम्
asmin kṣaṇe mahābāho rāvaṇaṃ tvaṃ vadhiṣyasi |evamuktvā tato.agastyo jagāma sa yathāgatam
"You will be able to kill Ravana at this very moment, O mighty armed one!" Saying
so, the sage, Agastya, thereupon, left as in the same way as he had come.


Word by word
27. tvam= you;vadhiShyasi= will be able to kill;raavaNam= Ravana;asmin kShaNe= at this very moment;mahaabaaho= O
the mighty armed!;evam uktvaa= saying so;agastya= the sage;Agastya;tataH= thereupon;jagaama= left;yathaagatam= as in the same way as
he had come.




28Yuddha Kanda 105.28
एतच्छ्रुत्वा महातेजा नष्टशोकोऽभवत्तदा |धारयामास सुप्रीतो राघवः प्रयतात्मवान्
etacchrutvā mahātejā naṣṭaśoko.abhavattadā |dhārayāmāsa suprīto rāghavaḥ prayatātmavān
Hearing this, Rama of extra ordinary energy, then became bereft of anguish. Feeling
greatly delighted, Rama retained that hymn in his memory with a devoted mind.


Word by word
28. shrutvaa= hearing;etat= this;mahaatejaaH=
Rama;of extraordinary energy;tadaa= then;abhavat= became;naShTa
shokaH= bereft of anguish;supriitaH= feeling greatly delighted;raaghavaH= Rama;dhaarayaamaasa= retained in memory;(that hymn of praise of the sun-god);prayataatmavaan= with a devoted mind.




29Yuddha Kanda 105.29
आदित्यं प्रेक्ष्य जप्त्वा तु परं हर्षमवाप्तवान् |त्रिराचम्य शुचिर्भूत्वा धनुरादाय वीर्यवान्
ādityaṃ prekṣya japtvā tu paraṃ harṣamavāptavān |trirācamya śucirbhūtvā dhanurādāya vīryavān
Sipping the water thrice and getting purified looking intently on the orb of the sun
and repeating this prayer, the valiant Rama obtained a great rejoice. Seizing hold of his bow and
seeing Ravana, Rama felt delighted in mind and marched forward for the fight. He stood voed to kill
Ravana, with an intense and all-sided effort.


Word by word
29;30. aachamya= sipping the water;triH= thrice;shuchiH bhuutvaa= and getting purified;prekShya= looking intently;aadityam= on the orb of the sun;japtvaa= and repeating this prayer;viiryavaan= the valiant Rama;avaaptavaan= obtained;param= a great;harSham= rejoice;aadaaya= seizing hold;dhanuH= of his bow;prekShya= and seeing;raavanam= Ravana;(Rama);hR^iShTaatmaa= felt
delighted in mind;samupaagamat= and advanced;yuddhaartham= for the fight;abhavat dhR^itaH= he stood voed;tasya vadhe= to kill Ravana;mahataa sarva
yatnena= with an intense and all-sided effort.




30Yuddha Kanda 105.30
रावणं प्रेक्ष्य हृष्टात्मा युद्धार्थं समुपागमत् |सर्वयत्नेन महता वधे तस्य धृतोऽभवत्
rāvaṇaṃ prekṣya hṛṣṭātmā yuddhārthaṃ samupāgamat |sarvayatnena mahatā vadhe tasya dhṛto.abhavat
The source page does not carry a separate English translation for this shloka. The Devanagari and IAST are complete.


31Yuddha Kanda 105.31
अथ रविरवदन्निरीक्ष्य रामं |मुदितमनाः परमं प्रहृष्यमाणः |निशिचरपतिसंक्षयं विदित्वा |सुरगणमध्यगतो वचस्त्वरेति
atha raviravadannirīkṣya rāmaṃ |muditamanāḥ paramaṃ prahṛṣyamāṇaḥ |niśicarapatisaṃkṣayaṃ viditvā |suragaṇamadhyagato vacastvareti
Seeing Rama with a delighted mind, and becoming most exhildrated on foreseeing the
death of Ravana, the sun-god, standing in the middle of a troop of celestials, exclaimed, "Hasten
up."

sun-god;atha= thereupon;muditamanaaH= with a delighted mind;param
prahR^iShyamaaNaH= and becoming most rejoiced;viditvaa= on foreseeing;nishicharapatisamkShayam= Ravana's death;avadat= spoke;vachaH= the

as he was in teh middle of a troop of celestials.

1Yuddha Kanda 107.1
ततः प्रवृत्तं सुक्रूरं रामरावणयोस्तदा |सुमहद्द्वैरथं युद्धं सर्वलोकभयावहम्
tataḥ pravṛttaṃ sukrūraṃ rāmarāvaṇayostadā |sumahaddvairathaṃ yuddhaṃ sarvalokabhayāvaham
Then ensued a fierce and a prolonged chariot-duel between Rama and Ravana, which was
frightful to all the worlds.


Word by word
1. tataH= then;tadaa= and there;sukruuram= a
very cruel;sumahat= and a very great;dvairatham= chariot-duel;yuddham= in battle;sarva loka bhayaavaham= which was frightful to all the

iti cintāparaścāsī dapramattaśca saṃyuge |vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi rāghavo rāvaṇorasi

daśarathasutarākṣasendrayo |rjayamanavekṣya raṇe sa rāghavasya |suravararathasārathirmahātmā |raṇaratarāmamuvāca vākyamāśu

  Loosing arrows at each other, Rama and Ravana perform a fierce battle. Ravana's flag-staff is thrown down by Rama's arrows. When Rama begins to cut off Ravana's head, another head starts to crop up in its place. The fierce encounter continues thus for seven days.

Home/Yuddha Kanda/Sarga 109

  Yuddha Kanda · Sarga 109
  Vibhishana laments a lot, after seeing Ravana lying dead on the battle-field
  Vibhishana laments a lot, after seeing Ravana lying dead on the battle-field. Rama comforts him, saying that a warrior killed in battle, need not be mourned.

bhrātaraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā śayānaṃ nirjitaṃ raṇe |śokavegaparītātmā vilalāpa vibhīṣaṇaḥ

his mind filled with an outburst of sorrow:
